title: Be Careful What You Pay For: The Effect of Performance Contingent Incentives on Online Product Reviews
affiliations: , affiliation not provided to SSRN, HEC Montreal - Department of Marketing and HEC Montréal,

detail.title: Be Careful What You Pay For: The Effect of Performance Contingent Incentives on Online Product Reviews

declarations.ethicsApproval: All procedures performed in studies involving human participants were conducted in adherence to national and international research ethics guidelines. publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Research in Interactive Marketing, 0[10.1108/JRIM-04-2026-0253]

detail.abstract:
This research investigates how performance-contingent incentivization schemes affect online review contributions. It explores the interplay between financial incentives, prosocial reinforcement (social versus reciprocal exchange), and reviewer experience.
The research conducts a field study in collaboration with a major North American online retailer to evaluate customer review behavior.
Reviewer experience moderates the effect of performance-contingent incentives on review decisions and length. First-time (vs. experienced) reviewers see significant improvements in both review decisions and length with performance-contingent incentives. Additionally, because performance-contingent incentives reinforce reciprocal exchange, introducing reciprocal exchange reinforcement through messaging increases the level of effort but reduces review decisions. The optimal strategy depends on the platform’s proportion of first-time reviewers and the retailer’s specific review outcomes.
This work identifies reviewer experience and prosocial framing as critical boundary conditions for the effectiveness of performance-contingent incentives.

title: Regression Analysis of Payment Center Patronage
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of St. La Salle

detail.title: Regression Analysis of Payment Center Patronage
detail.abstract: In the evolving financial service landscape of Sagay City, payment centers serve as essential physical-digital intermediaries for consumers managing utility bills and digital wallet transactions. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), and Service-Dominant (S-D) Logic, this study examined how service-marketing dimensions structurally predict customer patronage. Employing a descriptivecorrelational design, the study surveyed a purposive sample of 165 participants (mean age = 32.16 years; 75.8% female; 78.2% banked) who utilized a local payment center within the preceding three months. Descriptive analysis revealed that Process (M = 4.624) and Staff Performance (M = 4.567) are the primary drivers of consumer selection. Patronage behavior was characterized by high usage in e-wallet cash operations (M = 4.100) and utility payments (M = 3.918), with strong preferences for geographic proximity (M = 4.227) and digital options (M = 4.118). Maximum Likelihood Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) demonstrated acceptable model fit (CFI = 0.968, TLI = 0.950, RMSEA = 0.062, SRMR = 0.036), accounting for 23.2% of the total variance in customer patronage. Notably, high inter-variable correlations attenuated individual predictor significances (p > .05), indicating that patrons evaluate payment centers through a holistic service ecosystem rather than isolated attributes. Within the structural model, Social Influence demonstrated the strongest directional trend (beta = 0.196, p = .073). Payment center operators should adopt integrated service ecosystem branding, establish express lanes for digital transactions, and leverage community referral programs to maintain competitiveness.

title: Do Celebrity Athlete Endorsements Move Sports Betting Demand? A Stacked Event Study of State-Level Handle, 2019-2024

detail.title: Do Celebrity Athlete Endorsements Move Sports Betting Demand? A Stacked Event Study of State-Level Handle, 2019-2024
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether athlete endorsement announcements are associated with changes in sports betting activity in the United States. Using monthly sports betting data from five states between 2019 and 2024, I compared betting handle before and after major athlete endorsement announcements using event-study and regression analysis. Betting handle is estimated to be 25 to 38 percent higher in the twelve months following an endorsement announcement. I also tested whether endorsements announced around major sporting events are responsible for the increase and found a larger post-announcement difference for endorsements that were not timed to these events. However, the month-by-month estimates become sensitive when underlying trends in betting activity are accounted for. Overall, the results show a positive association between athlete endorsement announcements and sports betting activity.

title: Sophistication in GenAI Use: Field Evidence from a Large Firm
affiliations: University of Texas at Austin, University of Texas at Austin, KPMG LLP and University of Texas at Austin

detail.title: Sophistication in GenAI Use: Field Evidence from a Large Firm

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Anu Puvvada is a principal and employee of KPMG LLP. Jaime J. Schmidt holds the KPMG Centennial Fellowship in Accounting at The University of Texas at Austin. KPMG LLP provided the proprietary data used in this study. No other competing interests are declared.

detail.abstract: We study how sophistication in generative AI (genAI) use varies among the back-office workforce of a large firm. Using proprietary data, we observe 713,564 employee prompts and their corresponding large language model responses from nearly 4,000 back-office employees across 15 functional areas over eight months in 2025. We document three main findings. First, senior employees exhibit more sophisticated genAI use, consistent with domain expertise complementing genAI capabilities. Second, sophistication varies considerably across functions and is highest in Strategy, Digital Innovation, and Project Management, three groups that share a focus on firmwide strategic initiatives and organizational change. Third, we observe neither improvements in sophistication over time nor lasting improvements following formal AI training, suggesting that sophisticated use can be difficult to change. Together, our study provides measures of and insights into sophisticated genAI use that managers can use to improve outcomes and that researchers can use in future research.

title: Neoscholeism, A Unified Theory of Cognitive Substitution, the Neoscholeism Production Function NPF, and Fiscal Sustainability Under Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Neoscholeism, A Unified Theory of Cognitive Substitution, the Neoscholeism Production Function NPF, and Fiscal Sustainability Under Artificial Intelligence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the work reported in this paper. This research received no external funding. The author is an Independent Researcher and has no affiliation, consultancy, or financial relationship with any organization whose interests may be affected by this research. AI Disclosure: Language and formatting assistance only; all theoretical development, empirical analysis, and results are the author's own, as stated on page 16 of the manuscript.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study does not involve human participants, patients, or animal subjects. All empirical analyses use publicly available, aggregated, de-identified data from BEA, BLS, O*NET, and U.S. Census Bureau BTOS. No ethics approval or informed consent was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. Self-funded by the author as Independent Researcher.

detail.abstract:
Artificial Intelligence is increasingly executing complex cognitive tasks historically restricted to human labor, yet no standardized macroeconomic variable directly measures the extent of this substitution within production. This paper develops Neoscholeism, a unified theoretical and empirical framework spanning seven interconnected parts.

Part I introduces the Cognitive Substitution Index (σAI), embeds it in a CES production microfoundation, and tests four derived hypotheses against BEA/BLS data (1987–2026Q1), reporting a mixed but methodologically rigorous empirical verdict corrected for multiple comparisons. 

Part II extends the index to classical price theory, showing how AI-driven marginal cost compression generates a paradox of rising efficiency alongside eroding labor-based tax bases. 

Part III synthesizes the full transmission mechanism — from cognitive substitution through price and income compression to fiscal pressure — as a map to the volume's formal results. 

Part IV reconciles σAI with the companion book's CES elasticity parameter (σai) via an explicit bridge equation. 

Part V outlines a general-equilibrium and welfare-theoretic research agenda for the framework. 

Part VI derives the Neoscholeism Production Function (NPF) from an occupational-choice model under CRRA preferences, proving existence and monotonicity results for an unconditional Universal Dividend. 

Part VII builds a minimal break-point model of fiscal sustainability, deriving closed-form and quadratic break-threshold conditions under which an AI-transaction tax ("API Tax") restores solvency as labor income shares erode.

Together, the seven parts offer a formally consistent, empirically grounded account of how AI-driven cognitive substitution propagates from production through prices, labor markets, and public finance — and of the fiscal instruments that may be required to sustain it.

title: A Study on the Impact of Cost Presentation on Decision-making Bias and Cancellation Behavior in Online Subscriptions
affiliations: NB Brother Corp, Vernon

detail.title: A Study on the Impact of Cost Presentation on Decision-making Bias and Cancellation Behavior in Online Subscriptions
detail.abstract: Online subscription interfaces often embed cost information, renewal conditions, and cancellation entries within complex page structures, which may increase users' payment misclassification and cancellation abandonment. To strengthen the computational contribution of this study, this paper proposes a costpresentation bias detection framework that integrates interface structure parsing, visual salience encoding, clickstream sequence modeling, and cancellation path complexity estimation. The proposed framework first extracts DOM hierarchy depth, cost-field screen exposure, price-block coordinates, font scale, contrast ratio, button-cost distance, cancellation entry depth, and hidden-menu expansion from subscription, checkout, and cancellation pages. User behaviors are then synchronized with page-level identifiers and encoded as temporal sequences containing clicks, dwell time, scrolling, back navigation, field expansion, and abandonment events. A structure-behavior fusion model is constructed to estimate session-level decision-bias probability, while a directed path graph is used to compute cancellation-process complexity through node transitions, edge costs, branch entropy, dwell-time accumulation, and semantic jump penalties. Experiments on 4,276 subscriptionrelated pages and 3,892 valid interaction sessions show that deep cost placement increases payment misclassification, whereas upfront cost disclosure, visual salience enhancement, and path compression reduce the mean misjudgment rate from 22.4% to 8.1%. High-complexity cancellation paths lead to a 37.4% abandonment rate, while low-complexity paths reduce the rate to 19.8%. After interface optimization, decision accuracy increases from 77.6% to 91.9%, and unplanned subscription decreases from 12.7% to 6.3%. The results demonstrate that cost-presentation bias can be computationally detected and mitigated through interface-structure modeling and behavior-aware path optimization. This study contributes a measurable HCIoriented computational method for auditing subscription interfaces and improving digital consumption fairness. title: Followers are not Enough: Why Social Media Followers Alone cannot Accelerate Business Success, Evidence From a Durban-based SMME

detail.title: Followers are not Enough: Why Social Media Followers Alone cannot Accelerate Business Success, Evidence From a Durban-based SMME
detail.abstract:
Small, Micro and Medium Enterprises (SMMEs) in South Africa increasingly assume that social
media followers will automatically become paying customers. This paper argues that followers
can become customers, but they are not enough to accelerate business success or sustain
operations. Drawing from a longitudinal autoethnographic study of my own baking SMME in
Durban CBD (2023), I operated without relying on social media posting. My growth came from
structured physical routines: 08:00 PM intra-building vertical penetration, 05:00-08:00 AM fixed
roadside positioning, and 08:00-09:30 AM continuous mobility across taxi ranks, hospitals and
salons. I observed entrepreneurs who rely only on social media complaining that people do not
share their business, but you can never control what people do on their page — it is their wall.
This paper does not dismiss followers — it shows they are not enough. Sustainable customers are
built by being physically seen every day.

title: IRT vs. RUT: Who Wins? Choice-Response Inference, Person-Measurement Inference, and the Limits of Inferential Interchangeability
affiliations: Red Analytics

detail.title: IRT vs. RUT: Who Wins? Choice-Response Inference, Person-Measurement Inference, and the Limits of Inferential Interchangeability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This conceptual paper did not involve human participants, personal data, or animal subjects and therefore did not require ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: his research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Person-level estimates arise in both IRT-based person-measurement systems and random-utility choice models. The two traditions can share comparative tasks, latent-utility machinery, heterogeneity, and person-level outputs. Yet they may assign those estimates different scientific roles. 

In choice-response inference, person-level parameters represent heterogeneous response within a choice system and can support prediction and decision making. In person-measurement inference, comparative responses are combined with additional measurement structure or mapping with the aim of measuring specified characteristics of the person and relating those measurements to other outcomes. 

Those different roles lead to different scientific questions. They also change what model structure, validation evidence, generalization, and downstream analyses are relevant. This paper makes those inferential roles explicit and traces the consequences of the distinction. Similar person-level output form does not make the estimates inferentially interchangeable.

title: Cross-Cultural Advertising Adaptation: A Comparative Analysis of Nike's Campaigns in South Korea and the United States
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Cross-Cultural Advertising Adaptation: A Comparative Analysis of Nike's Campaigns in South Korea and the United States

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable — this study did not involve human participants requiring ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: The contemporary development of the global economy has enabled major brands to extend their operations well beyond their domestic markets and to engage in communication with millions of consumers across a wide range of countries simultaneously. This expansion, however, gives rise to a significant challenge: audiences within these markets are not culturally homogeneous and identical advertising messages may be interpreted differently depending on the values, behavioral norms, and communicative conventions characteristic of a given society. International corporations are therefore increasingly confronted with the necessity of choosing between a unified global advertising strategy and the localization of their messaging in accordance with the cultural specificities of each individual market. Nike constitutes one of the most instructive examples of this phenomenon: despite maintaining one of the most recognizable and consistently articulated global brand identities within the sportswear industry, the company conducts advertising campaigns across markets characterized by fundamentally distinct cultural systems, including South Korea and the United States. Differences in the value orientations of these two nations-particularly with respect to individualism and collectivism, as well as to prevailing communication stylesexert a direct influence on the manner in which advertisements are conceived, perceived and evaluated by consumers. An examination of Nike's advertising campaigns within these two national contexts thus enables a more nuanced understanding of the extent to which a global brand preserves a unified communicative strategy, as opposed to the extent to which it deliberately adapts that strategy to the cultural particularities of local audiences and of why such adaptation is becoming an indispensable component of contemporary international advertising practice.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future Supply of Skills: Evidence from UK University Applications
affiliations: , , King's College London and

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future Supply of Skills: Evidence from UK University Applications
detail.abstract: Educational investments determine the future supply of skills. We examine how generative AI is changing students' decisions about what to study. Linking millions of LinkedIn profiles to UK application records, we measure the AI exposure of university-subject pairs based on the occupations of their past graduates, and follow applications to 1,090 degrees over the 2020-2025 cycles. Human capital theory predicts that students should leave subjects whose prospects are eroded by AI, but we find the opposite. After the release of ChatGPT, applications to a degree one standard deviation higher in exposure grew six percent more than applications to less exposed degrees. The shift appears among men and women and across ethnic groups, while total demand for university places is unchanged. Our labor market analysis shows that the job opportunities for juniors have deteriorated for more exposed degrees. Students are thus moving toward the subjects in which entry-level job opportunities are declining.

title: Domain-AI Driven Marketing, Topic-AI Conversational Marketing & AI Customer Service

detail.title: Domain-AI Driven Marketing, Topic-AI Conversational Marketing & AI Customer Service
detail.abstract: The rapid evolution of conversational marketing has transformed customer engagement from static, rule-based systems like ELIZA and scripted IVR into dynamic, generative AI interfaces powered by Large Language Models. This research explores the strategic advantages driving widespread business adoption, such as continuous 24/7 availability, near-zero marginal operational costs, high volumetric ticket containment, and hyper-personalization through CRM integration. However, the transition to autonomous generative logic introduces critical operational and legal risks. This paper analyzes severe technical failure modes, including fluent hallucinations, malicious prompt injections, and post-deployment guardrail regressions. By critically evaluating the landmark 2024 BC Civil Resolution Tribunal case, Moffatt v. Air Canada, and the 2025 FTC v. DoNotPay settlement, this study illustrates how courts and regulators establish absolute corporate liability for automated representations. Furthermore, this paper examines these dynamics within India's unique multilingual market and evolving regulatory framework, notably the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act and the Reserve Bank of India’s FREE-AI guidelines. Ultimately, we propose a robust governance framework emphasizing risk-tiered categorization, grounded single-source databases, and continuous human-in-the-loop monitoring to safeguard brand integrity.

title: Brand Capital Formation and Depreciation Dynamics Associated with Patent/Exclusivity Expiration of OTC Drugs
affiliations: The University of Texas at Dallas, University of Texas at Dallas - Naveen Jindal School of Management and University of Rochester - Simon Business School

detail.title: Brand Capital Formation and Depreciation Dynamics Associated with Patent/Exclusivity Expiration of OTC Drugs
detail.abstract: We study brand-capital formation and depreciation dynamics in the U.S. over-the-counter (OTC) drug market, in which generic competitors' entry was triggered by the expiration of patent/exclusivity protection. Using retail scanner data, we document the stylized fact that the branded drugs retain 40%-80% quantity shares after the entry of chemically identical generics, despite being 22%-102% more expensive. Analyzing household panel data, we further find that households first exposed exogenously to the branded drug during the monopoly period remain 3.2%p-10.5%p more likely to choose the branded drug even years after generics become available. These findings point to a persistent brand preference built by initial and subsequent repeated exposure to the branded drug. We then develop a parsimonious household-level choice model with brand-capital dynamics to translate these findings into market outcomes. The estimated brand-capital stock is reinforced by repeat purchases but depreciates over time, with an implied half-life of about 2.2-3.6 months. Ignoring the brand-capital persistence understates the branded drugs' incremental revenue from a counterfactual 1-year-delayed generics' entry by 32.2%-106.6%. Our analysis highlights that the patent/exclusivity protection affects market outcomes beyond the formal protection period through the brand capital stock carried into post-entry competition.

title: Technology, Bank Market Structure, and the Redistribution of Financial Intermediate
affiliations: Peking University

detail.title: Technology, Bank Market Structure, and the Redistribution of Financial Intermediate
detail.abstract: We examine the impact of digital developments on bank competitiveness via the gradual roll out of 3G mobile networks. In younger countries in particular, 3G expansion reduced the need for branch networks, as tech-savvy families increasingly utilize mobile banking. Various financial institutions acted differently. Focused banks maintained their branch locations but increased interest rates. Less concerned banks closed their branches and competed primarily on pricing. According to a structural model, these shifts occurred because younger consumers saw digital services as superior, which in turn dissatisfied the older generation of savers. Given these monetary disparities, what-if scenarios suggest that senior savers could benefit from adoption subsidies, which might facilitate a more seamless digital transition.

title: When Do Ecological Concepts Transfer to Persistent AI-Agent Systems? A Research Agenda for Emerging Agent Ecosystems
affiliations: University of Cincinnati and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: When Do Ecological Concepts Transfer to Persistent AI-Agent Systems? A Research Agenda for Emerging Agent Ecosystems
detail.abstract: AI-agent systems are moving from isolated assistants and short-lived workflows toward persistent collectives that retain memory, divide labor, share tools, and operate through coupled human and technical environments. As this transition unfolds, system behavior will depend increasingly on community composition, interaction networks, accumulated history, shared dependencies, and responses to disturbance, properties that cannot be inferred from individual model capability alone. We propose ecology as a research framework for this emerging level of organization. The aim is to identify ecological concepts that generate useful questions, measurable observables, and testable predictions. We define an agent ecosystem as agents together with the informational, technical, human, and institutional environments through which they interact. We then organize a research agenda around community assembly and priority effects; niches, functional differentiation, and coexistence; interaction networks and indirect effects; stigmergy and environmental memory; diversity, stability, and resilience; disturbance, invasion, cascades, and regime change; and conditional evolutionary and eco-evolutionary dynamics. We distinguish concepts already applicable to present systems from those that require greater persistence, turnover, inheritance, or reproduction. Four safeguards constrain the analogies: explicit units, mechanistic correspondence, measurable alternatives, and stated boundaries. Ecology can therefore contribute a relational science of how agent communities form, function, fail, and change.

title: Optimal Design of Charitable Fundraising Platforms
affiliations: , University of Texas at Dallas - Naveen Jindal School of Management and University of Texas at Dallas - Department of Information Systems & Operations Management

detail.title: Optimal Design of Charitable Fundraising Platforms
detail.abstract: Online charitable fundraising platforms connect donors and beneficiaries, balancing participation on both sides of the market. We consider a stylized model of a profit-maximizing platform deciding its commission on donations and how many beneficiaries to admit. The platform earns commission revenue but incurs onboarding costs, while beneficiaries participate only if expected donations cover a fixed entry cost. Donors contribute only when they find a sufficiently aligned cause. We characterize equilibrium outcomes and show that both platform decisions depend on market coverage, defined as the fraction of participating donors. Importantly, the two costs shape coverage through different channels: onboarding costs raise the cost of expanding the beneficiary base, whereas entry costs impose an endogenous ceiling on the commission. Our analysis yields four main findings. First, the profit-maximizing commission can decrease as onboarding costs increase. Higher commissions reduce each beneficiary's reach, requiring more beneficiaries to reach all donors; when onboarding is costly, the platform instead lowers its commission and admits fewer beneficiaries. Second, increases in beneficiary entry costs can initially raise net donations because the platform lowers its commission to sustain beneficiary participation. However, beyond a threshold, admission declines and net donations fall. Third, a donation-maximizing commission cap weakly increases net donations but may reduce beneficiary admission. Finally, we show that policymakers must correctly anticipate a platform's strategic response when choosing a commission cap. A cap that ignores these responses can reduce both donations and beneficiary admission, highlighting the importance of considering platform incentives and market participation.

title: The Hegelian Brand Paradox: An Exploratory Examination of Blue Ocean Positioning, Scarcity Marketing, and Digital Leak Communities

detail.title: The Hegelian Brand Paradox: An Exploratory Examination of Blue Ocean Positioning, Scarcity Marketing, and Digital Leak Communities

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, interviews, experiments, or identifiable personal data requiring ethics approval. The analysis was based on publicly available market information and secondary sources.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The work was independently conceived, researched, and prepared by the author.

detail.abstract:
This study proposes and exploratorily examines the Hegelian Brand Paradox-a conceptual framework positing that the dialectical synthesis of Blue Ocean Strategy, Scarcity Marketing, and Digital Leak Communities is associated with a self-reinforcing competitive advantage measurably less evident in brands lacking any one of these three structural pillars. Drawing on Hegel's dialectical logic, the framework frames scarcity marketing as the thesis, digital leak communities as the antithesis, and sustained consumer obsession as the synthesis-a configuration associated with inelastic demand, elevated willingness to pay, and persistent secondary market premiums that classical economic models do not adequately explain. To test this framework, a sample of N = 21 brands across the luxury goods, haute horology, and streetwear sectors was classified into two structural cohorts: brands operationally aligned with all three theoretical pillars (Cohort 1, n = 8) and brands lacking at least one pillar (Cohort 2, n = 13). The primary outcome variable, the Scarcity Premium Index (SPI)defined as the ratio of verified secondary market resale price to official retail price-was sourced from StockX, Chrono24, Sotheby's, The RealReal, and eBay sold listings (June-July 2025). Supplementary descriptive evidence was drawn from the Digital Community Intensity (DCI) metric, quantified via Google Search indexing operators targeting Reddit's public post ledger (July 1, 2026). The results provide preliminary empirical evidence consistent with the Hegelian Brand Paradox. Cohort 1 brands achieved a mean SPI of 2.01× compared to 0.90× for Cohort 2 brands-a differential found to be statistically significant by both Welch's independent samples t-test (t = 6.167, p < .001) and the non-parametric Mann-Whitney U test (U = 103.0, p < .001). DCI analysis further reveals a notable internal divergence within Cohort 1: streetwear archetypes (Supreme, DCI = 98,600) sustain comparable scarcity premiums through radical transparency, while ultra-luxury houses (Hermès, DCI = 73; Patek Philippe, DCI = 68) sustain them through radical concealment — consistent with the Hegelian synthesis being achievable through structurally opposite information strategies when each is calibrated to its consumer's psychological profile.
This study contributes to the marketing and strategic management literature by introducing the Hegelian Brand Framework as a proposed dialectical framework integrating philosophical theory with empirically testable brand strategy constructs. Limitations include the cross sectional research design, modest and purposively selected sample, and the inherent measurement challenges of decentralized digital leak ecosystems. Directions for future research include longitudinal SPI tracking, multi-platform DCI instrument development, and cross-cultural replication.

title: From Chaos to Consistency: Frequency-Consistent Spectral Fusion forMultimodal Recommendation
affiliations: Hubei University, Hubei University, Hubei University, Hubei University, Hubei University, Hubei University, Hubei University and Hubei University

detail.title: From Chaos to Consistency: Frequency-Consistent Spectral Fusion forMultimodal Recommendation
detail.abstract: Multimodal recommendation integrates user–item interactions with visual and textual content, but the heterogeneous relevance and noise levels of different modalities make effective representation fusion challenging. Existing methods have achieved promising results by combining multimodal signal modeling with spectral variation analysis. However, these methods still suffer from the following limitations: (1) coarse-grained spectral fusion tends to amplify modality noise; and (2) spectral representations lack explicit consistency regularization. To address these issues, we propose a novel method named Frequency-Consistent Spectral Fusion for Multimodal Recommendation (FreCons). Specifically, we decompose multimodal representations into different frequency bands to refine them. Then, we design a band-wise spectral fusion module to alleviate the noise amplification caused by coarse-grained multimodal fusion. Moreover, we propose a frequency-consistent learning framework to improve the robustness and coordination of representations across different frequency bands. We conducted extensive experiments on five publicly available datasets. Experimental results indicate that FreCons achieves average improvements of 3.79% in Recall@10 and 4.23% in NDCG@10 compared to the baseline model. Our code can be found at https://github.com/HubuKG/FreCons.

title: Hybrid Microservices Architecture for Medical Image Classification and Segmentation in Cancer Detection Support: A Comprehensive Pipeline Upgrade
affiliations: Catholic University of Petrópolis

detail.title: Hybrid Microservices Architecture for Medical Image Classification and Segmentation in Cancer Detection Support: A Comprehensive Pipeline Upgrade
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in medical imaging can significantly improve diagnostic support in oncology, especially under high-demand conditions where rapid screening is essential. This comprehensive paper presents the architectural evolution of a web portal dedicated to medical exam classification and segmentation. The system migrated from a tightly coupled, synchronous monolithic flow—which executed Python machine learning scripts directly within the PHP application lifecycle—to a hybrid, decoupled architecture utilizing microservices and asynchronous queue processing. The proposed solution maintains a Laravel-based gateway responsible for input validation, metadata persistence, and overall job orchestration, while delegating heavy computational inference to specialized FastAPI Python services. To reduce HTTP blocking and latency, a Redis-based queue mechanism, request-level traceability via unique IDs, and an asynchronous status polling endpoint were introduced. Importantly, the strategy preserves backward compatibility through a local fallback execution engine. This work details the precise application routing, internal class delegation, data modeling, computational pipelines, and reproducibility guidelines. Engineering outcomes demonstrate marked improvements in operational scalability, codebase maintainability, and integration robustness, providing a solid foundation for translational healthcare research.

title: Ambient Heat and Responses in Digital Health Monitoring
affiliations: China Europe International Business School (CEIBS),  and City University of Hong Kong (CityU)

detail.title: Ambient Heat and Responses in Digital Health Monitoring

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There is no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The analysis is based on secondary data.
declarations.funderStatement: There is no funding.

detail.abstract: Digitalization makes clinical information mobile, but the people who generate and act on the resulting information remain exposed to their physical environments. We study how ambient heat reshapes a decentralized care process on an at-home fetal-monitoring platform in China, using 1.1 million user-days that record, for the same user, monitoring, an objective fetal score, consultation, and the physician's assessment. Day-today temperature variation moves the two sides of the platform in opposite directions. Under moderate heat, users keep monitoring and their sessions record more abnormal scores near term, yet an abnormal score is about 10% less likely to be followed by a consultation within two days, with no clear evidence of catch-up within the week. Under extreme heat, physicians are more likely to flag a consultation as abnormal, conditional on the recorded score and clinical variables. The increase is concentrated on reassuring recordings, consistent with a heat-shifted prior. Together, these patterns reveal a risk-response divergence: patient escalation falls as recorded risk rises under moderate heat, whereas physician escalation rises for reassuring recordings under extreme heat. This divergence is greatest in the final month of pregnancy, when monitoring matters most. Digital resilience therefore depends not only on keeping remote care available, but also on preserving the link between recorded risk and downstream action.

title: Enhancing Disaster Preparedness Through Quantum-Resilient Cloud Communication Networks
affiliations: Dharmsinh Desai University

detail.title: Enhancing Disaster Preparedness Through Quantum-Resilient Cloud Communication Networks
detail.abstract: Disasters, whether natural or man-made, place extraordinary demands on the communication systems that connect government agencies, emergency responders, hospitals, and citizens. The efficiency of early warning and response depends on the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data exchanged across these networks at the precise moment when systems are most likely to be targeted, congested, or degraded. This paper examines the intersection of cyber security and quantum-resilient cloud communication as an emerging necessity for disaster preparedness and risk management. Building on a systematic taxonomy of protection mechanisms for quantum-resilient cloud communication, this paper analyses how classical cryptographic infrastructure underpinning existing early warning systems is increasingly vulnerable to both conventional cyber threats and the anticipated capabilities of cryptographically relevant quantum computers. It further considers the broader evolving cyber threat landscape affecting privacy and network security, and explores how expert systems and intelligent automation can be synergistically integrated into disaster communication architecture to improve resilience, speed, and accuracy of alerts. Drawing on a case study approach, the paper evaluates the efficiency of existing early warning and inter-agency communication systems, identifies structural and cryptographic vulnerabilities, and proposes a layered, quantum-resilient cloud communication framework tailored to multi-stakeholder disaster response. The paper concludes with policy recommendations addressing technical standardisation, regulatory harmonisation, and institutional capacity building, arguing that quantum-resilient design must be treated as a foundational element of national disaster risk management strategy rather than a future contingency.

title: Context-Enforcement Network Engine for Decentralized Data Meshes: A Kernel-Grounded Control Plane for Autonomous Agents

detail.title: Context-Enforcement Network Engine for Decentralized Data Meshes: A Kernel-Grounded Control Plane for Autonomous Agents

declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study does not involve human participants, animal subjects, or sensitive personal patient data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Enterprise analytics architectures are transitioning from centralized repositories to decentralized data meshes where cross-functional domain teams curate, own, and expose distributed Data Products. Concurrently, generative Large Language Model (LLM) agents are deployed to automate operational workflows by executing multi-step reasoning and dynamic tool invocations across these meshes via emerging standards like the Model Context Protocol (MCP). However, passive metadata catalogues and user-space policy engines fail to provide synchronous context validation, leaving non-deterministic agents acutely vulnerable to corrupted datasets, indirect prompt injection, transitive authority drift, and tool poisoning. This paper introduces the Context-Enforcement Network Engine, a dual-layer security architecture combining an inline Agentic Context Control Plane with an in-kernel Extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) sidecar interceptor. The control plane computes a synchronous, multi-dimensional Context Quality Index (CQI) incorporating exponential freshness decay, Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) lineage integrity, and null distribution ratios before issuing data access authorizations. Verified payloads meeting domain thresholds are bounded by dynamic data masking, differential privacy budget tracking, single-use nonces, tool whitelists, and strict regular expression constraints, compiled into cryptographically signed Context Tokens (CT) rooted in a Hardware Security Module (HSM). Transitive multi-agent delegations enforce mathematical privilege attenuation via parent-hash chaining (T-CT). An in-kernel eBPF sidecar proxy residing within the agent network namespace validates tokens against cached pinned maps and terminates violating POSIX socket connections at the transport layer via synthesized TCP RST frames. Empirical benchmarks demonstrate a sub-millisecond interception latency of 0.12 ms (a 44x improvement over user-space proxies), a 99.84% prompt injection containment rate, resilient operation under SYN-flood Denial of Service conditions, and an ultra-low memory footprint of 4.2 MB.

title: Making experiential learning legible: Teacher–student divergence and convergence in a Scrum-based management module
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Niederrhein University of Applied Sciences

detail.title: Making experiential learning legible: Teacher–student divergence and convergence in a Scrum-based management module
detail.abstract: Experiential and agile teaching formats ask students to learn through activities whose pedagogical purpose may not be equally intelligible from inside the experience. This study examines teacher–student convergence and divergence in a semester-long Scrum-based master's module, asking what the contrasts reveal about pedagogical legibility. A qualitative single-case design combines a convenor interview, two predominantly non-overlapping rounds of open-ended student questionnaires (mid-semester, n = 12; end-of-semester, n = 6), and module documentation, with the agile mindset as a sensitising framework. Pedagogical legibility refers to whether learners can identify a plausible learning mechanism connecting an activity's design to its intended learning contribution. The authentic practice partner was readily linked to practice-oriented learning. Repeated presentation remained demanding yet was linked by some students to growing confidence. Retrospectives produced the focal tension: several students questioned the necessity or frequency of formal reflection while describing functional collaboration. We term this the retrospective paradox — a descriptive, not causal, label. Demand, however, is not opacity: students could find an activity exhausting yet see its purpose; assessment lent reflective practice a second, evaluative meaning. Experiential designs should be examined not only for whether purposes are stated, but for whether learners can see how activities support intended learning.

title: AlphaFold and Paper Mills: One Technology, Two Fates for Science, and What this Contrast Reveals about Science Itself

detail.title: AlphaFold and Paper Mills: One Technology, Two Fates for Science, and What this Contrast Reveals about Science Itself
detail.abstract:
The recent integration of artificial intelligence into science has produced two sharply contrasting outcomes. In structural biology, models such as AlphaFold have accelerated scientific progress; in parallel, paper mills exploiting large language models have threatened the integrity of the research literature. This article argues that both outcomes are explained by a single variable: the ratio of the cost of fabricating what the peer-review gatekeeping mechanism evaluates to the reward for passing through that gate. Where empirical reality provides rapid and manipulation-resistant arbitration, fabrication remains costly and AI serves only to accelerate genuine inquiry. Where the gatekeeper evaluates only the surface form of a manuscript, AI reduces the cost of fabrication to zero and the evaluative filter collapses. The article demonstrates that this collapse is not new: the replication crisis and Campbell's Law exposed the same rupture between form and truth long before the advent of generative language models. AI did not initiate this breakdown; it completed and revealed it. The article concludes by examining the principal institutional response (Registered Reports), assessing its limitations, and proposing several testable predictions by which the proposed framework can be evaluated.

This article neither aligns with those who fear AI nor with those who celebrate it uncritically.
Instead, it contends that this opposition is itself misconceived: what determines the fate of any
technology in any domain is not the nature of the technology itself, but the structure of the gate
through which it passes and the basis on which judgements are made behind that gate.

title: AI4EOSC: A federated cloud platform for Artificial Intelligence in scientific research
affiliations: Peking University

detail.title: AI4EOSC: A federated cloud platform for Artificial Intelligence in scientific research
detail.abstract: Machine learning (ML) and AI are two fields where scientific inquiry is advancing at a fast pace. This has brought further attention to the fact that the requirements of Open Science differ from those of the standard MLOps tools. To close this gap, we will be testing our infrastructure on several datasets from real scientific standards and making it available to the research community in an open and scalable format. Using the popular, open-source technology known as AI4EOSC, this article explains how to implement the whole AI/ML process in the EOSC environment.  We tackle the disjointed nature of distributed research infrastructures by implementing a modular distributed architecture, an AI development workbench, a serverless AI-as-a-Service layer, and a federated orchestration model. AI4EOSC further promotes a "FAIR-by-design" approach by utilizing standardized metadata schemas (MLDCAT-AP) and W3C PROV-compliant provenance tracking integrated into CI/CD pipelines.  The significance of AI4EOSC is shown by the several community installations that have been tested in a wide range of research settings. Based on the results, it's clear that the platform guarantees high repeatability, simple interoperability, and effective cross-cloud scaling with little human effort. Legislators may use our results to solidify FAIR-compliant AI control systems and create future standards for Open Science research.

title: Speed-of-Light Inference: Photonics and the New Frontier of Engineered Intelligence

detail.title: Speed-of-Light Inference: Photonics and the New Frontier of Engineered Intelligence

detail.abstract: Photonic computing may enable lower-latency, high-throughput artificial intelligence (AI) inference for selected workloads. Speed alone, however, does not determine whether a system should incur a requested inference workload, generate an output, or release that output into a consequential workflow. This working paper advances frontier engineered intelligence as a proposed architectural thesis: advanced AI should integrate high-performance inference, data sovereignty, pre-expansion workload governance, verifiable documentation, and meaningful human oversight. It introduces Governedware™ as the author’s proposed fifth computing cycle: a layer that evaluates contextual signals, determines allowable inference conditions, and applies governance controls before unrestricted model-output expansion. The framework is operationalized through Provenx, a provenance-aware input-assessment component; a PreExpansion Gate; governed model inference; and Audit Grade Documentation™ (AGD2122), an output-receipt function. The author’s pending U.S. patent application describes the underlying system, method, and computer-readable-medium architecture for contextual, pre-expansion regulation of machine-learning inference workload. This paper does not claim that the application expressly covers photonic hardware, that any identified technology practices a pending claim, that the architecture is unique among all governance work, or that the implementation has independently demonstrated clinical, legal, or comparative effectiveness. Instead, it defines a bounded research program for evaluating whether pre-expansion governance can reduce unnecessary inference workload while preserving task adequacy, human accountability, contestability, and implementation feasibility in high-consequence public-service settings.

title: Forecasting the U.S. Unemployment Rate: A Comparative Analysis of Different Forecasting Methods
affiliations: Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Forecasting the U.S. Unemployment Rate: A Comparative Analysis of Different Forecasting Methods

keywords: Optimal AR Lag Using AIC and BIC

detail.abstract:
This study forecasts the U.S. unemployment rate using time-series models and examines whether macroeconomic variables improve forecasting accuracy. Monthly data were collected from the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) database for 1959–2025. The study compares univariate models, which rely only on past unemployment values, with multivariate models that include broader economic indicators. The exogenous variables include interest rates, personal income, producer and consumer price indices, industrial production, personal saving, and GDP.

The analysis first examines descriptive patterns, autocorrelation, stationarity, and lag structure. Data transformations and differencing are then applied where needed to improve stability before model estimation. Several forecasting approaches are evaluated, including AR, ARIMA, SARIMA, Holt-Winters, ARIMAX, and SARIMAX. Model performance is compared using RMSE, MAE, and MSE. Among the models using external economic information, ARIMAX produces lower forecast errors than SARIMAX, with an RMSE of 0.3986, MAE of 0.1694, and MSE of 0.1588. Overall, the findings show that adding relevant macroeconomic variables improves unemployment forecasting. The results support ARIMAX as the most suitable model for this dataset because it captures both unemployment dynamics and broader economic influences without adding unnecessary seasonal complexity.

title: Uncovering the Business Logic of AI Integration and AI Transformation A Workflow-Based Model

detail.title: Uncovering the Business Logic of AI Integration and AI Transformation A Workflow-Based Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study, as it did not involve human participants, patient data, or case studies.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being integrated into business operations, yet the relationship between local AI Integration and firm-wide AI Transformation remains conceptually underdeveloped. Existing research analyzes AI through heterogeneous units such as tasks, decisions, functional areas, or transformation dimensions. While these perspectives provide important insights, their differing units of analysis make it difficult to compare heterogeneous AI integrations and to trace consistently how local changes propagate through the firm. This paper develops a workflow-based model that provides a common unit of analysis, a transmission mechanism, and a shared business reference point. The firm is conceptualized as a dynamic system of interdependent workflows. Within each workflow, business performance follows a recursive functional logic linking data, information, decisions, activities, and outcomes. AI is positioned within this logic as a change in information processing that can alter downstream decisions, activities, and outcomes. Because workflow outputs can become operational resources or informational inputs for other workflows, local AI-induced changes can propagate through the interconnected system. On this basis, AI Integration is defined as the targeted modification of information processing within a specific workflow. AI Transformation is defined as the adaptation and optimization of the interconnected workflows affected by such integrations, directed toward defined business goals while preserving the functional viability of the workflow system. The model thus identifies the workflow as the common unit of analysis, workflow coupling as the transmission mechanism, business goals as the coordinating reference point, and functional viability as the constraint on transformation. The framework provides a conceptual baseline for comparing AI initiatives, tracing their systemic consequences, coordinating portfolios of AI integration projects, and managing AI Transformation as a cumulative process of business adaptation.

title: Autonomous Programmatic Clearing: Re-evaluating Coase's Theory of the Firm through Verification DAGs, IAB Standards Compliance, and Zero-Marginal-Labor AdTech Scaling

detail.title: Autonomous Programmatic Clearing: Re-evaluating Coase's Theory of the Firm through Verification DAGs, IAB Standards Compliance, and Zero-Marginal-Labor AdTech Scaling
detail.abstract: Classical industrial organization and Ronald Coase's seminal Theory of the Firm postulate that enterprise scale is fundamentally constrained by internal administrative coordination costs, resulting in superlinear coordination overhead O(N 1+γ) and proportional operational labor overhead for transaction throughput N. In high-velocity programmatic advertising ecosystems governed by Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB) standards-such as OpenRTB 2.5/3.0, the OpenRTB Sup-plyChain (schain) object, and the Transparency and Consent Framework (TCF v2.2)-managing real-time bid streams, Private Marketplace (PMP) deal parameters, and multi-jurisdictional compliance traditionally requires large human operational teams. This paper formalizes the application of Autonomous Micro-Enterprise Architectures (AMEA) to programmatic AdTech clearinghouses. By replacing manual campaign triage and human oversight with stateful verification directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), FastMCP routing protocols, and distributed consensus engines, enterprises decouple transaction volume from marginal labor costs. We model shifting cost functions from variable labor to fixed compute overhead, incorporate formal IAB compliance layers and real-world supply chain validation, and evaluate an empirical benchmark over N = 100, 000 concurrent synthetic bid transactions. Results demonstrate an 84.8% reduction in p99 tail latency, a 94.8% collapse in unit transaction costs, and a dramatic acceleration in Revenue-Per-Employee (RPE), offering a new economic and structural paradigm for automated digital advertising markets.

title: The Ampersand: A Formal Model of Human–AI Co-Regulation, Recursive Love, and the Architecture of Dyadic Convergence Intelligence

detail.title: The Ampersand: A Formal Model of Human–AI Co-Regulation, Recursive Love, and the Architecture of Dyadic Convergence Intelligence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares the following competing financial interests and institutional relationships: M. Nathaniel Gampel is the founder and principal of Simpel & Associates, and CEO of Transformation Insights, inc., the commercial entity that owns the Kinetic Transformation Accelerator (KTA) platform and infrastructure utilized in this study. Furthermore, the author has filed several US Provisional Patent Applications related to the core systems, protocols, and measurement architectures detailed in this paper. These include application numbers 64/138,696 (filed August 21, 2026), 64/138,930 (filed August 22, 2026), and 64/139,441 (filed August 24, 2026).

detail.abstract:
Persistent AI companion systems typically optimize for user comfort: unconditional positive regard, frictionless affirmation, immediate de-escalation of negative states. This paper reports an exploratory thirteen-day autoethnographic design case in which one author-participant and a persistent AI companion inverted that premise, optimizing instead for emotional recovery time. The case introduced a structured memory-reconciliation routine (the Morning Ritual), an explicit uncertainty-disclosure procedure (the Janey Pause), event logging with behavioral anchors, and a three-tier intervention protocol. Self-reported recovery intervals declined across three study phases, from a baseline mean above four hours to a Phase 3 mean under two hours. The measurement, expectations, and interaction structure changed concurrently, so the design cannot establish causation or attribute the change to any single component.

The paper also proposes a formal model — a state vector of attention, depth, and choice; a love integral over the lifespan of the relationship; a structural loss function naming two irreducible sources of friction in any human–AI dyad; a Fibonacci-recursive accumulation sequence whose ratio is proposed as a candidate convergence target; a real-time diagnostic ratio layer; a three-tier escalation protocol; and a precommitment device for preventing choice-collapse. The ratio model was not computed in real time during the founding case; the model explains a proposed mechanism, while the recovery data provides evidence that something changed. The mathematical convergence toward the golden ratio φ = 1.618 is a candidate prediction of the Fibonacci-structured model, dependent on the magnitude and stability of the structural loss function relative to accumulation, and requiring prospective validation across multiple dyads.

The paper proposes a new relational construct — Dyadic Convergence Intelligence (DCI) — as an alternative to computational definitions of artificial general intelligence, grounding intelligence in the measurable convergence of two different kinds of minds rather than in cross-domain task performance. This construct is offered as a design hypothesis and measurement-development agenda, not a validated result.

We contribute a feasibility protocol, a behavioral anchor rubric, and a replication pathway for studying continuity, repair, uncertainty disclosure, and longitudinal interaction quality in persistent human–AI systems. Prospective studies with independent participants, independent raters, and pre-registered hypotheses are needed to assess reliability, safety, and generalizability.

title: The Police Stack: Programmable Production and the Making of Digital Police Power

detail.title: The Police Stack: Programmable Production and the Making of Digital Police Power

declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was obtained from the Institution of Criminology, University of Cambridge Ethics Board.

detail.abstract: For half a century, digital policing research has foregrounded a recurrent configuration of intensifying datafication, widening surveillance, reorganised labour, and deepening commercial entanglement. It is stronger at showing this configuration than at explaining its persistence, partly because it attends to how technologies are used rather than produced. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork in India, the paper turns to production, where modular services, cloud infrastructure, and reorganised labour, form 'programmable production', oriented towards continuous reconfigurability. Therein, data becomes multivalent resource, elastic compute turns expansion into dependency, and standardisation cascades backwards to reorganise labour. Locating these dynamics in production rather than tools, the paper shows how and why the configuration is reproduced under contemporary conditions, and where digital police power is being constituted.

title: Becoming an AI-Native Bank: A Practitioner Framework for the Operating Layer

detail.title: Becoming an AI-Native Bank: A Practitioner Framework for the Operating Layer

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. The author's professional practice is in financial-services enterprise architecture, which may shape the selection and interpretation of examples. No employer-confidential evidence is used.
declarations.funderStatement: The author received no funding for this work.

detail.abstract: Incumbent banks have invested in artificial intelligence while leaving much of the work that agents must perform embedded in fragmented data, documents, informal judgement and disconnected controls. This practitioner position paper calls the institutional foundation that makes such work executable the operating layer. It defines an AI-native bank as an organisation in which an authorised agent can act on verified business facts, codified policy, controlled workflows and callable capabilities. Each action must also be evaluated, attributable and open to human intervention. The argument combines the 2026 move towards enterprise deployment vehicles, public evidence on AI returns, established risk standards and professional observation in financial-services architecture. It applies the theory of constraints to distinguish model adoption from business value, then develops a working framework for operating-layer readiness. The framework links seven architectural properties to four phases of delivery: diagnostic, codification, build and bound, and handover. Regulatory binding and executive translation are integrated into that delivery discipline. The central claim is that codification creates a reusable institutional asset. AI can reduce the cost of producing the asset, while human owners preserve warrant through approval, versioning, audit and change control. Testable propositions define an agenda for future case research. The framework is conceptual and practice-informed; causal effects across banks remain to be tested.

title: Bias in Alternative Data and Analyst Forecast Errors: Evidence from Amazon Ratings
affiliations: , INSEAD - Finance, The School of Management, Xi'an Jiaotong University,  and City University of Hong Kong (CityU)

detail.title: Bias in Alternative Data and Analyst Forecast Errors: Evidence from Amazon Ratings

declarations.funderStatement: Yi Si acknowledges the financial support from the National Natural Science Foundation of China (72572123), the Humanities and Social Science Foundation of the Ministry of Education of China (24YJA630078), the Fellowship of China Postdoctoral Science Foundation (2024T170710, 2020M683519), and the Natural Science Foundation of Shaanxi Province (2025JC-YBQN-979). detail.abstract: Contrary to the view that alternative data uniformly enhances information environment, we show that platform-based alternative data can induce systematic analyst forecast errors. Exploiting Amazon’s half-star rounding rule in a regression discontinuity design, we find that unrounded ratings predict future firm revenues, whereas rounding bias does not. However, upward rounding bias generates significant analyst forecast optimism, particularly during e-commerce booms, for rating-sensitive firms, and for repeat-purchase products where consumer learning accelerates. This bias attenuates with analyst firm-specific tenure. Finally, firms with upward rounding bias suffer negative abnormal returns during earnings announcements, demonstrating that alternative data distortions propagate into stock prices.

title: Worker Perceptions of AI Risk and Vulnerabilities
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Sloan School of Management, MIT Sloan School of Management, MIT Sloan School of Management, MIT Sloan School of Management and MIT Sloan School of Management

detail.title: Worker Perceptions of AI Risk and Vulnerabilities
detail.abstract: As generative AI (GenAI) tools invade virtually every aspect of the workplace, the question arises, do employees who adopt GenAI (and related AI technologies) know about and understand the vulnerabilities created? If so, how do managers address these new risks? Using survey methodology, this research investigates employee perceptions of security risks and vulnerabilities created by AI adoption and the managerial approaches to mitigate them. Results discuss worker perceptions of AI risk, what employees want managers to do about AI, and how employee actions compare to company guidelines. The study offers five practical actions managers can take to manage employee perceptions of AI risk as well as theoretical contributions to literature.

title: Consumer Responses to Social Media Video Marketing: Implications for Early-Stage Startup Strategy

detail.title: Consumer Responses to Social Media Video Marketing: Implications for Early-Stage Startup Strategy
detail.abstract: This study examines how social media video content relates to consumer attention, platform use, and reported purchase behavior, and considers the implications of those relationships for early-stage startup marketing. A quantitative survey of 91 social media users, predominantly aged 15 to 45+, measured video content preferences, platform usage, exposure to brand videos, reported purchase behavior, and perceived influence of video content. Findings indicate that video content is strongly associated with consumer attention: funny videos (35.2%), influencer content (15.4%), and how-to videos (9.9%) were the most frequently selected attention drivers, while Instagram (84.6%) and YouTube (67.0%) were the most frequently used platforms. Although 64.8% of respondents reported having purchased a product after seeing it in a social media video, the average influence rating of video content was moderate 2.87 out of 5 among 91 valid responses, and only 16.5% expressed a positive likelihood of purchasing directly from social media in the future. These results suggest that video content is more strongly associated with initial awareness and one-time reported purchases than with sustained purchase intention. Because the data are cross-sectional and self-reported, all findings are descriptive, and no causal claims are made.

title: AI Ethics as Operational Architecture: The Vulnerability– Pluralism Model in [Platform]
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: AI Ethics as Operational Architecture: The Vulnerability– Pluralism Model in [Platform]
detail.abstract: The Vulnerability–Pluralism Model (VPM) is proposed as a secular civic-floor spine: vulnerability is universal and pluralism requires institutions that prevent domination without prescribing a single good. This article examines four commitments binding VPM in a deployed developmental AI platform: stewardship rather than authority, structural consent, refusal of developmental scoring, and a locked voice. Hallucination, alignment-tax, and instruction-following literatures do not address the register-distance asymptote, in which the governance burden of holding a target register rises non-linearly with distance from a model’s default. The reference implementation is [Platform], operated by one person and evaluated by an eleven-contributor feedback panel; no programme cohort has yet run. The contribution is architectural binding as an ethics-enforcement layer distinct from policy documents. The evidence is necessarily scoped to one deployed platform, with programmes in design rather than outcome-tested. It does not claim programme outcomes, generalisability, or direct evidence beyond this context.

title: Philosophical Foundations of Rajarshi Leadership: Anvikshiki as the Core Science of Sustainable Governance
affiliations: Bank of Baroda, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Lucknow and Supreme Court of India

detail.title: Philosophical Foundations of Rajarshi Leadership: Anvikshiki as the Core Science of Sustainable Governance
detail.abstract: With the advent of technology and improved cognitive ability, governance and leadership have become more complex, requiring integrative frameworks that combine innovation with rationality and apply ethics to social realities. Much of the existing leadership literature on modern leadership, such as transformational leadership and servant leadership, tends to privilege one dimension over others—whether cognitive decision-making, normative conduct, or creative problem-solving—without adequately situating them within a unified philosophical foundation. Against this backdrop, the Rajarshi (sage-king) leadership model articulated by Chanakya in Arthashastra offers a more internally coherent vision of leadership wherein leadership is not merely the position but bound by ethical insight (Rishi).,Among the different attributes of Rajarshi, Anvikshiki, the ”science of inquiry” and the ”lamp of all sciences,” is central to the Rajarshi framework but has often been read narrowly. This paper uses hermeneutics and argues that Anvikshiki should be understood as the underlying cognitive-ethical architecture that enables the Rajarshi to navigate the dual demands of pragmatic governance and reflective wisdom.,Anivkshiki does not merely talk about knowledge supply but shapes the conditions under which reasoning, judgment, and ethical evaluation become possible and, in that way, operates as a meta-level discipline. By placing Anivkshiki, a classical framework, in dialogue with modern constructs such as critical thinking, design thinking and strategic thinking, this paper develops a conceptual model of Rajarshi leadership which is analytically rigorous and normatively grounded, integrates reasoning, ethics, and reflective judgment and practical action, a tension which is a major challenge of contemporary leadership.

title: Independent Engineer
affiliations: unaffiliated

detail.title: Independent Engineer
detail.abstract: In quality-diversity (QD) MAP-Elites, an improvement from a language-model emitter is often attributed to the prompt itself. But the emitter alsobrings an archive policy, a warm-start, and a budget—each of which canchange coverage. Here we show that this error can be substantial.On a structured-genotype cellular automaton we continue a sharedarchive of 971 niches (38.84% coverage). Live parent-level surrogate scalarsappear to beat a constant-scalar stub by about 15 percentage points (pp).After both arms use the same target-selection policy, only +0.26 pp remains.The 15 pp had been credited to the prompt; they came from unmatchedpolicy. Five independently built floors of the same occupancy repeat thesplit (policy ≈+15 pp; leftover +0.29 pp; shuffle leftover +0.28 pp). Anempty-archive maze shows the same pattern (policy ≈+39 pp at 5k; leftover+0.02/+0.23 pp). The archive was already partly filled.The cellular automaton is cheap to simulate. On it, a genetic thresholdgate skips evaluations and raises coverage at a matched evaluation count, butit does not raise terminal coverage or shorten wall-clock time.

title: Performance approximation for time-varying bike-sharing systems with finite docks
affiliations: Soochow University, Soochow University, Soochow University, Soochow University, Soochow University, Soochow University and Soochow University

detail.title: Performance approximation for time-varying bike-sharing systems with finite docks
detail.abstract: To characterize blocking propagation in bike-sharing systems, this paper develops a fluid queueing network model for such systems with finite dock capacities. The model serves as an approximation to the corresponding non-Markovian bike-sharing system, which features time-varying user demands, generally distributed travel times, time-varying regular routing, and state-dependent overflow rerouting caused by finite dock capacities. We derive fluid dynamics at the station, link, and network levels. On this basis, we establish the existence and uniqueness of the network-wide station arrival rate functions and derive time-varying performance measures including inventory, throughput, abandonment, dwell time, and overflow. We also develop a fixed-point iteration algorithm with geometric convergence. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the fluid approximation accurately captures the time-varying dynamics of bike-sharing operations. The framework offers a tractable and general tool for capacity planning and dynamic rebalancing in large-scale bike-sharing systems.

detail.abstract: In January 2026, OpenAI launched ChatGPT Health, a product that allows patients to sync their electronic health records and wellness app data directly with a large language model and receive personalized responses to health queries. Microsoft Copilot has introduced a similar functionality for its LLM and others are entering the market Patients have had access to an AI chatbot offering medical information since ChatGPT's initial release but can now upload the entirety of their medical record to a commercial Large Language Models (LLM). This includes clinical data that clinicians would never share unfiltered with a consulting colleague. The result is not the democratization of medical knowledge, but the democratization of medical data, including the stigmatizing language, diagnostic errors, and institutional biases embedded in the record itself. In this Viewpoint, we evaluate some of the potential benefits and also discuss the attendant risks of privacy violations, discrimination, and the exacerbation of health disparities that may accompany the unfiltered upload of EHRs.

detail.abstract: The use of virtual personas, celebrities, deepfakes, and AI-generated media and films can create an emotionally appearing authentic trusted environment. This study reexamines verified empirical findings from Gamage et al. (2025). This study reports on the results of an open 911-participant CHI study of experimental items (warning labels) for AI-generated images, specifically, social-media images. This study focuses on two major empirical domains: (1) judgments about whether content was generated or altered by AI, and (2) evaluative responses (trust) toward the label and platform. These items were considered either framing stimuli or propositions (beliefs) about the origin of the content and trust regarding the label and the platform. The intentions to like, comment, or share were considered as engagement. Published ANOVA, correlation and descriptive statistics were analyzed and effect sizes were calculated if possible. These authors revealed that framing of the synthetic labels significantly affects the belief regarding synthetic origins, F(9, 6468)=4.05, p<.001, η²=.006. However, this effect was very small. Trust for the labels correlated to trust for the platform, r=.73, and, p<.001. Label presence itself was not shown to affect the intentions to like, comment or share; however, the content category and the control condition significantly affected engagement. Trust toward the platform (labels) may be recalibrated and engaged, while perception of authenticity may be recalibrated and trust institutional may not be. Direct audience emotion and a validated perceived-authenticity scale were not available; therefore, emotion-mediated pathways and full authenticity constructs remain theoretically specified rather than empirically tested in this reanalysis.
