title: Critical Peak Rebates for Residential Gas: Effectiveness and Selection During the European Energy Crisis
affiliations: ZEW – Leibniz Centre for European Economic Research, University of Augsburg and VU University Amsterdam

detail.title: Critical Peak Rebates for Residential Gas: Effectiveness and Selection During the European Energy Crisis

publicationDetails.detailsText: ZEW – Centre for European Economic Research Discussion Paper No. 26-036

detail.abstract: The abrupt shortage of natural gas imports during the 2022/2023 energy crisis following Russia's war against Ukraine forced European countries to rapidly cut consumption. In response, governments and energy providers introduced voluntary gas-saving programs offering financial incentives to residential customers. We study one such program-a critical peak rebate (CPR) launched by one of Germany's largest energy providers-that offered a six-month per-unit bonus for demand reductions at a time when wholesale gas prices spiked but regulated retail prices remained fixed, muting the price signal households actually faced. Combining household meter readings with survey data, we use a difference-indifferences design to "stress test" a CPR scheme. We show that the program-induced average gas savings amount to 13.2 to 17 percent. Participation was more likely among higher consumption, higher income and pro-socially motivated households, who also achieved larger absolute savings. This reveals a trade-off between program effectiveness and distributional considerations in the design of demand flexibility programs.

title: Data leakage and cross-dataset generalization in breast ultrasound classification: an audit of the BUSI benchmark and an evaluation of transfer to an independent cohort
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Data leakage and cross-dataset generalization in breast ultrasound classification: an audit of the BUSI benchmark and an evaluation of transfer to an independent cohort
detail.abstract: Background. The Breast Ultrasound Images (BUSI) dataset is the most widely used public benchmark for breast-ultrasound classification. Reported performance on it is high, and for the three-class task several studies report a recall of 100% for the healthy (normal) category. We ask how much of that performance comes from the images themselves and how much from the way the dataset is built, and whether anything that survives transfers to an independent cohort. Methods. We audited all 780 BUSI images for exact and near-duplicate content with a DCT-based perceptual hash, and for label conflicts inside the resulting duplicate groups. We then corrected the evaluation itself: group-aware nested cross-validation that keeps near-duplicates in one fold, a model input with the expert segmentation mask removed, and decision thresholds chosen on validation data alone. Against this protocol we switched three leakage sources back on, one at a time, and measured each: the mask in the input, mask-derived region-of-interest cropping, and duplicate leakage across splits. One ablation replaces the network with a logistic regression on 20 global image statistics, so its result cannot depend on the architecture. Finally we froze the BUSI-trained encoder, applied it unchanged to the independent BUS-BRA cohort (1,875 images from 1,064 patients), and split the transfer gap into preprocessing and scannervendor parts. Results. About 40% of the BUSI images sit in near-duplicate groups, and eight groups (18 images) carry conflicting labels. Under the leakage-controlled protocol the two-class benign-versus-malignant AUROC is 0.887 ± 0.018, and three-class recall of the normal category falls to 70.8% ± 15.1, which makes it the hardest category rather than the easiest. Putting the mask back into the input lifts the two-class AUROC to 0.995. Mask-based ROI cropping produces a clean dose-response: normal recall runs 100.0 → 99.0 → 85.5% as the field-of-view gap between the classes is closed. The 20-feature probe, with no spatial reasoning at all, still recovers 97.7% normal recall, so what it detects is whether an annotation existed, not healthy tissue. Decision thresholds are unstable, spanning a 10-to-17-fold range across folds. On BUS-BRA the encoder drops to AUROC 0.607 ± 0.031 from a fold-matched internal 0.887 ± 0.018. Scanner vendor does not explain the drop: the GE scanners that make up 91% of the cohort reproduce the overall 0.61 across all five folds. Preprocessing does not explain it either, since on a single fold aspect-ratio and contrast correction each recover less than 0.04 AUROC. Conclusion. Much of the accuracy reported on BUSI reflects how the dataset is assembled rather than diagnostic skill. We identify which artefacts are responsible and by how much, and show that a model with them removed does not generalize to an independent cohort. Work with this dataset should therefore use group-aware evaluation, mask-free inputs, thresholds fixed on validation data, and external validation.

title: Understanding Structural Barriers and Opportunities for Scaling Agroecological Innovations: Lessons from Push-Pull Technology in East Africa
affiliations: Ataturk University, International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology (ICIPE), affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology (ICIPE), Ataturk University, International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology, International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology, Justus Liebig University Giessen and Justus Liebig University Giessen

detail.title: Understanding Structural Barriers and Opportunities for Scaling Agroecological Innovations: Lessons from Push-Pull Technology in East Africa
detail.abstract: CONTEXT: Agroecological innovations such as Push–Pull Technology (PPT) offer promising solutions to interconnected challenges of pest pressure, soil degradation, and climate vulnerability in smallholder systems. Despite well-documented benefits, the scaling of PPT remains limited.,OBJECTIVE: This study applies the Agricultural Innovation Systems (AIS) framework to examine the actors, systemic barriers, and opportunities influencing PPT adoption and scaling in Kenya and Uganda, with emphasis on how structural-functional dynamics shape innovation performance.,METHODS: A qualitative multi-actor design was employed, involving 85 key informant interviews across six AIS domains and 18 focus group discussions. Data were analyzed using a hybrid coding strategy combining deductive codes with inductively emerging themes, which are categorized under AIS functions and micro-level systemic failures and opportunities.,RESULTS: Transdisciplinary collaboration among stakeholders has transformed PPT from a pest management technology into a multifunctional agroecological innovation that enhances pest control, soil fertility, crop productivity, livestock feed availability, and environmental sustainability. However, scaling remains constrained by weak institutional integration, fragmented extension systems, limited private-sector engagement, inadequate multi-actor coordination, and persistent perceptions of PPT as an experimental technology. Entrepreneurial initiatives, including community-based seed multiplication, fodder commercialization, and cooperative development, provide pathways toward localized ownership and market integration.,CONCLUSIONS: Sustainable scaling of PPT requires strengthening innovation governance through improved coordination among research, extension, policy, and market actors, while expanding participatory extension approaches and community-led initiatives. The findings demonstrate that effective scaling of agroecological innovations depends on robust innovation systems that integrate institutions, markets, and knowledge networks, offering lessons for broader agroecological transitions across sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Cross-device evaluation of photoplethysmography-based atrial fibrillation screening: a pilot comparison of raw-waveform and pulse-rate-variability models
affiliations: Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Iasi, Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Iasi and Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Iasi

detail.title: Cross-device evaluation of photoplethysmography-based atrial fibrillation screening: a pilot comparison of raw-waveform and pulse-rate-variability models
detail.abstract: Background and Objective: Photoplethysmography (PPG)-based atrial fibrillation (AF) classifiers may perform well in their development dataset yet fail after transfer to another sensor and clinical setting. We assessed transfer from clinical PPG to a low-cost device and tested whether sampling-rate manipulation alone explains external behavior.Methods: A CNN-BiLSTM, Random Forest, and XGBoost were developed with MIMIC PERform AF (35 subjects; 19 AF and 16 non-AF; 125~Hz). The CNN used raw signals; tree models used six PPG-derived pulse-rate-variability features. Subject-disjoint five-fold cross-validation preceded zero-shot testing in 10 hospital patients (2 AF; 8 non-AF) recorded at approximately 26~Hz with an ESP32+MAX30102. ECG was concurrent for nine patients and preceded PPG by approximately 10 minutes for one non-AF patient. A 125-to-26-to-125~Hz MIMIC experiment served as a sampling-rate negative control.Results: Within MIMIC, window-level AUC was 0.921 for the PPG+ECG CNN, 0.829 for the separately trained PPG-only CNN, 0.919 for Random Forest, and 0.920 for XGBoost. Patient-level AUC for the PPG-only CNN was 0.694. Externally, the PPG-only CNN predicted AF for all patients (2/10 correct; specificity 0/8). Random Forest and XGBoost made the same patient-level calls (7/10 correct; sensitivity 2/2; specificity 5/8). Resampling changed patient-level AUC from 0.694 to 0.691 for the PPG-only CNN and from 0.921 to 0.928 for Random Forest, without changing any subject classification.Conclusions: Source-domain performance did not predict external behavior. Resampling alone did not reproduce the failure, but the experiment cannot identify hardware as causal because device, population, site, and acquisition conditions remained confounded. Larger multi-device validation is required.

title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Financial Volatility Forecasting: Uncertainty-Gated Residual Boosting Across Prophet-Style, Gradient-Boosting, and Classical Time-Series Models

detail.title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Financial Volatility Forecasting: Uncertainty-Gated Residual Boosting Across Prophet-Style, Gradient-Boosting, and Classical Time-Series Models
detail.abstract: Financial volatility forecasting is a setting in which flexible machine-learning models can exploit nonlinear interactions, yet unconstrained corrections can become unreliable when market dynamics move away from the conditions represented in the training sample. This paper develops Uncertaintyand Disagreement-Gated Residual Boosting (UDGRB), a concrete hybrid forecasting algorithm rather than a model-agnostic framework. The method first constructs a dynamic structural anchor from ARIMA, simple exponential smoothing, a heterogeneous autoregressive (HAR) model, and a transparent Prophet-style additive trend model with piecewise-linear changepoints and Fourier seasonality. A LightGBM residual learner then predicts the remaining log-volatility error. Two quantile LightGBM models estimate residual-correction uncertainty, while cross-model dispersion measures structural disagreement. A multiplicative gate shrinks the machine-learning correction according to these two signals; the gate penalties are selected only on a chronologically separate validation period and are allowed to be exactly zero, yielding data-driven sparsification or fallback when a gating signal has no incremental value. The empirical study uses 7,983 real Microsoft daily OHLCV observations from 13 March 1986 to 10 November 2017, distributed with the public pmdarima dataset and traceable to the Kaggle US stocks/ETFs price-volume collection. We form 1,598 leakage-controlled weekly forecasting observations after lag construction and evaluate 567 one-week-ahead forecasts from 2007-2017. The primary target is annualized close-to-close realized volatility; a Parkinson high-low range estimator supplies an alternative volatility proxy. Baselines include naive persistence, ARIMA, exponential smoothing, HAR, the Prophet-style additive model, standalone LightGBM, and dynamic forecast combination. On close-to-close volatility, UDGRBachieves the lowest MAE (8.292) and MASE (0.610), improving MAE by 3.09% over standalone LightGBM; the Diebold-Mariano test for absolute-error loss gives p = 0.0427. On the Parkinson target, the validation criterion selects the no-shrinkage corner, so the method automatically reduces to the residual hybrid; it again obtains the lowest MAE (7.177). HAR produces the best variance-scale QLIKE on both targets, showing that the ranking is loss-dependent rather than universally dominated by one model. Importantly, on the primary target the uncertainty gate reduces QLIKE relative to the ungated residual hybrid by 0.0241 on average, with an eight-week moving-block bootstrap 95% interval of [-0.0640,-0.0003]. The experiments therefore identify a specific role for uncertainty-aware residual shrinkage: it improves point accuracy and protects residual boosting when validation evidence supports intervention, while preserving a statistically stronger structural solution when it does not.

title: Electro-anatomical Factors Contributing to Arrhythmia Recurrence as Atypical Flutter After PVI. Atrial Computer Model
affiliations: Health Research Institute Hospital La Fe, La Fe University and Polytechnic Hospital, La Fe University and Polytechnic Hospital, Spain and Centro de Investigaciones Biomédicas en RED en Enfermedades Cardiovasculares (CIBERCV), La Fe University and Polytechnic Hospital, La Fe University and Polytechnic Hospital, Polytechnic University of Valencia, Polytechnic University of Valencia, Polytechnic University of Valencia and Health Research Institute Hospital La Fe

detail.title: Electro-anatomical Factors Contributing to Arrhythmia Recurrence as Atypical Flutter After PVI. Atrial Computer Model
detail.abstract: Aims,After pulmonary vein isolation (PVI), 4-10% of patients show atypical flutter recurrence, most commonly, perimitral flutter (PMF). The factors that favor this phenomenon have not been fully described. This study evaluates different electro-anatomical factors and their impact in PMF recurrence after PVI using computer models.,Methods and results,Computational simulations were performed in three realistic bi-atrial models, with four different ablation patterns, which vary in the corridor size after PVI. Model characterization was performed using clinically acquired data from electro-anatomical maps. The Courtemanche et al. cellular model was adjusted to match clinically measured effective refractory period (ERP) values. An arrhythmogenic activity was induced and its temporal evolution was studied, classified as non-sustained arrhythmia, atrial fibrillation (AF) or PMF. The influence of several electro-anatomical factors on arrhythmic activity evolution was studied, such as conduction velocity (CV), posterior wall corridor size, left atrium volume, ERP, anisotropy, and the reconnection of a lateral mitral isthmus ablation line. Greater PMF organization was observed in models with slower CV, larger volumes, and narrower conduction gaps in the mitral ablation line. Statistically significant differences were observed for posterior wall narrowing (P<0.01), prolonged ERP (P<0.01), and increased anisotropy ratios (P=0.02), all of which were associated with higher PMF organization.,Conclusion,Electro-anatomical measures in patients with PMF showed a reduced CV around the perimitral region. Simulation analyses suggested that this slower conduction may facilitate PMF stabilization. PMF recurrence appeared to be influenced by multiple factors, including ERP, anisotropy, and conduction gaps along prior ablation lines.

title: Disclosure Without Duty: Illinois's Disability Designation and the Standard It Inverts

detail.title: Disclosure Without Duty: Illinois's Disability Designation and the Standard It Inverts
detail.abstract: On August 21, 2026, Illinois enacted a statute permitting driver's license applicants to request an intellectual disability or autism spectrum disorder designation on the credential. The measure joins three existing instruments aimed at the same encounter, awareness registration plates, awareness decals, and the Blue Envelope Program enacted three months earlier, and like each of its predecessors, it moves information from the disabled person toward the officer while attaching no obligation to the officer who receives it. This Article argues that the designation inverts the allocation of duty that federal disability law already fixes. Under Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act and its implementing regulations, the obligation to communicate effectively rests on the public entity and is not conditioned on self-identification, and the governing wrongful-arrest standard asks whether the officer knew or should have known of the disability. A designation regime converts that constructive-knowledge standard into an actual-notice production burden carried by the protected class. The Article further contends that the statute's voluntariness defense fails on its own terms. Survey evidence establishes that a majority of autistic adults decline to disclose a diagnosis to police, and that the stated reason is fear of how police will respond, so the statute solicits from the protected class precisely the conduct that class has already declined for reasons the record supplies. Finally, the designation is keyed to the one encounter in which a licensed driver produces a credential, while the encounters that generate serious injury are pedestrian stops, welfare checks, and family emergency calls, several of them cases in which the disability was already known to the responding agency. The enrolled text confirms a further asymmetry. The same statute amends the Vehicle Code's confidentiality section to add confirmation of an intellectual disability or autism spectrum disorder to the documents held by the Secretary of State, and then exempts from confidentiality both law enforcement officials conducting any civil or criminal investigation and any other entities the Secretary may authorize by rule. Three months earlier the same legislature enacted a companion disclosure tool that expressly forbids entering the same information into any database. The Article closes by identifying what a duty-creating statute would contain, using a sister-state enactment that paired an identical designation with a mandatory training requirement.

title: A local melting arrival time field guided deep learning framework for the design and optimization of ocean thermal energy conversion heat engines
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A local melting arrival time field guided deep learning framework for the design and optimization of ocean thermal energy conversion heat engines
detail.abstract: Ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) systems provide an important technical pathway for environmentally self-powered underwater platforms, where the melting rate and melting uniformity of the phase-change heat-transfer unit directly affect the cycle period and energy conversion efficiency of the heat engine. However, existing fin optimizations usually rely on complete melting time and liquid fraction, making it difficult to resolve the spatial propagation sequence of the melting front in the PCM region. Moreover, a large number of transient CFD simulations substantially increases the computational cost of screening complex fin configurations and limits rapid optimization in high-dimensional geometric design spaces. This study proposes a local melting arrival-time field-guided deep learning optimization framework to establish an effective mapping among fin design parameters, local melting-time fields, and overall heat-transfer performance. The fin geometry is first continuously represented using a signed distance function (SDF) and then input into a deep convolutional network to reconstruct the local melting arrival-time field in the PCM region and further predict the complete melting time and melting-time nonuniformity. By coupling the scalar surrogate model with the NSGA-II multi-objective optimization algorithm, the framework rapidly screens candidate configurations under constant metal usage and geometric feasibility constraints, enabling efficient and physically interpretable optimization of phase-change heat-transfer structures. The optimized configurations obtained by the proposed framework exhibit shorter complete melting times and more uniform phase-change processes. The results show that ResUNet reconstructs the melting-time field with high accuracy, with average RMSE, R², PSNR, and SSIM values of 59.55 s, 0.972, 27.68 dB, and 0.917, respectively. The scalar prediction model achieves an average relative error of 4.87% and an overall R² higher than 0.985. Compared with CNN-1D, the MAEs of complete melting time and melting nonuniformity are reduced by 9.6% and 15.1%, respectively. Multi-objective optimization yields 60 Pareto non-dominated solutions; representative configurations show CFD-validated deviations below 2.8%, and their complete melting times are reduced by 12.4%-21.7% relative to the RSM optimum. The proposed framework improves the design efficiency of phase-change units in OTEC heat engines and provides an effective method for optimizing environmentally self-powered underwater systems.

title: When Technologies Shape Innovation Systems: Evidence from Agricultural Bioinputs
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: When Technologies Shape Innovation Systems: Evidence from Agricultural Bioinputs
detail.abstract: CONTEXTAgrifood transitions increasingly depend on innovations whose performance is embedded in complex ecological and institutional contexts. Yet innovation-systems research has primarily examined how institutions, organizations, and networks shape technological development, devoting comparatively less attention to how technological characteristics themselves generate specific institutional requirements.OBJECTIVEThis article develops a technology-sensitive perspective on Agricultural Innovation Systems and applies it to agricultural bioinputs in Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Uruguay. It examines how technological characteristics shape the capacities required for the development, validation, adoption, and scaling of emerging biological technologies.METHODSThe study combines documentary analysis with 25 semi-structured interviews conducted with researchers, regulators, firms, extension specialists, and other actors involved in agricultural biological technologies across the four countries. A comparative analysis was used to identify recurrent technological characteristics and the institutional demands associated with them.RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONSThe analysis identifies five recurrent characteristics of agricultural bioinputs: ecological context dependence, biological variability, knowledge-intensive application, performance uncertainty, and interaction with farming practices. Across the four countries, these characteristics generate recurring demands for localized experimentation and agronomic validation, adaptive regulation and quality assurance, specialized expertise and advisory services, continuous monitoring, and coordination across actors. Although national institutional configurations influence how these demands are addressed, their recurrence across different contexts suggests that they cannot be explained solely by institutional differences. Agrifood transitions therefore require more than technological substitution; they also depend on aligning institutional capacities with the characteristics of emerging technologies.SIGNIFICANCEBy incorporating technological characteristics as an explicit analytical dimension of innovation-systems research, the article extends Agricultural Innovation Systems and Technological Innovation Systems approaches. It provides a framework for identifying the institutional capacities required to support emerging technologies and offers insights for the design of innovation policies aimed at enabling sustainable agrifood transitions.

title: Process Modelling, Simulation and Technoeconomic Evaluation of Batch vs. Continuous Reactive Crystallization for Enzymatic Amoxicillin Synthesis
affiliations: Wuhan Institute of Technology and Wuhan University of Technology

detail.title: Process Modelling, Simulation and Technoeconomic Evaluation of Batch vs. Continuous Reactive Crystallization for Enzymatic Amoxicillin Synthesis
detail.abstract: Cost-effective production of generic antibiotics remains a pressing industrial priority, particularly for high-volume β-lactam APIs where narrow profit margins and stringent environmental regulations constrain manufacturing options. This paper presents an integrated process systems engineering framework for the in-silico design, simulation, and technoeconomic comparison of three amoxicillin manufacturing routes: (i) conventional batch enzymatic synthesis followed by separate pH-swing crystallization; (ii) batch reactive crystallization integrating enzymatic synthesis with in-situ product removal; and (iii) continuous reactive crystallization in a mixed-suspension mixed-product removal (MSMPR) cascade. Kinetic models for penicillin G acylase-catalyzed synthesis are parameterized from literature data, coupled with population balance crystallization kinetics and solubility correlations. The continuous reactive crystallization route achieves the highest reactor productivity and the lowest process mass intensity (PMI = 18.4), yet the conventional batch enzymatic route—despite its larger equipment footprint—emerges as the most economically advantageous, with a total present cost 1.5–4.8 times lower than the reactive crystallization alternatives. These findings suggest that continuous manufacturing is not always the better choice; its viability depends importantly on whether the productivity gains offset the added separation complexity and catalyst recovery costs.

title: Low-carbon operation optimization of industrial park,integrated energy systems: A dynamic carbon emission,responsibility and cooperative game approach
affiliations: North China Electric Power University - Department of Power Engineering, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Tsinghua University and North China Electric Power University - Department of Power Engineering

detail.title: Low-carbon operation optimization of industrial park,integrated energy systems: A dynamic carbon emission,responsibility and cooperative game approach

keywords: dynamic carbon emission responsibility factors of electricity

detail.abstract: Under China's dual-carbon targets and the ongoing development of new power systems, industrial-park energy systems are shifting from fossil-fuel-based distributed supply toward low-carbon, collaborative, and flexible operation. Existing park-level planning studies often overlook three coupled challenges: redundant capacity caused by independent investment decisions among multiple factories, high storage investment when electrical storage is used to perform long-duration energy shifting, and static carbon accounting that cannot reflect time-varying grid conditions. To address these gaps, we proposes an optimization framework for an electric integrated energy system that couples a dynamic electricity carbon responsibility factor with a multi-factory cooperative game. First, an electric park topology centered on air-source heat pumps, seasonal thermal energy storage, and shared short-term storage is developed to exploit the temporal complementarity of heterogeneous factory loads. Second, a physical net-carbon tracking model based on a dynamic electricity carbon responsibility factor is introduced to distinguish the carbon responsibility of electricity purchases and sales at different times. This mechanism encourages the park to increase consumption during periods of low-carbon electricity surplus and to reduce grid purchases, or even discharge to the grid, during high-stress periods. Third, an improved Shapley-value allocation mechanism incorporating load-shifting contribution ratio (LSCR) and energy-load coupling contribution (ELCC) is formulated to quantify the marginal contributions of individual factories to flexibility provision and local renewable-energy consumption. Compared with the economic optimum, the scheme reduces dynamic-factor carbon responsibility from 10,150.31t to zero with a 30.12% cost increase, while lowering statutory static carbon emissions by 44.51%. The improved Shapley mechanism preserves budget balance and converts load shifting and renewable-consumption contributions into explicit economic compensation. The results demonstrate that the coordinated design of dynamic carbon-responsibility signals, multi-timescale storage, and cooperative cost allocation provides a temporally responsive and coalition-stable modeling framework for zero-carbon industrial parks.

title: Harnessing Convolutional Neural Intelligence for Sustainable Electricity Stewardship in Connected Built Environments: A Fourth Industrial Revolution Perspective
affiliations: Peking University

detail.title: Harnessing Convolutional Neural Intelligence for Sustainable Electricity Stewardship in Connected Built Environments: A Fourth Industrial Revolution Perspective
detail.abstract: Urbanization, electrification, and the proliferation of connected technologies are intensifying electricity demand across commercial and industrial buildings, creating an urgent need for intelligent systems that can improve energy efficiency while supporting decarbonization objectives. This study develops a convolutional deep-learning framework for forecasting building electricity consumption and identifying abnormal operational patterns through pervasive sensing and adaptive intelligence. The proposed methodology utilizes the ASHRAE Great Energy Predictor III dataset, comprising more than 60 million hourly meter observations from 1,448 buildings across 16 campuses, and integrates historical energy measurements, weather conditions, and building characteristics. The analytical workflow incorporates data cleansing, normalization, feature construction, convolutional representation learning, demand forecasting, and statistical anomaly assessment, followed by adaptive updating to maintain diagnostic reliability under changing operating conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed convolutional architecture achieves an R² of 91.7%, with MAE and RMSE values of 0.051 and 0.064, respectively, outperforming support vector regression, random forest, gated recurrent unit, bidirectional long short-term memory, and feed-forward neural models. Compared with the strongest recurrent benchmark, the proposed approach delivers approximately 76-fold higher forecasting fidelity while reducing computational latency by 67.1%, achieving inference within 1.7 seconds. Economic assessment further indicates potential annual savings of $42,600 for a representative commercial building and an estimated payback period of 14 months. The findings confirm that convolutional intelligence integrated with continuous sensing and adaptive anomaly recognition can provide a scalable pathway for predictive energy management, operational fault detection, and cost-effective decarbonization of intelligent buildings.

title: MetaMatch: A Semi-Supervised Diagnostic Model for Colorectal Cancer Based on Tongue Images with Meta-Feature Enhancement and Uncertainty-Aware Fusion
affiliations: Fuzhou University, Fuzhou University, Fuzhou University, Fuzhou University, Fuzhou University, Fuzhou University, Fuzhou University, Fuzhou University, Fuzhou University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Fuzhou University - School of Mechanical Engineering and Automation, Sun Yat-sen University (SYSU) - Department of Endoscopic Surgery and Guangdong Second Provincial General Hospital

detail.title: MetaMatch: A Semi-Supervised Diagnostic Model for Colorectal Cancer Based on Tongue Images with Meta-Feature Enhancement and Uncertainty-Aware Fusion
detail.abstract: Background: Colorectal cancer (CRC) ranks among the highest in both global incidence and mortality. Colonoscopy screening, although the gold standard, is difficult to implement at scale due to its invasiveness and low patient compliance. Tongue diagnosis in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) is non-invasive and convenient, yet inherently subjective. Deep learning-based diagnostic methods are constrained by the scarcity of high-quality labeled samples, limiting their diagnostic performance.,Methods: We propose MetaMatch, a semi-supervised diagnostic model. First, we design a meta-feature-enhanced network, MetaNet, which generates pathological semantic guidance signals from visual features and dynamically modulates convolutional features through a closed-loop mechanism of generation, evolution, and application, guiding the network to focus on subtle lesion regions. Second, we embed the FreeMatch adaptive thresholding mechanism into both MetaNet and WideResNet, enabling synergistic co-evolution between pseudo-label confidence and pathological perception, thereby forming a positive feedback loop between semi-supervised training and feature extraction. Finally, we design an Uncertainty-Aware Complementary Weighted Fusion (UACF-W) mechanism that quantifies sample uncertainty via prediction entropy and employs a three-interval adaptive decision strategy to dynamically fuse MetaNet and WideResNet.,Results: In CRC tongue image diagnosis, MetaMatch achieves a test accuracy of 83.9%, sensitivity and specificity both at 83.9%, an AUC of 91.2%, and a compact parameter count of only 6.03M.,Conclusion: MetaMatch enables accurate diagnosis with limited labeled samples, providing a feasible AI-driven solution for non-invasive, large-scale CRC screening and advancing the objectification of TCM tongue diagnosis. Prospective clinical studies are warranted to validate its translational potential.

title: Sparse Feature Selection, Not Deep Learning Capacity, Drives Spatial Transfer in Crop Classification
affiliations: The George Washington University, The George Washington University, The George Washington University, The George Washington University, George Washington University - Department of Geography and The George Washington University

detail.title: Sparse Feature Selection, Not Deep Learning Capacity, Drives Spatial Transfer in Crop Classification
detail.abstract: Crop-type maps from satellite image time series are a backbone of agricultural monitoring, yet the machine-learning models that produce them are almost always trained and tested within a single region, leaving open how they behave when deployed to new areas where no labels were collected. Using a South African Sentinel-2 dataset (optical only), we benchmark twenty-three classical and deep models under spatial transfer to a disjoint holdout tile and identify the model property that decides success: sparse, axis-aligned feature selection. Models that commit to a few features at a time, gradient-boosted trees, logistic regression, and the attentive TabNet, transfer robustly (macro-F1 0.56--0.60), whereas high-capacity dense temporal networks (CNN-BiLSTM, a Transformer encoder, L-TAE) degrade sharply; a controlled comparison shows that attention capacity is not the lever, sparsity is. We turn this insight into a method: L-TAE-S, a sparse-attention temporal encoder that ties the best model for out-of-region macro-F1 (0.60) at a fraction of the training cost, and whose field-level variant has the smallest train-to-holdout gap of any model. We further show that conventional in-region validation inverts these rankings, the dense networks that lead in-region (macro-F1 0.72--0.78) fall furthest under transfer, which is why models intended for operational crop mapping must be evaluated across regions rather than within one. Field-level aggregation is a second, substitutable robustness lever, and the most transferable models retain near-full accuracy using only a quarter of the training fields. Together these results give practitioners a concrete design principle for crop classifiers that must generalize to unlabeled farmland.​

title: Sequential Hydro-Mechanical-Thermal-Stochastic Stability of Highway Slopes Under Rainfall, Drawdown, and Seismic Loading
affiliations: National Taiwan University of Science and Technology, National Taiwan University of Science and Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Sequential Hydro-Mechanical-Thermal-Stochastic Stability of Highway Slopes Under Rainfall, Drawdown, and Seismic Loading
detail.abstract: This paper presents a sequentially coupled hydro-mechanical-thermal-stochastic stability framework for highway cut slopes under rainfall infiltration, rapid drawdown, and pseudo-static seismic loading. The fully coupled multi-physics problem is decomposed into five sequentially solvable sub-problems hydraulic, mechanical, stability, thermal, and stochastic addressed via spectral Galerkin projection, asymptotic homogenization, and polynomial chaos expansion within a staggered time-stepping scheme. Novel spectral analytical solutions are derived for pore-water pressure redistribution during rapid drawdown, extending classical consolidation theory to variably saturated conditions through the Van Genuchten–Mualem framework with suction-dependent coefficient of consolidation. Analytical predictions achieve [[EQUATION]] relative errors below 8.3% against SEEP/W numerical results, with spectral convergence demonstrated through [[EQUATION]]-mode truncation. A generalized polynomial chaos expansion ([[EQUATION]], [[EQUATION]]) propagates parametric uncertainty, enabling reliability-based design with Hasofer Lind index and Sobol sensitivity indices. Application to an I-90 Snoqualmie Pass representative slope reveals marginal initial stability ([[EQUATION]]), critical deterioration under rapid drawdown ([[EQUATION]]), and instability under seismic loading ([[EQUATION]]). Multi-objective geosynthetic reinforcement optimization identifies an optimal configuration ([[EQUATION]], [[EQUATION]], [[EQUATION]]) improving [[EQUATION]] by 57.5% at a cost-effectiveness index of [[EQUATION]] with reliability index [[EQUATION]]. The framework achieves computational speedups exceeding [[EQUATION]] compared with monolithic integration.

title: Keeper Acquisitions? A Survival Analysis of Technology Mergers
affiliations: European University Institute - Department of Law (LAW)

detail.title: Keeper Acquisitions? A Survival Analysis of Technology Mergers

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: No party funded this research.

detail.abstract: Technology mergers are frequently assessed through the lens of "killer acquisitions", whereby large firms buy targets to eliminate them as competitors. This article examines what acquirers keep instead. Using a hand-collected dataset of 364 acquisitions completed by Google, Amazon, Meta, Apple, and Microsoft between 2014 and 2024, we introduce survival analysis to the study of post-acquisition outcomes in technology mergers. We follow two dimensions of each acquisition target: the termination of its independent online presence and the tenure of its senior employees within the acquirer. Classifying every transaction as horizontal, vertical, or conglomerate, we document an inversion. Vertical targets face roughly two-and-a-half times the termination hazard of conglomerate targets, but their senior teams are retained longest. Conversely, horizontal targets persist longer in the market, but their teams disintegrate nearly twice as fast post-acquisition. Talent retention is pervasive throughout, with 86% of transactions hiring targets' senior employees, the median acquired team remaining intact for 49 months, and a third being employed as of January 2025. Overall, vertical acquisitions appear to shed targets' form but keep their substance, while the reverse holds for horizontal deals. Our findings suggest that what acquirers keep may warrant as much attention as what they kill, speaking to recent debates on merger policy reform, acquihires, and innovation-centered competition law.

title: Institutional Monetary Heteronomy as a Theoretical Framework for Officially Dollarized Economies

detail.title: Institutional Monetary Heteronomy as a Theoretical Framework for Officially Dollarized Economies
detail.abstract: Mundell's Theory of Optimum Currency Areas (OCA) provides a classical framework for assessing the feasibility of sharing a common currency. This study examines its applicability to Ecuador and El Salvador, two officially dollarized economies (ODE), and concludes that neither OCA theory nor the classical monetary theories adequately explain their macroeconomic dynamics. Using a theoreticalhermeneutic approach, it argues that an Institutional Monetary Heteronomy (IMH) model offers a more suitable conceptual framework for understanding the loss of sovereignty, structural dependency, and conditioned stability that characterize dollarized monetary systems.

title: Development of a Lean–Energy–Carbon Coupling Framework for Sustainable Manufacturing Performance Improvement in Automotive Components
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Rajabhat Rajanagarindra University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Development of a Lean–Energy–Carbon Coupling Framework for Sustainable Manufacturing Performance Improvement in Automotive Components
detail.abstract: This paper provides a quantitative Lean-Energy-Carbon coupling paradigm to simultaneously optimize production cycle time, energy usage, and carbon emissions in automobile elastomer manufacture. Unlike traditional lean implementations which have been mainly implemented for waste minimization, this research directly and measurably links process time, thermal energy consumption, and CO2 emissions at the micro-process level. The proposed Lean–Energy–Carbon Coupling Framework (LEC Framework) integrates the 3 Gen principle, Risk Priority Number (RPN) analysis, and ECRS methodology with real-time electrical measurement and carbon footprint modeling. A case study on an automotive rubber component demonstrates that mold geometry redesign and operator–machine synchronization significantly improve system performance. Experimental results show a 62.26% reduction in cycle time and a 25.8% decrease in energy consumption, corresponding to an annual reduction of 2.61 tCO2e per production line. The findings confirm that energy consumption in thermal forming processes is strongly time-dependent and that eliminating idle time produces proportional environmental benefits. This work introduces a reliable, data-driven framework integrating lean manufacturing with carbon-aware production, providing a scalable solution for SMEs migrating to sustainable and low-carbon manufacturing systems. Statistical validation using the Shapiro–Wilk test, independent-samples t-test, and Cohen’s d effect size confirmed that the observed improvements were statistically significant (p < 0.01) and operationally meaningful.

title: Meeting the Challenge of Correspondent Bank Relationship Withdrawals in fully Dollarized Microstates
affiliations: Kiffmeister Consulting

detail.title: Meeting the Challenge of Correspondent Bank Relationship Withdrawals in fully Dollarized Microstates
detail.abstract: Officially dollarized microstates surrender the monetary autonomy of an issuing central bank in exchange for the stability of a foreign currency, and in doing so make their domestic financial systems dependent on correspondent banking relationships (CBRs) that global banks are increasingly unwilling to maintain. The existing International Monetary Fund and World Bank literature treats CBR withdrawal primarily as a crossborder payments problem, and its prescriptions are addressed to that dimension. This paper argues that these remedies leave unaddressed a distinct structural vulnerability: that the domestic financial architecture of officially dollarized microstates inherently depend on CBRs. Focusing on the Federated States of Micronesia, Palau, Timor-Leste, and the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the paper examines emerging digital financial infrastructure and instruments as potential complements to the standard prescriptions, assessing their capacity to sustain domestic circulation independent of a conventional CBR, and the extent to which they may allow governments to recapture economic benefits analogous in some respects to the seigniorage that dollarization forgoes.

title: Climate-resilient Retail Lending: A Framework for Integrating Climate Risk, Sustainable Banking and Financial Innovation

detail.title: Climate-resilient Retail Lending: A Framework for Integrating Climate Risk, Sustainable Banking and Financial Innovation
detail.abstract:
Climate related financial risks are becoming increasingly material to banking institutions, with growing evidence suggesting that physical climate hazards and transition-related economic adjustments can influence borrower resilience, collateral quality and mortgage lending outcomes. While substantial progress has been made in climate-risk measurement, sustainable finance and banking regulation, comparatively limited attention has been devoted to understanding how climate-risk insights can be translated into retail lending practices and lending-product design.

This study addresses this gap by investigating the relationship between climate-related risks and mortgage lending outcomes and by examining how climate-risk information can be systematically incorporated into retail lending practices to enhance banking resilience while supporting climate adaptation and the transition towards a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy. The research develops a Climate-Resilient Retail Lending Framework that links climate-risk exposure, mortgage lending outcomes and climate-responsive lending design.

The study adopts a sequential mixed-methods approach combining theoretical synthesis, quantitative analysis and expert validation. The empirical component focuses on the U.S. mortgage market and utilises publicly available mortgage, banking, climate and socioeconomic datasets to examine whether climate-risk indicators provide explanatory value beyond conventional credit-risk determinants. Findings are subsequently translated into framework development and refined through engagement with banking practitioners, credit-risk specialists, climate-risk experts and sustainable-finance professionals.

The research contributes to climate finance and sustainable banking literature by advancing a product-level perspective on climate-risk integration. It further seeks to provide empirical evidence on the influence of climate-related risks on mortgage lending outcomes and to develop an evidence-based framework through which financial institutions can incorporate climate-related considerations into retail lending practices. In doing so, the study aims to demonstrate how retail lending can contribute simultaneously to banking resilience, climate adaptation and the transition towards a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy.

title: Development beyond Industrialization: Testing Rodrik and Hausmann with Cross-Country Data

detail.title: Development beyond Industrialization: Testing Rodrik and Hausmann with Cross-Country Data
detail.abstract: The London Consensus (LSE Press, 2025) revisits the foundations of economic policy for developing countries. Two of its chapters advance different views on how such countries grow. Dani Rodrik warns that the manufacturing-led path is closing, a process he terms "premature deindustrialization," whereas Ricardo Hausmann argues that prosperity flows from exporting an increasingly complex basket of goods. This paper examines both claims with crosscountry data. Using the GGDC/UNU-WIDER Economic Transformation Database, I find that the manufacturing employment share follows an inverted-U in income and that its peak shifts towards lower income over successive decades, a pattern consistent with premature deindustrialization. Using the economic complexity framework, I find that economic complexity is positively associated with income, reproducing Hausmann's central stylised fact. The analysis is diagnostic and associational rather than causal.

reference: ECB Working Paper No. 2026/3276
title: When the Crowd Speaks: AI-based retail investor sentiment indicator with Reddit data
affiliations: and European Central Bank (ECB)

detail.title: When the Crowd Speaks: AI-based retail investor sentiment indicator with Reddit data
detail.abstract: Retail investors increasingly discuss markets in real time on social media, yet these discussions remain difficult to measure systematically. This paper introduces the Reddit Retail Investor Sentiment Indicator (R-RISI), a high-frequency measure of retail investor sentiment based on Reddit posts from major investing and crypto-related subreddits between 2015 and April 2026. Using ChatGPT 5.1, we classify posts by sentiment and topic and show that large language models provide more accurate labels for informal social media language than widely used finance-specific models such as FinBERT, which tends to over-assign neutral sentiment. R-RISI is constructed by aggregating daily positive and negative posts, weighting them by user engagement and standardising the resulting series using a rolling one-year z-score methodology. The indicator can be flexibly built for broad asset classes, portfolios, individual securities or thematic groups, allowing sentiment to be tracked at a much higher granularity than traditional retail investor indicators. We show how sentiment and dominant discussion topics evolve over time within each of the extracted subreddits. R-RISI closely reflects major market developments and aligns with established sentiment indicators while providing higher frequency and more timely signals. Empirically, changes in R-RISI contain statistically significant short-term information for market prices. This relationship is particularly relevant during periods of market stress: changes in R-RISI matter more for next-day S&P 500 returns when markets are in decline. The indicator therefore offers a timely and granular tool for analysing retail investor behaviour and monitoring sentiment-driven market dynamics in an environment of growing retail investor participation. A regularly updated version of the indicator is available through an accompanying R-RISI online dashboard.

title: Quantum and Damages in International Commercial Arbitration: Causation, Valuation, Lost Profits and the Limits of Expert Evidence
affiliations: Senior Judicial Magistrate at Bangladesh Judicial Service

detail.title: Quantum and Damages in International Commercial Arbitration: Causation, Valuation, Lost Profits and the Limits of Expert Evidence
detail.abstract: Damages are often the point at which international commercial arbitration moves from legal principle to economic consequence. Yet quantum is frequently treated as a technical appendix to liability rather than as a distinct adjudicative exercise governed by causation, remoteness, certainty, mitigation and the compensatory principle. This article develops an integrated framework for assessing quantum in cross-border commercial disputes. It examines the relationship between legal causation and economic modelling; the selection of valuation dates and the use of post-breach information; the proof of lost profits; the appropriate use of discounted cash flow, market, asset and cost approaches; and the treatment of mitigation, avoided costs, tax, currency and interest. Particular attention is given to the role and limits of expert evidence. Drawing on the CISG, the UNIDROIT Principles, the 2026 ICC Arbitration Rules, the 2020 IBA Rules on the Taking of Evidence, and leading commercial decisions including The Golden Victory, Bunge v Nidera, Sharp v Viterra and RTI v MUR Shipping, the article argues that experts must assist rather than displace arbitral judgment. Valuation models should be transparent, assumption-driven and capable of sensitivity testing; tribunals should distinguish legal entitlement from financial measurement and should explain the chain from  breach to counterfactual, from counterfactual to loss, and from loss to monetary award. The proposed approach seeks to reconcile full compensation with evidentiary discipline, avoiding both speculative overvaluation and artificial under-compensation.

title: Evaluating Social Welfare Functions: A Unified Fifteen-Principle Framework with Islamic Perspectives — A Systematic Assessment and Empirical Application

detail.title: Evaluating Social Welfare Functions: A Unified Fifteen-Principle Framework with Islamic Perspectives — A Systematic Assessment and Empirical Application

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None declared. The author has no financial or personal relationships that could have influenced this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received.

detail.abstract: How should we aggregate individual well-being into a societal ranking that can guide policy decisions? This paper provides the first systematic evaluation of ten major social welfare functions against a unified fifteen-principle framework (seven technical and eight normative). We make three contributions: (1) a unified evaluative framework enabling systematic comparison across distinct philosophical traditions, (2) an operational nested CES Islamic SWF rooted in Al-Ghazali's tripartite hierarchy, illustrated with empirical data from 34 Indonesian provinces, and (3) a practical policy decision matrix for function selection based on policy objectives. Our analysis reveals that no single SWF satisfies all desirable properties; the choice is inescapably normative. Atkinson's SWF and Sen's income-based SWF exhibit the broadest compatibility, while the Islamic SWF offers a distinctive multidimensional alternative integrating material, spiritual, social, environmental, and intergenerational dimensions. We conclude with comprehensive mapping tables and practical guidance for policymakers.

title: When Workers are Scarce: Labor-shortage Exposure and Corporate Default Risk
affiliations: Queen Mary University of London, Northern Trust Corporation - Northern Trust Asset Management and Griffith University - Griffith Business School

detail.title: When Workers are Scarce: Labor-shortage Exposure and Corporate Default Risk
detail.abstract: We examine whether firm-level labor-shortage exposure predicts corporate default risk. Using an earnings-call-based measure of labor scarcity, we find that firms discussing labor shortages more intensively subsequently move closer to the default boundary. The effect is economically meaningful, with a one-standard-deviation increase in LBSE associated with a roughly 3-4% decline in distance-to-default. Identification tests around the 2017 tightening of U.S. immigration policy show that labor-intensive firms experience both a relative increase in LBSE and a subsequent deterioration in default risk. The result is robust to alternative exposure and default-risk measures, demanding fixed effects, macro-labor controls, Bartik 2SLS, matching, entropy balancing, placebo timing tests, and subsample analyses. Channel tests point to higher debt costs, weaker organizational capital, and lower operating performance. Overall, the evidence recasts labor scarcity as a credit-risk exposure, not merely an operating constraint.

title: The Problem of Copyright Compliance in the Music Industry of Bangladesh: An analysis
affiliations: and Southeast University

detail.title: The Problem of Copyright Compliance in the Music Industry of Bangladesh: An analysis
detail.abstract: According to the 2015 Report of International Property Rights Index, Bangladesh in terms of Intellectual Property (IP) protection stands itself at 128th out of 129 countries. Moreover, it is the Asian country with the highest copyright piracy rate. In this connection, one of the major victimized sectors is music industry where piracy rate is shockingly 96%. Availability of pirated musical works, absence of adequate incentive for musical actors and weaker legal and social structure are mainly responsible for such unhappy situation. This paper examines the reasons for this shocking situation, seeks possible alternatives from international and foreign standards and essentially provides some recommendations to improve copyright enforcement in music industry of Bangladesh.

title: The Distribution of Observational Capacity in Environmental Governance: Epistemic Position, Establishment, and the Duty to Look

detail.title: The Distribution of Observational Capacity in Environmental Governance: Epistemic Position, Establishment, and the Duty to Look
detail.abstract: The architecture developed in the earlier papers of this series presupposes throughout that parties can observe the field they govern: conditions must be characterised, changes assessed against records, couplings established, and approaching thresholds detected. This paper takes that presupposition as its subject. Observational capacity is unevenly held, its distribution follows the distribution of instruments and of operational tenure, and the international record shows warning and monitoring coverage lowest where exposure is highest. The method is conceptual and the paper's contribution is to state why this distribution is a matter of justice and not of service quality, and what follows procedurally. Four positions are developed. Observational capacity is constituted by duration and cannot be acquired at the moment of need, since establishing that a coupling obtains requires paired records spanning a multiple of the coupling's own timescale, so capacity is a stock accumulated by presence and no expenditure substitutes for the years not observed. This yields an establishment frontier whose adverse property is that the couplings requiring the longest records are those whose alteration is least reversible, so the parties least instrumented are excluded from precisely the claims that matter most. A governing principle keyed to a property that must be established, as this series' principle is, therefore allocates protection along the distribution of instruments unless something is done about it, and four asymmetries compound: over establishment, over the standards defining what counts as unusual, over the credibility accorded to accounts, and over which couplings are examined at all. The paper's constructive proposal is a duty to look, owed by parties holding capacity toward couplings their own conduct bears on, with an adverse inference available where the duty is unmet, drawing on the treatment of evidential control in the law of proof; and a set of presumptions operating where capacity is absent, so that the silence of the unobserved is not read as the safety of the unobserved. The paper surveys environmental justice, procedural rights in environmental law, epistemic injustice, community-based monitoring, indigenous data sovereignty, the sociology of undone science, and the law of evidential control, states what each owns, and identifies the residue. It reports no empirical study.

title: Trade, Power, and Resources in the New Political Economy of Energy Diplomacy and Supply Chain Resilience

detail.title: Trade, Power, and Resources in the New Political Economy of Energy Diplomacy and Supply Chain Resilience

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known personal, financial, or professional conflicts of interest that could have influenced the research, analysis, or conclusions presented in this paper. No external funding was received for this work. The author has no financial or advisory relationships with any organizations, technology companies, or government agencies that could be perceived as having influenced the study design, interpretation of findings, or policy recommendations presented herein.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve primary data collection, experiments, or interventions with human participants, patients, or animals. The research is based entirely on a structured narrative synthesis of publicly available peer-reviewed literature, international agency reports, and published statistics. Therefore, formal ethics committee approval was not required. All sources cited are properly attributed in the references.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted without external funding. The author's institutional affiliation provided access to library resources and academic databases but did not provide financial support for the research or publication.

detail.abstract: The global shift from fossil fuels toward renewable energy is not only a technical or envi ronmental project; it is reshaping the very structure of international economic power. This paper examines how the transition away from hydrocarbons is forcing states to rethink trade policy, industrial strategy, and diplomacy around a new class of strategic goods: crit ical minerals, battery components, and clean-technology hardware. Using the analytical lens of International Political Economy (IPE), the study places two rival traditions– neo mercantilism and liberal institutionalism– alongside Global Value Chain (GVC) theory to explain why supply chains that once seemed like purely commercial arrangements have become sites of geopolitical contest. The paper argues that market concentration in mining and, more importantly, in mineral processing has given a small number of states, most no tably China, a form of structural leverage that is increasingly described as the “weaponiza tion of interdependence.” It traces how policy responses in the United States and the European Union– from the Inflation Reduction Act to the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism– are reorganizing trade flows along political rather than purely comparative advantage lines, producing strategies commonly labelled friend-shoring and near-shoring. The paper also investigates the macroeconomic consequences of this fragmentation, par ticularly “greenflation,” and evaluates strategic stockpiling and diversification as resilience tools. A separate section considers how these dynamics are experienced by developing countries, which hold much of the world’s mineral wealth yet often capture the smallest share of its value, and asks what a genuinely “just” energy transition would require. The paper concludes that supply chain resilience cannot be achieved through unilateral protec tionism alone; it requires coordinated, rules-based cooperation that treats critical mineralsas a shared strategic concern rather than a zero-sum prize. Twelve original figures are used throughout to illustrate market concentration, policy timelines, and resilience frameworks, and the paper closes with a set of concrete policy recommendations for both advanced and developing economies.

detail.abstract:
This essay asks why some countries became rich while others stayed poor, and what changes when a technology, for the first time, embeds part of cognitive capacity itself in the infrastructure. It reads the classic explanations of the Great Divergence (geography, institutions, useful knowledge, fossil energy, colonialism) as components of a single mechanism, the multiplier: effective productive capacity is the capacity of the individual multiplied by the quality of the system. Technology transfers; the system that makes it productive does not. The empirical anchor is Comin and Mestieri's finding that adoption lags converge while intensity of use diverges, and that this second divergence explains about 80 per cent of the income gap since 1820. Applied to artificial intelligence, the mechanism produces two simultaneous forces: on the side of access, AI converges (it raises the productivity of less experienced workers most, and the price of inference has fallen by over 99 per cent in two years); on the side of production, it diverges (AI compute hubs exist in 32 countries, over 150 have none, and four US companies will invest 720-745 billion dollars in 2026). Which force prevails in a country depends on its multiplier: institutions, energy, skills, organisation. The final part examines Europe and Italy (productivity, energy prices, skills, adoption gap between large and small firms, Transizione 4.0 and Nuova Transizione 5.0 incentives) and closes with five verifiable conditions, each with an indicator, for a convergence that can be checked against the data of the coming years.

title: Beyond the Unemployment Rate: A Structural Labor Market Indicator
affiliations: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland

detail.title: Beyond the Unemployment Rate: A Structural Labor Market Indicator

publicationDetails.detailsText: Finance and Economics Discussion Series, issue 058, 2026[10.17016/FEDS.2026.058]

publicationDetails.journalName: Board of Governors: Finance & Economics Discussion Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: Labor market variables frequently send conflicting signals about the degree of slack or tightness, often complicating policy assessments at critical junctures. This paper develops a Structural Labor Market Indicator (SLMI) for the U.S. economy that addresses the limitations of existing univariate measures or atheoretical statistical approaches that synthesize multiple labor market indicators but cannot distinguish between supply and demand driving forces. We construct the SLMI using a medium scale New Keynesian DSGE model featuring search and matching frictions, endogenous labor force participation, and variable hours. The model is disciplined by a comprehensive dataset that includes not only labor market variables but also other macroeconomic aggregates. The SLMI synthesizes model-implied gaps across multiple labor market dimensions using principal component analysis. We show that GDP growth and inflation provide substantial information about labor market slack beyond what labor market variables contain, validating our multi-variable structural approach. Relative to alternative measures, the SLMI often provides earlier warnings of deteriorating conditions at recession onset but recovers more gradually during expansions.

title: Can Governments Really Change Retirement Saving Habits? A Comparison between Australia and New Zealand
affiliations: Formerly Co-Director, Retirement Policy & Research Centre, University of Auckland

detail.title: Can Governments Really Change Retirement Saving Habits? A Comparison between Australia and New Zealand

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: No-one funded the research.

detail.abstract: Australia's compulsory system has transformed how household wealth is packaged there: superannuation is 49% of Australian household financial assets against 11% in New Zealand. However, it has not made households wealthier, relative to their incomes: net worth is nine to ten times income in both countries, and the median New Zealand adult ranks fourth in the world for wealth, only one place behind Australia. Australian household debt has climbed to 177% of income while New Zealand's has been flat at about 125% for two decades. Once Australia's superannuation tax concessions are counted, the true fiscal gap between the two retirement systems over the long-term is roughly half what the headline superannuation numbers suggest. Poverty rates amongst the old in each country also don't establish a 'winner'. Nothing in the available data shows widespread under-saving in New Zealand. This paper suggests that making KiwiSaver compulsory can wait until the data exist to justify it. However, New Zealand does need a data-and research-led discussion about both public and private provision for retirement. We have never done that.

title: Autoencoder-based H&E stain deconvolution: a cross-domain approach with histological image segmentation and classification analyses
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Autoencoder-based H&E stain deconvolution: a cross-domain approach with histological image segmentation and classification analyses
detail.abstract: Background and Objective: Cancer diagnosis in hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) histological images relies on visual assessment by specialists, which is complex and subjective. Computational methods have been used to support histopathological analysis, especially in segmentation and classifica- tion tasks. However, color variations caused by tissue preparation, staining, and digitization protocols may affect image appearance and algorithm per- formance. This study aimed to propose and evaluate an autoencoder-based method for H&E stain deconvolution by a cross-domain estimation of con- centration maps.Methods: The proposed method was based on the Beer–Lambert opti- cal model and investigated different loss functions, skip-add connections, and training strategies for stain deconvolution. Public histological image datasets were used for quantitative evaluation, visual analysis, and downstream ex- periments involving nuclei segmentation and image classification. Structural similarity index measure (SSIM) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) were used when reference concentration maps were available.Results: In the dataset with reference concentration maps, the best val-ues achieved across the proposed configurations were SSIM and PSNR of 0.8436 and 39.4546 for hematoxylin, and 0.7530 and 35.7264 for eosin, re- spectively. Although literature methods achieved higher quantitative values on global reconstruction metrics, the proposed method generated visually interpretable maps aligned with relevant histological structures. This struc- tural and biological fidelity is critical in clinical computer-aided diagnosis, as it mitigates stain-mixing artifacts and ensures that feature extraction relies on true tissue morphology rather than pixel noise. In downstream tasks, the deconvolved HE channel input alone did not outperform RGB images in nuclei segmentation, whereas the combined RGB+HE representation was more competitive, with gains of up to 0.0130 in sensitivity. In classification, the effect of deconvolution varied according to the dataset and network. For multiclass colorectal images, the best result of the proposed method was an F1-score of 0.4164. In the binary cervical dataset, the proposed method with RGB+HE input achieved an F1-score of 0.9888 and an AUC of 0.9988.Conclusions: Autoencoder-based H&E stain deconvolution is a promis- ing strategy for generating complementary representations to RGB images in histopathological analysis. However, limitations remain regarding the se- lective separation of hematoxylin, eosin, and background, which motivates future works.

title: Length-of-stay prediction using physician latent traits
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Length-of-stay prediction using physician latent traits
detail.abstract: Background and Objective: Variation in length of stay (LoS) across physicians is documented in the multilevel-modelling literature, but that literature is explanatory. In prediction models the physician identifier is routinely dropped because of missingness and high cardinality. In public EHRs the physician exists only as a de-identified identifier with no observed attributes, leaving nothing from which to build a feature.Methods: We used 294,701 admissions from MIMIC-IV v3.1 (148,239 patients, 1,807 physicians), restricted to information available at admission; diagnosis codes, assigned at discharge, were excluded as leakage. Cyclic dual latent discovery (CDLD) found a 64-dimensional latent trait for each physician from interaction records alone, combined with 54 patient features, and assessed by five-fold cross-validation with fold-paired t-tests. As comparators we added the physician's historical mean LoS (raw and empirical-Bayes shrunk) and case volume as single columns.Results: The historical mean alone reached RMSE 4.302 days (R² 0.085), below the 54-feature patient model (4.387 days, R² 0.048). Adding physician latent traits gave 4.270 days (R² 0.098), improving on patient features alone by 0.117 days (p<0.0001). Of that improvement, 0.090 days (77%) was reproduced by the single mean column; latent traits added 0.027 days (23%; p<0.001, all five folds). Shuffle and stratification analyses showed that latent discovery depended primarily on records per entity.Conclusions: Physicians with no observed attributes can be represented from interaction records and contribute to LoS prediction. Patients, whose records are sparse, could not, which supports the asymmetric design. Whether the gain translates into operational benefit was not evaluated.

title: The Cost of being Different: Name Rarity and Analyst Research
affiliations: , College of Management and Economics and China Center for Social Computing and Analytics and Tianjin University

detail.title: The Cost of being Different: Name Rarity and Analyst Research
detail.abstract: We examine whether the rarity of an analyst's given name, a stable attribute of personal identity, is associated with how analysts produce research and how their research is received by market participants. Using nationwide frequencies covering approximately 1.2 billion Chinese citizens, we measure the rarity of the characters in each analyst's given name. Analysts with rarer names issue forecasts that depart farther from consensus, and these departures are more informative. Their reports draw on scarcer information sources, and their coverage portfolios are more focused. Yet this differentiated research receives weaker recognition: rare-name analysts obtain less management access, are less likely to attain star status, and elicit smaller short-window reactions to favorable recommendations. Those recommendations subsequently earn higher risk-adjusted returns over the following one to three months. Together, the findings reveal a wedge between production and recognition. The identity associated with differentiated information production also shapes the access, professional evaluation, and market attention that determine how quickly that information is incorporated.

title: Characterizing the Conditional Pricing Kernel: A New Approach
