title:
When the Middle Class Undermines Progress: 
The Political Economy of AI Regulation
affiliations: Copenhagen Business School and University of Chicago - Harris School of Public Policy

detail.title:
When the Middle Class Undermines Progress: 
The Political Economy of AI Regulation
detail.abstract: The classic literature argues that a large middle class is a prerequisite for economic development. Is this true when AI progress threatens to disrupt the labor market? On the one hand, uncertainty about the consequences can impede the passage of AI-friendly regulation: voters fear the prospect of losing when the uncertainty is resolved. On the other, granular information about reform consequences may reduce political support as well. In our model, a larger middle class hampers reform, compensatory redistribution is most politically effective when its welfare justification is weakest, and AI regulatory sandboxes encounter resistance because new information undermines reform coalitions.

title:
Stakeholder Management in Publicly Listed Professional Sports Clubs: 

A Comparative Case Study of Manchester United, Borussia Dortmund, and Juventus

detail.title:
Stakeholder Management in Publicly Listed Professional Sports Clubs: 

A Comparative Case Study of Manchester United, Borussia Dortmund, and Juventus
detail.abstract:
Publicly listed professional sports clubs operate in complex stakeholder environments where sporting performance, financial objectives, regulatory obligations, commercial interests, and supporter expectations must be managed simultaneously. This study examines stakeholder management in project-based activities within publicly listed professional sports clubs and explores how stakeholder complexity influences organisational and project outcomes.

A qualitative multiple-case study approach was adopted, focusing on Manchester United plc, Borussia Dortmund, and Juventus Football Club. Publicly available secondary data, including annual reports, sustainability reports, and official club publications covering the period from 2021 to 2025, were examined through documentary analysis. A total of 433 pieces of evidence were collected, coded, categorised, and analysed using thematic analysis.

The findings identified six major themes: stakeholder engagement and relationship management; human capital and sporting development; community and social responsibility; corporate governance and accountability; commercial sustainability and strategic partnerships; and innovation and digital transformation. Stakeholder engagement and relationship management emerged as the dominant theme, highlighting the importance of fans, employees, sponsors, communities, shareholders, and other stakeholder groups in club activities. The comparative analysis indicates that the three clubs seek to balance sporting objectives with commercial, governance, and social responsibilities, although differences exist in the intensity and approaches to stakeholder engagement and disclosure.

The study concludes that effective stakeholder identification, mapping, engagement, governance, and human capital management are important for managing stakeholder complexity in publicly listed sports clubs. The findings contribute to the limited literature examining stakeholder management specifically within project-based activities of publicly traded professional sports organisations.

title: Forty-Six Years of Unverifiable Alpha: The Track-Record Verification Problem in Quantitative Finance — Its Literature, Its Cost, and Its Closure in Zero Knowledge

detail.title: Forty-Six Years of Unverifiable Alpha: The Track-Record Verification Problem in Quantitative Finance — Its Literature, Its Cost, and Its Closure in Zero Knowledge

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder and sole owner of Mizan Verification, Inc., which develops the verification system and authored the open standard (VTR-1) discussed in Sections 6–8 of this paper. The author therefore has a direct commercial interest in the problem surveyed here being regarded as solved. This conflict is also disclosed prominently within the paper itself; Sections 2–5 rest entirely on the published literature and can be evaluated independently of it.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study involves no human participants, patient data, or personal data; it is a literature survey and mechanism description based entirely on published sources and publicly verifiable computational artifacts.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was self-funded by the author through Mizan Verification, Inc.

detail.abstract: For forty-six years, a single structural problem has governed how capital is allocated to systematic strategies: a trading track record cannot be verified without inspecting the research that produced it, while the research cannot be disclosed without destroying its value. This paper surveys the literature of that problem across three strands — the economic impossibility result (Grossman and Stiglitz, 1980), the statistical machinery of multiple-testing correction, whose decisive input was never checkable (White, 2000; Hansen, 2005; Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado and Zhu, 2014; Harvey, Liu and Zhu, 2016), and the empirical evidence that self-reported performance systematically bends toward its reporters' incentives (Getmansky, Lo and Makarov, 2004; Bollen and Pool, 2009; Agarwal, Daniel and Naik, 2011). We propose a taxonomy separating the field's unsolvable constraints (non-stationarity, capacity, crowding) from its solvable institutional failures, and argue that the verification deadlock is the largest member of the solvable class: the root failure from which backtest overfitting's persistence, reporting distortion, and pedigree-based allocation each descend. We derive an order-of-magnitude cost estimate, explain structurally why five decades of remedial mechanisms — audit, process standards, platform custody, databases, and disclosure under NDA — each failed, and show that disclosure-based verification adversely selects against genuine skill. Finally, we describe the closure: zero-knowledge proof systems now permit the full evaluation of a track record — returns, costs, out-of-sample behaviour, and the number of strategies tried, committed as the leaf count of a Merkle tree fixed before evaluation — to be verified by anyone without the strategy being revealed. We summarize the mechanism (Muavia, 2026b), the open standard built on it (VTR-1; Muavia, 2026a), and the production evidence, including published refusals of celebrated return streams and the first pre-registered, cryptographically chained live track record. Limitations and open boundaries are stated.

title: Why Risk-based Premiums will not Close the Catastrophe Protection Gap: Conventional Pricing, Reinsurance Capacity, and Public Scheme Design

detail.title: Why Risk-based Premiums will not Close the Catastrophe Protection Gap: Conventional Pricing, Reinsurance Capacity, and Public Scheme Design
detail.abstract: Only about one-fifth to one-quarter of the economic losses caused by natural catastrophes in the European Union are insured, and the gap is widening as climate-related losses grow. EIOPA and the ECB have proposed an EU-level scheme combining a public-private reinsurance pool, funded by risk-based premiums, with a public disaster fund. This paper asks whether risk-based pricing at a public layer can close a gap that risk-based pricing at the private layer has not. The capital-market-imperfections account of catastrophe insurance failure presupposes a knowable loss distribution; climate non-stationarity removes that condition, and catastrophe pricing is better understood as conventional valuation under fundamental uncertainty. A five-equation model of conventional pricing, with a demand side, makes reinsurance capacity endogenously cyclical and generates a rationing ratchet whose threshold is derived analytically and verified by simulation: prices soften within a few periods of a market break while attachment points and terms do not, and once climate-driven model revisions recur faster than underwriting structure unwinds, the insured share falls persistently. Simulated coverage is fifteen points lower under conventional pricing with drifting losses than under a constant-load benchmark, and the model reproduces the documented moments of the 2022-2026 cycle. Drawing on the French and Spanish schemes, the paper sets out the design features a workable public layer requires: solidarity pricing, an explicit public tail guarantee, and countercyclical funding.

title: Routing and Distributed Inquiry in Environmental Governance: Delivering Reports under an Incomplete Structure

detail.title: Routing and Distributed Inquiry in Environmental Governance: Delivering Reports under an Incomplete Structure
detail.abstract: The event layer developed earlier in this series leaves two questions open by design. An emitting party names the parties it believes a change affects, and that naming is a revisable claim and not a routing instruction, so an arrangement must complete the delivery; and a report asserts consequence without prescribing a response, so an arrangement must have some means of doing more than delivering when more is warranted. This paper takes up both. The method is conceptual, with one small quantitative observation. On routing, the paper distinguishes three modes by what each requires and what each costs: delivery to parties the emitter declared, delivery along correspondences established from paired records, and delivery inferred from structural adjacency where no correspondence has been established. The modes trade reach against precision, and the paper's central observation is that the trade is not symmetric: because the physical structure of a field is incomplete in every party's hands, reach can be bought only by delivering to parties for whom the report is irrelevant, and the marginal volume required per additional coupling reached rises steeply, while the cost of that volume falls on receivers as the habituation that the event layer identifies as its characteristic decay mode. Routing breadth is therefore a governed parameter trading blindness against habituation, and neither end of its range is safe. On inquiry, the paper proposes a bounded, question-relative process that an arrangement may open when a report warrants more than attention, which tasks observation under the duty to look, assembles the holdings that bear on the question with disagreement preserved, and terminates in an action, a finding that the material does not warrant one, or a determination of what could not be established. The paper argues that inquiry has an epistemic function beyond the question it answers, since an inquiry that establishes a coupling adds it to the carriage map, so an arrangement learns its own structure from the inquiries it runs. The paper treats strategic silence and the corruption of routing observables inside the design and not as afterthoughts, surveys the literatures on information routing, on regulatory escalation, and on inquiry design, and identifies the residue. It reports no empirical study.

title: Generativity, Attribution and Ownership in Environmental Governance: The Enabling Contribution and What It Is Owed

detail.title: Generativity, Attribution and Ownership in Environmental Governance: The Enabling Contribution and What It Is Owed
detail.abstract: A distributed governance arrangement of the kind this series develops generates findings through a chain: records are maintained, provenance and registers are kept, changes are reported and conjectures accumulated, holdings are assembled and inquiries run, and derived artefacts result. This paper asks how contribution to such a chain should be attributed and what an owner of a derived artefact may do with it. The method is conceptual. The paper's first position is that the costs and the attribution run in opposite directions along the chain. Cost falls at the beginning, on observation sustained through periods in which nothing is found, on provenance kept by each handler, and on the recording of determinations that nothing could be established; attribution accrues at the end, to the party that made the finding. The paper names the neglected class the enabling contribution, and argues that its neglect is structural and not an oversight, since an enabling contribution is identified only in retrospect and only by the finding it enabled, so no procedure operating at the time of the contribution can recognise it. The second position is that proportional attribution is unavailable here for a reason that does not turn on measurement difficulty. Apportionment schemes require a defined set of alternative combinations against which a contribution's marginal value is assessed, and for a fifty-year record the relevant counterfactual is not a coalition of parties without one member but a different history, which no apportionment defines. The paper therefore declines shares and proposes that attribution record the chain and not divide it, with the specific requirement that the chain include what was maintained through periods without findings and what was determined to be unestablishable. The third position concerns ownership. Because a derived artefact is generated from a commons whose loss is irreversible, the governing question is not who owns the artefact but what an owner may do with it, and the paper argues that enclosure of a derived artefact is an alteration of a governed condition attracting the burden that this series' principle imposes, so the owner's rights are bounded by what their exercise forecloses. The paper surveys authorship and credit practice, apportionment theory, intellectual property and its exceptions, data attribution standards, and commons-based provision, states what each owns, and identifies the residue.

title: Stretch-Pseudo-invariant Constitutive Artificial Neural Networks: Poynting-Aware Model Discovery under Simple Shear
affiliations: Universidade do Estado do Rio de Janeiro, Universidade do Estado do Rio de Janeiro, Universidade do Estado do Rio de Janeiro, Universidade do Estado do Rio de Janeiro and Universidade Federal Fluminense

detail.title: Stretch-Pseudo-invariant Constitutive Artificial Neural Networks: Poynting-Aware Model Discovery under Simple Shear
detail.abstract: Simple shear is a fundamental deformation mode for characterizing soft materials; however, invariant-based hyperelastic models exhibit an inherent invariant degeneracy in simple shear, where $I_1=I_2$, preventing the unique identification of individual invariant contributions from shear stress data alone. Moreover, conventional invariant-based formulations may struggle to reproduce reverse Poynting effects, characterized by positive normal stresses, observed in isotropic and anisotropic soft materials. To address these limitations, this work extends principal-stretch-based constitutive model discovery through a mixed stretch-pseudo-invariant Constitutive Artificial Neural Network (CANN) framework. Although motivated by the constitutive challenges revealed under simple shear, the proposed representation is formulated in terms of general deformation measures and is not restricted to this loading mode. By incorporating shear and normal stress data simultaneously into a physics-informed loss function, the proposed framework exploits the coupling between shear deformation and normal stress generation to provide additional constitutive information otherwise inaccessible from shear stress data alone. The isotropic branch employs symmetric principal-stretch metrics, while the anisotropic branch combines orientation-modulated stretch features with the pseudo-invariants $I_4$ and $I_5$, and introduces custom square-root activation functions to represent lower-order stiffness-softening responses while avoiding numerical stiffness. Thermodynamic consistency, $C^1$-continuity, and zero residual stress at the reference state are enforced by construction. To promote parsimony and interpretability, $L_1$-regularization combined with threshold-based hard pruning eliminates unexcited kinematic pathways, yielding compact symbolic strain energy density functions. The framework is validated against experimental data for unreinforced elastomers and unidirectional fiber-reinforced composites with fiber orientations of $0^\circ$, $45^\circ$, and $90^\circ$. The proposed CANN outperforms the considered invariant-based CANN baselines, accurately capturing both classical and reverse Poynting effects, as well as complex off-axis fiber interactions, while discovering compact and physically interpretable constitutive equations.

title: Adaptive Resampling for Physics-Informed Neural Networks Using a Spring-Based Node-Moving Method
affiliations: Utrecht University, Utrecht University, Utrecht University, South China University of Technology, Utrecht University and Utrecht University

detail.title: Adaptive Resampling for Physics-Informed Neural Networks Using a Spring-Based Node-Moving Method
detail.abstract: Partial differential equations (PDEs) are central to modelling physical systems, but their numerical solution can be computationally expensive. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are a mesh-free method that embed the governing PDEs into the training loss, yet their accuracy depends strongly on the placement of collocation points. We introduce a spring-based node-moving PINN (sn-PINN) that adaptively redistributes a fixed set of collocation points during training, thereby avoiding the increased computational costs compared to other adaptive refinement strategies. At selected intervals, PDE residuals define local spring stiffnesses in a virtual spring system, whose equilibrium relocates points toward regions where the PDE is harder to satisfy. The method is evaluated on one- and two-dimensional steady-state benchmark PDEs and compared with static and random-resampling PINNs. For problems with steep gradients, sn-PINN consistently improves accuracy, reducing the relative L​2 error by up to approximately one order of magnitude compared with the baselines. These results show that residual-driven node movement is an effective fixed-budget adaptive strategy for PINNs, especially for one-dimensional problems with steep gradient, which could be extended to higher-dimensional cases with complex steep-gradient patterns.

title: Microplastic and metal coupling in a semi-arid reservoir (Presa de Boca), Mexico: baseline evidence from water chemistry and surface elemental signatures
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Microplastic and metal coupling in a semi-arid reservoir (Presa de Boca), Mexico: baseline evidence from water chemistry and surface elemental signatures
detail.abstract: Reservoirs in semi-arid regions are increasingly exposed to complex mixtures of anthropogenic contaminants, yet key knowledge gaps persist regarding the distribution of microplastic-like particles (MPs), their interactions with dissolved metals, and their potential role as contaminant vector. To address these gaps, we conducted an integrated investigation of MPs and metals in surface water samples of Presa de la Boca, Monterrey, a key recreational and freshwater reservoir in northern Mexico. MP abundance ranged from 4–66 particles L⁻¹, yielding overall pollution load index (PLI) > 1, which indicate high pollution intensity across the reservoir. MP abundance exhibited a clear spatial gradient, with elevated concentrations at urban shoreline sites, reduced levels in mid-lake zones, and secondary accumulation at distal locations driven by in-reservoir transport. MPs were dominated by fragments, with smaller sized MPs (20-100 µm) categorising them as high-impact morphotypes, respectively. Dissolved metals, including aluminium, iron, manganese, zinc, copper, nickel, arsenic, and barium, were quantified using Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectroscopy. To explore whether MPs act as reactive carriers, isolated plastic like particles were further examined using Scanning Electron Microscopy coupled with Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy, revealing pronounced surface weathering and the consistent presence of aluminium, iron, calcium, magnesium, and trace lead adhered to MP surfaces. These observations suggest potential surface association between environmentally weathered particles and dissolved or suspended metal species within the reservoir. The study provides baseline evidence on the co-occurrence of MPs and metals in a semi-arid Mexican freshwater system and highlights the need for future polymer-confirmation and adsorption-based investigations to better understand MP–metal interactions in freshwater environments.

title: The strategic use of IPO withdrawals
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Gothenburg - Department of Business Administration, , affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Gothenburg - Centre for Finance - School of Business, Economics and Law

detail.title: The strategic use of IPO withdrawals
detail.abstract: This paper examines IPO withdrawals as strategic decisions rather than failed offerings. We argue that the IPO process generates costly and credible information about firm value that can be leveraged across alternative exit channels, particularly mergers and acquisitions. Using a comprehensive sample of IPO filings, we show that withdrawal probability is about 6.9 percentage points higher for firms backed by venture capital investors, consistent with these owners treating the IPO as a real option rather than a commitment to public ownership. We further show that a larger valuation wedge between IPO-implied prices and firms’ continuation values increases the likelihood of becoming an acquisition target following an IPO attempt. A real-option-based valuation framework yields consistent results, underscoring the role of exit flexibility. These effects imply economically meaningful increases in acquisition probability, ranging from 11% to 30% relative to the unconditional likelihood of becoming a target. We further address potential endogeneity concerns by examining common determinants of IPO withdrawal and acquisition target status, as well as whether acquisition-prone firms systematically attract VC ownership, and find that these alternative explanations do not drive our main results. Together, our findings highlight the informational and option value of the IPO process and the interdependence of public and private exit routes.

title: Designing digital talent ecosystems through micro-credentials: the case of Campus IL
affiliations: Rajagiri Business School

detail.title: Designing digital talent ecosystems through micro-credentials: the case of Campus IL
detail.abstract: The accelerating pace of digital transformation has driven organizations to increasingly seek professional learning mechanisms that can be integrated with routine work responsibilities and accessed independently of spatial and temporal constraints. Micro-credentials have gained prominence as modular, digitally mediated mechanisms for recognizing discrete competencies, signalling a broader transformation in lifelong learning and workforce capability development. Using a two-stage exploratory qualitative design, this study first explores how micro-credentials are structured within a national platform to support K–12 teachers’ professional development, followed by an examination of the factors that shape user experiences of the resulting learning ecosystem. The first phase employs an exploratory single-case study to examine Campus-IL’s micro-credential ecosystem. Guided by the principles of grounded theory, the second phase employs Gioia methodology to explore the user perspectives of 14 K–12 teachers who completed micro-credential courses for professional development. The first phase identifies a five-stage double-looped capability development model comprising: Learning, Planning, Doing and Documentation, Reflection, and Peer Evaluation. The second phase identifies four dimensions shaping users’ experiences: work–family domain interference, digital disengagement, limited management support, and design discrepancies. Together, the findings provide an exploratory understanding of how a platform-based micro-credential ecosystem is structured and experienced in supporting digitally enabled pathways for lifelong learning, quality education, and continuous workforce capability development, with relevance to SDG 4 and SDG 8.

title: Responsibility for Environmental Critical Transitions: Attributing the Approach in Place of the Crossing

detail.title: Responsibility for Environmental Critical Transitions: Attributing the Approach in Place of the Crossing
detail.abstract: Environmental harm following a critical transition presents a responsibility problem that ordinary causal doctrine handles badly. Many parties contributed forcing over decades; the transition occurred at a threshold whose crossing no party's contribution was sufficient to produce and which each party's contribution was necessary to; the harm manifested later; and the crossing itself was ordinarily not observed at the time. This paper proposes a relocation of the causal question. The method is conceptual and doctrinal. Its scope is deliberately narrow: the general difficulties of apportionment in distributed generative systems are treated in separate work and are not re-argued here, and the paper confines itself to what is specific to environmental transitions. The central claim is that causation of the crossing is not apportionable while causation of the approach is, and that responsibility should therefore attach to a party's contribution to the approach and not to its contribution to the transition. The ground is structural: at a threshold each contribution is necessary and none is sufficient, which is the configuration in which shares are undefined, whereas cumulative forcing toward the threshold is additive and admits shares by construction. Relocating the question to the approach makes the tractable quantity the object of the doctrine, and the paper argues this is what the leading proportional-contribution litigation has in substance already done, in affirming a principle of proportional liability for contribution to a global forcing while failing on the facts of the particular exposure. Three further results are developed. The relocation converts responsibility into a quantity over rates, which connects it to the differential treatment developed earlier in this series and makes the relevant evidence the record of a party's forcing over time. It supplies a determinate join to the supervisory duties treated in a companion paper, since a breach of an epistemic duty is evidence of a kind courts already receive and does not require the attribution the conduct-keyed regime was adopted to avoid. And it locates the discovery and limitation difficulty precisely, since a crossing established years after it occurred, by estimates a companion paper shows to be biased toward reporting stability, gives defendants an honest ignorance defence that the epistemic duties are the appropriate answer to. The paper surveys attribution science, the doctrines of necessity and sufficiency, proportional and market-share liability, and the climate litigation record.

title: Development of Thermo-Mechanical Separable Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Its Verification against Four Benchmark Problems
affiliations: Seoul National University and Seoul National University

detail.title: Development of Thermo-Mechanical Separable Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Its Verification against Four Benchmark Problems
detail.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) provide mesh-free approximations of partial differential equation solutions, yet coupled thermo-mechanical problems remain challenging because dense multidimensional residual evaluation, constitutive enforcement, and material interfaces create a demanding multi-objective optimization problem. This study develops a thermo-mechanical separable physics-informed neural network (TM-SPINN) and systematically verifies it against four analytical benchmarks. The framework combines coordinate-wise low-rank representations, sequential thermal-to-mechanical learning, layer-wise domain decomposition, and unit-mean residual-based attention. The benchmarks comprise a pressurized hollow cylinder, a homogeneous heated hollow cylinder, a heated multilayer hollow cylinder, and a infinite line heat source in an elastic medium, thereby examining pure mechanical equilibrium, homogeneous thermoelasticity, material-interface continuity, and localized transient thermoelasticity. Accuracy is assessed using field contours and radial profiles, relative L2 errors, and R2 scores. TM-SPINN reproduces the analytical solutions with close quantitative agreement across the benchmark suite: relative L² errors range from 1.10 × 10⁻⁴ to 6.35 × 10⁻², and all reported R² scores range from 0.9930 to 1.0000. These results demonstrate that the proposed formulation accurately reproduces the four benchmark classes considered, including heterogeneous interfaces and localized transient heating.

title: Cross-View Persistence-Guided Regional Feature Refinement for Vehicle Re-Identification
affiliations: Longyan University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Longyan University

detail.title: Cross-View Persistence-Guided Regional Feature Refinement for Vehicle Re-Identification
detail.abstract: Vehicle re-identification (ReID) depends on local cues whose visibility changes across cameras. Dense features remain sensitive to occlusion, reflection, and global pooling. This study presents Many-to-Many Adaptive Region Correspondence for Vehicle Re-Identification (MARC-VeID), a single-backbone method for persistence-guided regional refinement. The model retains the DINOv3-pretrained ConvNeXt-Base through Stage 3 and removes Stage 4 to preserve spatial detail. Adaptive Identity Region Refinement (AIRR) discovers overlapping soft regions and forms regional tokens. It assigns an image-conditioned weight to each token and writes the weighted evidence back through a zero-initialized residual path. During training, Many-to-Many Cross-View Region Correspondence (MCRC) aggregates regional support across same-identity images. It provides a detached cross-view target and a weighted regional contrastive loss. MCRC is removed at inference. The deployed network outputs one normalized 512-dimensional descriptor. MARC-VeID reaches 88.7% mAP and 98.1% Rank-1 on VeRi-776 with 60.4 M parameters, 13.4 GFLOPs, and 73 FPS. It also improves a matched baseline on VeRi-Wild, VehicleID, and all evaluated cross-dataset transfer directions. Controlled ablations support regional refinement, target detachment, regional contrast, and Top-2 partner aggregation.

title: Volatility and Drawdown
affiliations: Diaman Partners Ltd

detail.title: Volatility and Drawdown
detail.abstract: Once drift and horizon are fixed, drawdown is a near-deterministic function of volatility rather than a risk measure independent of it. For a Brownian motion with drift µ and volatility σ, three exact relations hold. The current drawdown converges to an exponential law with mean σ 2/2µ, hence quadratic in σ at fixed drift. The maximum drawdown over a horizon T equals √ π/2 σ √ T at zero drift and grows as (σ 2/µ) 0.635 + ln(µ √ T/σ) at positive drift. Both are special cases of a single universal function, E[MDDT] = σ √ T G(S √ T), where S = µ/σ is the Sharpe ratio. At constant Sharpe the expected drawdown is exactly linear in σ. I compute G in exact form through the spectral expansion of the first-passage time of the drawdown process, and validate it against Monte Carlo to better than 0.11% after a continuity correction. Empirically I use 56 series: 34 US single stocks that have been in the S&P 500 continuously since its creation in March 1957 and are still listed, US total-return equities since 1885, gold since 1971, and eighteen crypto-assets since 2010. These give 15,101 non-overlapping windows whose realised volatility spans a factor of 113, from 3.7% to 416% per annum. The regression of ln MDD on ln(σˆ √ T) gives a slope of 1.06 (R 2 = 0.77) over realised drawdowns covering nearly three orders of magnitude, and 1.08–1.14 horizon by horizon. Rescaled by σˆ √ T, every series collapses onto the theoretical curve G. The single-stock block changes one conclusion. The ratio of realised to simulated drawdown under the Brownian null is 0.87 for single stocks and flat across horizons, against 0.98 for equity indices rising to 1.18 at five years. Conditional on realised volatility, single-stock drawdowns are never fatter-tailed than Gaussian: 0.1% of windows exceed the simulated 95th percentile at every horizon. For indices the excess appears at five years, where 10.4% do. The constant-volatility model misses a market-wide regime effect; it does not miss an idiosyncratic one. A dedicated section tests the model on Bitcoin, using the 200-week rolling volatility as the ex-ante input. Realised cycle drawdowns have fallen from 85% to 53% while cycleaverage σ200w has fallen from 113% to 56% (47.9% at the latest reading); normalised by σ200w √ T the four halving cycles collapse into a ±20% band. The model’s median forecast of the two-year forward drawdown is accurate to 3%. Applied to the cycle now in progress, and conditional on the 53% already realised, it puts the full-cycle drawdown at 56–64% and the probability of breaking the June 2026 low at 29–66%, depending on the drift assumed for the remainder.

title: Merger-enabled Innovation and Upward Pricing Pressure: A Local Theory-of-Benefit Test
affiliations: Econic Partners,  and University of Bergamo

detail.title: Merger-enabled Innovation and Upward Pricing Pressure: A Local Theory-of-Benefit Test
detail.abstract: Merger review often quantifies unilateral pricing incentives while treating claimed innovation efficiencies as exogenous. We develop a local theory-of-benefit test for horizontal mergers said to enable process innovation. The test separates benefit generation from benefit transmission. A project is merger-enabled only if the transaction raises its expected operating return above implementation cost while realistic less restrictive arrangements do not. The resulting product-level efficiency vector then enters benefit-adjusted upward pricing pressure for each merging product. Common ownership does not create a direct investment incentive when an investment only lowers the investor's own cost and that benefit was already internalized. Moreover, efficiencies on products receiving diverted demand can strengthen the incentive to raise another product's price, so aggregate savings are not sufficient. We extend the framework to uncertainty, multiproduct ownership, demand-enhancing innovation, and local price-investment feedback. The method provides an implementable first screen based on pre-merger quantities, margins, diversion, pass-through, and contemporaneous project evidence.

title: Big Push Toward Big Data
affiliations: Tsinghua University - Tsinghua University School of Economics and Management, Tsinghua University - Institute of Economics and Tsinghua University - School of Economics & Management

detail.title: Big Push Toward Big Data
detail.abstract: Economic activity generates data, those data improve forecasts, and better forecasts raise activity. Individual firms' data-processing decisions can also respond to economic activity and the behavior of other firms. This paper studies when these feedbacks become a macroeconomic data flywheel. Firms learn about persistent demand from raw data generated by economy-wide activity or by their own operations, and they choose how effectively to convert those data into usable signals. We show that multiple steady states can exist and that the economy can become stuck in a low-production, low-data trap. A Big Push policy supplies public signals at a labor cost and has state-dependent crowd-in and crowd-out effects. Provision crowds in private activity when endogenous information is scarce but crowds it out once information is abundant. A permanent push can eliminate the low-data state while drawing productive labor away from the surviving high-data state. A temporary push of sufficient strength and duration can lead the economy out of the low-data trap.

title: How Government Subsidies Shape Export Performance in the BRIC Countries: A Firm-Level Transmission Framework
affiliations: Lipscomb University, Florida Gulf Coast University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: How Government Subsidies Shape Export Performance in the BRIC Countries: A Firm-Level Transmission Framework
detail.abstract: Government subsidies have become prominent instruments of industrial policy, yet limited attention has been devoted to the firm-level processes through which such support translates into international competitiveness. Drawing on strategic trade theory and institutional theory, we develop a multidimensional transmission framework linking government subsidies with export performance through R&D capability, technological innovation, and willingness to export. We examine the proposed relationships using five years of firm-level data from 140 manufacturing firms in Brazil, Russia, India, and China. Structural equation modeling and path analysis support all seven hypothesized relationships: subsidies are positively associated with the three organizational mechanisms, R&D capability is positively associated with technological innovation, and each mechanism is positively associated with export performance. The findings provide initial evidence consistent with multiple firm-level transmission pathways through which industrial-policy support may contribute to international competitiveness and extend international business research on the organizational consequences of industrial policy.

title: Disaster Image Classification Using CNN Transfer Learning with Weighted-Strata Grey Wolf Optimizer and Representation by Arithmetic Programming
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Disaster Image Classification Using CNN Transfer Learning with Weighted-Strata Grey Wolf Optimizer and Representation by Arithmetic Programming
detail.abstract: Automatic disaster image classification is capable of increasing the speed of emergency response. However, high-dimensional features generated by convolutional neural networks (CNN) often contain redundant information that reduces efficiency and accuracy of classification. Most previous studies have depended on metaheuristic algorithms to select features without constructing ones and applied uniform optimization across dimensions which makes the search prone to premature convergence. Therefore, this study proposes a framework that combines CNN transfer learning with the Weighted-Strata Grey Wolf Optimizer (WS-GWO) for feature selection and Representation by Arithmetic Programming (RAP) for synthetic feature construction. The WS-GWO was used to divide the solution space into dimensional strata to ensure stability while RAP formed representations through arithmetic operations on Group 1 and Group 2 features. The Comprehensive Disaster Dataset (CDD) containing 13,557 images across six disaster classes was used. The results showed that ConvNeXt-Base achieved the highest validation accuracy of 96.28% among the 29 backbone architectures tested and was selected as the feature extractor. The proposed framework achieved an accuracy of 96.39%, an increase of 0.38 percentage points compared with the unoptimized features, and recorded the highest accuracy among the eight benchmark swarm algorithms in Scenario E. The scenario that combined all original features with both sets of arithmetic representations also proved to be optimal with an average accuracy of 96.26% and the smallest standard deviation of 0.11%. These results demonstrate that the combination of feature selection and construction based on dimensional stratification could improve both the accuracy and stability of disaster image classification.

title: Climate Policy Uncertainty and Industrial Transition Risk: A Time-Frequency Spillover and Resilience Network Analysis in China
affiliations: Peking University

detail.title: Climate Policy Uncertainty and Industrial Transition Risk: A Time-Frequency Spillover and Resilience Network Analysis in China
detail.abstract: This research builds a comprehensive contagion network to examine the temporal relationships between climate policy uncertainty in China and the risk of climate transition in China's industries using complex network theory and time-frequency spillover approaches. To determine the transfer of risks across industries, we analyze daily time series data from national carbon trading markets, stock indexes of China's financial sector, and macro-level climate policy uncertainty indicators. By gauging their resilience using two metrics—absorption intensity and absorption duration—we also examine the persistence of industrial climate transition risks after external policy shocks.According to real-world statistics, long-term structural risk spillovers, rather than short-term market noise, are the primary drivers of the total risk spillover impact, and these effects might vary over time. The majority of net risk consumers are carbon-intensive sectors that rely on conventional energy sources. Nevertheless, uncertainties surrounding climate policy provide a significant threat that greatly affects the risks associated with industrial shifts. While hazards were consistent across industries, actual resilience capacity varied. Such variations occurred as a result of differences in legislative limitations, adaptation costs, and operational flexibility. At last, our research provides crucial intellectual support and strategic guidance to climate politicians, authorities in the financial markets, and corporate leaders. This will allow them to successfully navigate systemic transition shocks and ensure a strong green and low-carbon shift.

title: Spatial–spectral transformer regression improves soil organic carbon estimation from fused VNIR–SWIR hyperspectral imaging
affiliations: Griffith University, Griffith University, Griffith University, Griffith University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Griffith University, Griffith University, Griffith University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Southern Mindanao, University of Queensland, Griffith University and Griffith University

detail.title: Spatial–spectral transformer regression improves soil organic carbon estimation from fused VNIR–SWIR hyperspectral imaging
detail.abstract: Accurate estimation of soil organic carbon (SOC) is vital for soil monitoring and carbon accounting, yet conventional laboratory analyses are destructive and labour-intensive. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) offers a rapid, non-destructive alternative by simultaneously capturing spectral profiles and surface spatial heterogeneity. In this study, we investigated SOC estimation from fused visible-near-infrared (VNIR) and shortwave-infrared (SWIR) hyperspectral imagery using 555 tropical soil samples represented by 1,656 image cubes spanning 268 contiguous spectral bands. Four predictive modelling paradigms were benchmarked: partial least squares regression (PLSR), a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), a dual-branch Fusion-ResNet (FResNet), and the proposed Spatial-Spectral Transformer Regression (SSTR) model. Under a strict sample-code grouped evaluation across 10 independent splits, SSTR yielded the highest mean predictive performance among the evaluated models. In the 8:2 split, SSTR reached R² = 0.8198 ± 0.0361, Pearson r = 0.9258 ± 0.0079, RMSE = 0.7396 ± 0.1043%, and RPD = 2.4040 ± 0.2493, compared with PLSR (R² = 0.5568 ± 0.0566). Furthermore, SSTR used 2.57 M parameters compared with 43.30 M for FResNet (a 94.1% reduction), and maintained higher mean performance under constrained training data (20% training ratio: R² = 0.6329 ± 0.0365, RPD = 1.6583 ± 0.0810). These findings support the use of joint spatial-spectral representation learning for proximal SOC sensing and provide a methodological basis for future evaluation with imaging spectroscopy.

title: Institutional Investor Attention and Fund Performance
affiliations: Peking University

detail.title: Institutional Investor Attention and Fund Performance
detail.abstract: This article examines the information processing techniques used by large-scale investors by analysing the amount of time and attention that funds devote to online news stories about both the overall economy and individual enterprises. We want to see how it influences their investment choices and the overall performance of the funds. Using a time-series approach and a dataset that records stock ownership and news consumption habits, we can examine how market volatility affects people's focus. Looking at how paying attention to certain stocks alters portfolio weights and value contributed at the business level is also done using cross-sectional regression models. One of the three key takeaways from the data is that funds gravitate toward macro news when aggregate volatility is high and that funds that do so to a greater extent end up with better returns in the long run. The second finding reveals a positive correlation between larger stock portfolios and cross-sectional fund attentiveness. Additionally, when it comes to high-value news, fund attention significantly boosts the value-add of individual holdings. In light of these findings, policymakers and legislators should push for more open information settings and real-time reporting to improve market efficiency and equity in the allocation of resources.

title: A New Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge
affiliations: VID Specialized University

detail.title: A New Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge

keywords: India's Plant Variety and Farmers' Rights Act
TRIPS Agreement (Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights)
Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge

detail.abstract: Among the most contentious practices within a globalized and corporatized economy is allegations of so-called 'biopiracy'. This refers to the taking of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge without either free, prior and informed consent or any mechanisms for benefit-sharing with the community that provided the resource. Attempts to revise the TRIPS Agreement (Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights) to bring it more in compliance with the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) have not led to concrete results. The article analyzes CBD provisions, binding protocols and non-binding guiding documents, and two less known treaties of the United Nations. The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), that joined the United Nations in 1974, has-after negotiating for almost 15 yearsadopted the WIPO Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge. The article demonstrates how this WIPO Treaty is embedded in the 'defensive strategy' of traditional knowledge protection, enabling patent examiners to reject a patent as the alleged invention does not represent new and applicable knowledge. The alternative, termed 'positive strategy', is witnessed primarily in India's Plant Variety and Farmers' Rights Act, which has resulted in more grants of certificates for so-called 'farmers' varieties' compared to all other varieties together. Other United Nations treaties include elements of such protection, but not on the level of specify and subsequent implementation as found in India. The negotiations of what became the WIPO Treaty has generated increased awareness of indigenous peoples' traditional knowledge and should be easy to ratify as it aligns with existing legislation.

title: Heterogeneous Knowledge in Distributed Environmental Governance: Emergence, Integration, and the Preservation of Disagreement

detail.title: Heterogeneous Knowledge in Distributed Environmental Governance: Emergence, Integration, and the Preservation of Disagreement
detail.abstract: Governance of an interdependent environmental field requires knowledge that no party holds. Knowledge of such a field stands distributed among hydrological services, ecological programmes, health authorities, industrial operators, and populations resident in the systems concerned, and their holdings differ in variable, in resolution, in evidential standard, and in the kind of claim they issue. The prevailing response is integration understood as reconciliation: harmonise the categories, resolve the disagreements, and produce a single account on which decisions may rest. This paper argues that reconciliation so understood is unavailable and that its pursuit is harmful, and proposes an alternative conception of what integration can be. The method is conceptual, developed through an examination of what aggregation procedures preserve and what they discard. Three insights are advanced. Knowledge of a distributed field is not the union of what its parties hold, since the relations among their holdings, including their disagreements, carry information that no party's holding contains. Aggregation over claims that stand in logical relations to one another cannot in general be conducted claim by claim without producing conclusions no party accepts, which is a known impossibility whose bearing on environmental assessment has not been drawn. And the claims held by parties in such a field are of kinds that cannot be averaged, since a probability, a rate ratio, a monetary estimate, a qualitative account, and a legal duty are not five measurements of one quantity. From these the paper develops a conception of integration as temporary, question-relative assembly that preserves disagreement, uncertainty, and acknowledged ignorance as first-class content, together with the provenance required to prevent a single source counted twice from appearing as two confirmations. The paper surveys social epistemology, judgment aggregation, expert elicitation, post-normal science, co-production, epistemic injustice, and the traditional-knowledge literatures, states what each owns, and identifies the residue. It reports no empirical study and establishes no formal result.

title: A Diaconal Approach Guiding Strategic Alliance-Building
affiliations: VID Specialized University

detail.title: A Diaconal Approach Guiding Strategic Alliance-Building
detail.abstract: Two terms that are included in separate preambular paragraphs to the 2015 Paris Agreement, just transition and eco-justice, are analysed, to understand how they emerged and how they have implications for strategic alliance building and policymaking. Churches and church-related organisations have to prioritize with whom to cooperate, which relates to which notion of sustainability that is chosen. The article explains two Norwegian decades long cooperations, also identifying the main content of the massive investment programmes in green technology that are underway in the USA and the EU, that shift considerably the modes of cooperation. The article builds on the practice of diakonia as identified in Called to Transformation. Ecumenical Diakonia by the World Council of Churhes and ACT Alliance, and theological perspectives, asking how they can be tools for alliance building. Specifically, the article identifies two opposing views on nature: instrumental and intrinsic; two opposing understandings of environmental compensation; and two rationales for cooperation in relation to nature: "technology fix" and "nature first".

title:
Furnisher, not Excluded: 
Mapping the Scope Gap Between CEMAC’s Credit Information-sharing Mandate and Mobile Money Data

detail.title:
Furnisher, not Excluded: 
Mapping the Scope Gap Between CEMAC’s Credit Information-sharing Mandate and Mobile Money Data
detail.abstract: The Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa (CEMAC) launched its first regional credit bureau, BIC-CEMAC, in January 2026 with a founding cohort of 41 commercial banks and 20 microfinance institutions — and no mobile money operators. This is notable because both dominant Cameroonian mobile money issuers, Orange Money Cameroun and MTN’s Mobile Money Corporation, have held Établissement de Paiement (EP) licenses since 2022 and 2023 respectively, and are, under the primary text of BEAC Instruction N°014/2020 (Article 3), mandatorily bound to furnish credit information to the bureau on the same terms as banks. This paper undertakes a close textual analysis of the two governing instructions — 014/2020 (furnisher obligations) and 010/2020 (client-consent architecture) — and finds that the absence of EPs from the founding cohort does not reflect legal exclusion but a narrower, more consequential problem: the mandated data-content categories in Article 3 were drafted around a bank-shaped template of formal credit exposures and payment incidents, and do not contemplate the transactional and behavioral data (cash-in/cash-out volume, merchant payment frequency, airtime top-up patterns) that has underpinned alternative-data credit scoring in comparable African markets. We situate this within the information-economics literature on credit registries (Pagano & Jappelli, 1993; Djankov, McLiesh, & Shleifer, 2007) and argue that CEMAC’s 2018–2020 regulatory architecture predates a demonstrable regional and continental shift — visible in UEMOA’s 2016-era grands facturiers furnisher category and Morocco’s 2024 reform — toward explicitly naming telecom and mobile data as bureau-eligible inputs. We propose a targeted amendment to Instruction 014/2020 rather than new primary legislation, and identify testable near-term indicators — including whether MTN’s Momocash micro-credit product is already generating Article 3-reportable exposures — for assessing whether the gap is closing.

title: Natural Resources, Institutions, and Green Economic Diversification in Azerbaijan: An Integrated Analytical Framework
affiliations: Fukuoka University - Faculty of Economics, Independent and Azerbaijan Technical University

detail.title: Natural Resources, Institutions, and Green Economic Diversification in Azerbaijan: An Integrated Analytical Framework
detail.abstract: Azerbaijan's hydrocarbon resources have financed economic growth, public investment, and infrastructure development, but have also reinforced dependence on commodity exports. This article examines how natural resource endowments, institutional quality, productive capabilities, and green-transition policies interact in shaping economic diversification. The study adopts a qualitative analytical design combining a narrative review of academic literature, document analysis of international and national policy and development documents, and contextual synthesis of Azerbaijanspecific empirical evidence. On this basis, it develops an integrated framework in which resource revenues provide financial capacity, institutions govern resource allocation and policy implementation, productive capabilities enable structural transformation, and green policies orient diversification toward sustainable activities. The framework suggests that resource wealth contributes to long-term diversification when revenues are converted into human capital, innovation, infrastructure, and competitive non-oil activities. For Azerbaijan, renewable energy, digital transformation, green industry, and private-sector development are identified as mutually reinforcing priorities. The paper recommends strengthening institutional coordination, investment governance, research and innovation capacity, private-sector capabilities, and international technology partnerships. Its principal contribution is an Azerbaijan-specific conceptual framework integrating resource-based financial capacity, institutional quality, productive capabilities, and green transition, providing a basis for policy design and future empirical testing in resource-rich economies.

title: From Formal Equality to Reserved Representation: Omani Women's Political Rights and Institutional Embedding; A Literature Review
affiliations: Independent Public Policy Analyst

detail.title: From Formal Equality to Reserved Representation: Omani Women's Political Rights and Institutional Embedding; A Literature Review
detail.abstract: This review examines why decades of formal political equality for Omani women did not produce sustained elected representation and what the move toward reserved representation reveals about political institutional embedding. It argues that Oman’s problem was not absent recognition, but the weak conversion of eligibility into durable representation. Women’s access to voting and candidacy, reported from 1994, was not matched by party recruitment, list placement, territorial guarantees, or mechanisms counteracting gendered networks. The Shura Council consequently produced intermittent representation: one woman was elected in 2015, two in 2019, and none in 2023. The 2026 announcement of eleven additional seats for women, one per governorate, marks a shift from non-discrimination toward guaranteed descriptive presence. Yet it remains an announced allocation rather than an operational quota until its legal basis, selection, accountability, and continuity are published. Oman shows that political rights become embedded when organisational rules make inclusion reproducible across electoral cycles.

title:
Beyond the Memorandum: Deconstructing the Strategic Miscalculations of the Sudanese "Russian Partnership" Proposal
A Comprehensive Analysis of the Flamingo Naval Base Agreement and Its Multidimensional Impacts on Sudan's Civil War, Regional Stability, and Geopolitical Alignment
affiliations: Al-Neelain University - Department of Economics

detail.title:
Beyond the Memorandum: Deconstructing the Strategic Miscalculations of the Sudanese "Russian Partnership" Proposal
A Comprehensive Analysis of the Flamingo Naval Base Agreement and Its Multidimensional Impacts on Sudan's Civil War, Regional Stability, and Geopolitical Alignment

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The subject is very important for Sudan's future.
declarations.ethicsApproval: There is no conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: No Funding

detail.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive academic analysis of the proposed Russian naval base at Flamingo (Port Sudan) and its multifaceted implications for Sudan's ongoing civil war, regional geopolitical dynamics, and the viability of Sudanese statehood. Through critical examination of primary documents, official statements, and strategic analyses, this study argues that the Russian naval base agreement represents both a strategic opportunity and a profound miscalculation for Sudan's ruling military council. The deal, offering a 25-year lease for a naval logistics facility in exchange for advanced Russian weaponry embodies the desperate calculus of a besieged regime seeking survival through great-power patronage (Larsen & Wivel, 2025). However, this paper contends that the agreement fundamentally misreads Russia's pragmatic realpolitik, overestimates the strategic value of a fixed naval installation in an era of technological warfare, and risks transforming Sudan into a frontline state in renewed great-power competition. Drawing on international relations theory, regional security studies, and critical analysis of the memorandum that surfaced from an unnamed Sudanese faction, this study demonstrates that the naval base deal is symptomatic of deeper institutional dysfunction within Sudan's military establishment. The paper concludes that sustainable peace in Sudan requires not external military patronage but genuine institutional reconstruction, national reconciliation, and a coherent strategic vision that transcends the transactional logic of weapons-for-bases diplomacy (de Waal, 2026).

reference: 125 Michigan Law Review (forthcoming 2027)
title: Supreme Court Lawmaking and Clear Error as Characterological Discipline

detail.title: Supreme Court Lawmaking and Clear Error as Characterological Discipline
detail.abstract:
This Article proposes a characterological interpretation of clear error deference as it operates in Supreme Court constitutional lawmaking. It adds a fifth justification to the four on which scholars and judges have rested Rule 52(a)(6)—epistemic competence, structural allocation, systemic efficiency, and public legitimacy—attuned to the domain of an apex court making prospective, binding constitutional rules. Drawing on George Herbert Mead’s concept of the generalized other and Erving Goffman’s rules of deference and demeanor, the Article argues that the Rule functions as a role-orienting idiom in an interrelated system: an institutional practice through which a justice signals regard to others, settles expectations of behavior, and pluralizes inputs to lawmaking. This interpretation is characterological because a justice’s internal commitment to her role within a system built on role relationships triggers the idiom and mediates its content; positive law does neither.

Guarding against unitary enunciation of legal rules and unitary management of Article III, the Rule as institutional practice steadies and broadens constitutional lawmaking that must carry authority in a fractious and heterogeneous polity. The act of confronting a record one did not build and displacing the findings of another in a shared system yields three benefits. For the individual justice, the practice enlarges deliberative reasoning by interjecting the presence of other minds at the juncture where the temptation to overreach is greatest. For Article III, it sustains a schema of pluralized, diffuse, and accountable lawmaking power and gives the Court’s pronouncements the social form of authority exercised through role rather than asserted through will. For constitutional law, it sustains the capacity to arbitrate political disagreement by registering and speaking to it.

The Article then demonstrates that the Roberts Court has repeatedly violated the Rule so understood. It isolates five injuries, in roughly escalating order: the disruption of the mutualistic teamwork on which functional differentiation within a unified, hierarchical judiciary depends; the loss of doctrinal and public transparency over Court action; the invitation to view the Court as politicizing justice; the undermining of the Court’s own lawmaking authority at the endpoint of totalizing supremacy; and the disintegration of the deference practices that turn a system into a system of law. It concludes by positioning the Rule alongside other deference practices to argue that Article III lawmaking acquires its authority through a complex system of role-mediated judgments that positive law can capture only in part.

title: Differential Environmental Governance: Coordination through Change among Systems Sharing No Common Ontology

detail.title: Differential Environmental Governance: Coordination through Change among Systems Sharing No Common Ontology
detail.abstract: Coordinated action on an interdependent environmental field requires that parties describing the field in different terms act together on the same processes. The usual route to such coordination is agreement about states: a shared account of what a quantity is, and a shared target for it. This paper argues that agreement of that kind is expensive in representational commitment and frequently unavailable, and proposes a primitive that is cheaper. The method is conceptual and definitional, developed through a graded account of what agreement of successive kinds requires. The paper's central observation is that agreement about the direction and unusualness of a change demands far less shared representation than agreement about the identity of the quantity that changed, so that parties who cannot describe a system in common terms may nonetheless recognise, report, and act on correspondences among changes. Three consequences are developed. Differentials are proposed as an ontology-light coordination primitive, with the conditions under which correspondences among changes are identifiable and the conditions under which they mislead. The argument is grounded in a dynamical result and not in convenience alone: transitions induced by the rate at which a system is forced are not detectable from its state, so a governance arrangement addressed only to states is blind to a class of transition in principle. And the limits of the primitive are stated at length, including its blindness to a system already in an unacceptable state whose rate of change is zero, from which follows a division of labour between constraints stated over states and governance conducted over changes. The paper concedes the philosophical treatment of difference and repetition, the structural analysis of relational value, existing rate-based regulatory instruments, and derivative action in control engineering, and identifies what remains unclaimed. It reports no empirical study and establishes no formal result.

title: Expressly Authorised, Procedurally Underdetermined: Judicial AI and Reviewable Justice in Abu Dhabi

detail.title: Expressly Authorised, Procedurally Underdetermined: Judicial AI and Reviewable Justice in Abu Dhabi

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author serves as a Judge of the Egyptian Court of Appeal within the Egyptian Ministry of Justice. This professional affiliation is disclosed for transparency. The author has no financial, advisory or institutional relationship with the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department, the Abu Dhabi Department of Government Enablement, or any technology provider discussed in this article. The research was conducted independently, and the views expressed are solely those of the author and do not represent the Egyptian Ministry of Justice or any court or public authority.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required because this study constitutes doctrinal legal research based exclusively on publicly available legislation, official documents, policy instruments and academic literature. It involved no human participants, interviews, surveys, experiments, confidential information or personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: Abu Dhabi has announced an AI Judicial Platform intended to support judicial and legal decisionmaking under 'full human supervision and validation', with phased implementation expected from September 2026. This article asks whether the UAE-Abu Dhabi legal framework translates impartiality, reasoned adjudication, equality of arms and judicial independence into enforceable and reviewable safeguards when AI materially assists civil or commercial adjudication in the onshore Abu Dhabi courts. Through doctrinal and institutional analysis, it shows that judicial AI enters neither a legal vacuum nor a merely soft-law environment. Articles 52-54 of Abu Dhabi Law No 6 of 2024 expressly authorise such systems and bind their use to fundamental rights, nondiscrimination, privacy, security, audit, transparency and responsible decision-maker control. The difficulty is procedural: published law and official information do not yet demonstrate a system-use challenge, an AI-inclusive judicial record, case-specific contestability of materially relied-upon output, or a publicly verifiable allocation of control over functions, updates, logs, audit and suspension. Four stress tests expose the resulting mismatch between person-shaped impartiality rules and infrastructure-shaped bias; facially sufficient reasons and unrecorded machine influence; judicial technological advantage and adversarial contestability; and formal judicial authority and external infrastructural control. The article proposes meaningful and reviewable human control as the governing standard and recommends risk-based assessment, proportionate logging, disclosure, party response, independent audit and judicial control of updates and suspension. As an ex-ante publicsource assessment, it does not infer that undisclosed safeguards are absent; it identifies the conditions necessary to make material AI influence visible, answerable and reviewable.

title: The Political Economic Analysis of the Ideology of the Predominant Islamic Fundamentalist Groups in Sudan
