detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence has become one of the most influential investment themes in healthcare. Yet much of the current discussion continues to treat AI exposure as a sufficient proxy for future value creation. This perspective article introduces the Clinical Alpha Framework, a new conceptual model proposed by the author to distinguish between two mechanisms of value creation in AI-enabled healthcare companies: AI Alpha and Clinical Alpha. AI Alpha represents value generated by technological narratives, investor expectations, and perceived innovation potential. Clinical Alpha represents value generated through verifiable clinical evidence, regulatory validation, real-world adoption, and measurable improvements in healthcare delivery and patient outcomes. To formalize this distinction, the article introduces three original conceptual tools: the Clinical Alpha Matrix, a two-dimensional classification framework; the Proposed Clinical Alpha Index (PCAI), a theoretical scoring model for assessing clinical value creation; and AI-Clinical Divergence (ACD), which captures the degree of misalignment between market enthusiasm and validated clinical performance. The central proposition is that while AI Alpha may dominate valuation dynamics in the short term, Clinical Alpha is more likely to determine sustainable value creation over longer investment horizons.

title: Multi-objective energy efficiency optimization torque distribution strategy for dual-motor all-wheel-drive commercial vehicles considering road adhesion conditions
affiliations: Shandong University of Technology, Shandong University of Technology, Shandong University of Technology, Shandong University of Technology and Shandong University of Technology

detail.title: Multi-objective energy efficiency optimization torque distribution strategy for dual-motor all-wheel-drive commercial vehicles considering road adhesion conditions
detail.abstract: Dual-motor all-wheel drive (DM-AWD) commercial vehicles can improve energy efficiency by coordinating the operating points of the front and rear motors within high-efficiency regions. However, the conventional torque distribution strategies based on motor efficiency optimization do not explicitly account for road adhesion conditions on motor energy consumption, tire wear, and driving stability, which results in limited adaptability to varying operating conditions. To address this limitation, a motor torque distribution strategy considering road adhesion conditions is proposed. First, a unified multi-objective energy optimization framework was developed to account for motor efficiency maps, tire slip energy loss and road adhesion utilization. Second, a dynamic weighting method for real-time adjustment of the optimization objectives according to tire-road adhesion conditions was designed to adapt to changes in operating conditions. Furthermore, a multi-objective optimization method based on offline optimization initialization guided sequential quadratic programming (OOIG-SQP) was proposed to determine the torque distribution coefficient in real time. Simulation results show that compared with the traditional efficiency optimization torque distribution strategy that does not consider road adhesion conditions, the proposed torque distribution strategy reduced total energy consumption by 1.15% and 2.49% respectively, reduced tire slip energy loss by 1.06% and 26.0% respectively, and decreased the weighted RMS adhesion utilization by 0.80% and 14.5% respectively, it effectively improves the vehicle's economy, driving stability and tire wear under different road adhesion conditions.

title: Unverified Digital Transformation Disclosure, R&D Capability, and Stock Price Crash Risk
affiliations: , Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) - School of Business and Technology Management and Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) - Department of Management Science

detail.title: Unverified Digital Transformation Disclosure, R&D Capability, and Stock Price Crash Risk
detail.abstract: We examine whether a firm's digital transformation (DT) orientation, measured from its annual report business description, predicts one-year-ahead stock price crash risk, and whether prior R&D capability governs that relation. Because no line item under U.S. GAAP isolates digital investment, the annual report and its narrative are the primary standardized record of a firm's DT stance, and with no reported figure to delimit what that stance entails, otherwise identical narratives may describe a program never operationalized. We use R&D intensity, audited under ASC 730, over the two fiscal years preceding the filing year as a marker of capacity observable when the stance is taken rather than recovered from outcomes realized afterward. In U.S. non-technology firms over 2010-2023, DT carries a valuation premium that is positive even where capability is absent. Next-year crash risk conditions on that same margin. The marginal effect of DT is positive among firms with little or no prior R&D, crosses zero near the eighty-third percentile of R&D intensity, and turns negative among firms with a substantial accumulated R&D base. The relation concentrates in the left tail, predicting crash weeks but not comparably defined jump weeks. It is absent in placebo years and survives selection and competing-moderator checks. The price rewards even the unbacked digital stance; the return distribution that follows does not.

title: Academic Leadership in the Boardroom and Corporate Green Breakthrough Innovations: The Moderating Role of Internal R&D Intensity
affiliations: Peking University

detail.title: Academic Leadership in the Boardroom and Corporate Green Breakthrough Innovations: The Moderating Role of Internal R&D Intensity
detail.abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine if academic leaders can assist businesses in developing scientifically sound new ideas and whether in-house research and development departments can supplement or replace external scientific consultants. This research examines resource dependency theory through the lens of resource supply using panel data collected from 991 publicly listed, innovative U.S. enterprises. To determine if there is a correlation between having academic directors and developing ground-breaking ideas grounded in science, the empirical research examines the publication histories of various firms. To test the robustness of our findings, we use instrumental variable analysis in conjunction with natural experiments driven by the untimely death of prominent academics. The findings demonstrate a robust correlation between the involvement of academic directors and advancements in scientific knowledge. Companies with a longer publishing history have a greater positive correlation, demonstrating that in-house R&D knowledge and outside academic knowledge are complementary rather than mutually exclusive. Additionally, we demonstrate that the findings are robust when using instrumental variable analysis in conjunction with natural studies centred on the unexpected deaths of eminent academics. These findings reinforce the correctness of the main points. The role of strategic leadership in facilitating science-based innovation and increasing the innovation potential of enterprises via the use of external academic information is further illuminated by these findings. Businesses and policymakers should work towards better connections between academic research and corporate R&D if they want to encourage innovative breakthroughs.

title: Sustainable Development Beyond Dominant Knowledge
affiliations: , Universidad Nacional de Jaén, IET MJP Rohilkhand University, Aligarh Muslim University Aligarh and Aligarh Muslim University Aligarh

detail.title: Sustainable Development Beyond Dominant Knowledge
detail.abstract: Sustainable Development has been the defining institutional commitment of the international community for over three decades. It has produced various treaties, agreements and many policies. It has also coincided with the crossing of seven of nine planetary boundaries, the accelerating loss of one million species and a world in which 783 million people go hungry inside a food system that produces enough for fifteen billion. The dominant framework through which sustainable development is defined, measured, governed and taught is built on a specific epistemological foundation. Indigenous knowledge systems, ecological tipping points, and the intrinsic value of non-human life are not merely overlooked by this framework but are structurally invisible to it. This article tries to trace a single argument that both ecological and epistemological crises are the same. Genuine transformation requires an ontological reorientation, a fundamental shift in what institutions believe exists, what they believe has value and whose knowledge they are willing to trust. Nature, unlike institutions, will not wait.

title: A simple ML-Driven Ionic Liquid Electrochemical Sensor Array with Wavelet-Derived Kinetic Insights for Selective Hydrogen and Oxygen Monitoring in complex gas mixtures
affiliations: University of Missouri, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Oakland University and University of Missouri

detail.title: A simple ML-Driven Ionic Liquid Electrochemical Sensor Array with Wavelet-Derived Kinetic Insights for Selective Hydrogen and Oxygen Monitoring in complex gas mixtures
detail.abstract: Selective and simultaneous monitoring of hydrogen and oxygen is critical for safety in the expanding hydrogen economy, yet conventional electrochemical sensors face persistent challenges of cross-sensitivity and signal drift that compromise reliability during long-term operation in real-world. Here, we present an ionic liquid–based electrochemical gas sensor array, composed of three identical cells operated at distinct electrode potentials (-1.5 V, -1.2 V, and +0.4 V, vs. Pt quasi-reference electrode), for the selective classification and quantitative determination of hydrogen and oxygen in variable gas backgrounds containing methane and sulfur dioxide interferents in real-time. Chronoamperometric signals are preprocessed using the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to decouple analyte-induced transients from baseline drift, and a compact set of 21 physics-informed features extracted from DWT detail coefficients is used to train four supervised machine learning models including Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Multilayer Perceptron, and XGBoost for gas classification and concentration prediction. Under 7-fold cross-validation, Random Forest achieves the highest classification balanced accuracy of 92.86% with the lowest coefficient of variance, and the lowest regression mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) for both hydrogen and oxygen. Beyond practical sensing performance, we derive a kinetic descriptor analytically proportional to the effective gas sensing rate constant, revealing that oxygen recovery kinetics decelerate at higher concentrations, which is consistent with increased superoxide O2•– formation at higher oxygen concentrations, which may promote surface accumulation and side reactions with ionic liquid and reactive interferent species such as SO2 providing a mechanistic explanation for the greater susceptibility of oxygen sensors to baseline drift.

title: The theory, method, and application of deep learning-based filtering: A review
affiliations: Zhejiang University of Technology and Zhejiang University of Technology

detail.title: The theory, method, and application of deep learning-based filtering: A review
detail.abstract: State estimation is concerned with fusing noisy measurements of a physical system with the dynamics describing its state evolution for the purpose of inferring unmeasurable states and denoising measurable ones. Traditional state-estimation techniques rely on mathematical representations in the form of state-space models, which generally stem from the hand-crafted model derivation. To cope with real-world dynamics, an intelligent system needs to learn the correlation between measurements and the underlying state in the absence of domain knowledge. This ability, known as learning-based state estimation, provides a foundation for systems to learn state estimation directly from data in imperfect environments. The growing attention to this research area highlights both its practical value and inherent challenges. In this work, we focus on the scope of real-time state estimation within state-space models. Accordingly, we present an extensive review of state estimation techniques grounded in deep learning, seeking to bridge the basic settings, theoretical foundations, representative methods, and practical applications. Based on existing theoretical and empirical results, we summarize the general objectives of deep learning-based filtering as ensuring a state-space representation aligned with true dynamics and a proper filtering policy. Then we provide a systematic taxonomy, extensively analyzing how representative methods address state estimation problems and how they are adapted to particular challenges in realistic applications. By exploring emerging trends in detail, we believe that such a holistic perspective can greatly aid future research within this domain and related areas.

title: UTPK: Unified Target-Aware Prior Knowledge for TransferableMulti-Target Adversarial Attacks
affiliations: University of Jinan, University of Jinan, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Jinan, University of Jinan, University of Jinan, University of Jinan and Shandong Normal University

detail.title: UTPK: Unified Target-Aware Prior Knowledge for TransferableMulti-Target Adversarial Attacks
detail.abstract: Transferable targeted adversarial attacks aim to mislead black-box models into predefined adversarial predictions. Although recent methods have introduced single-target generative attacks that train a generator for each target class to produce highly transferable perturbations, this strategy incurs heavy computational costs in multi-target settings. In contrast, multi-target adversarial attacks employ a shared class-conditional generator for multiple categories, significantly reducing computational overhead and improving practical efficiency. However, such generator simply use class labels as conditions, overlooking the semantic diversity knowledge within target classes, which leads to ambiguous mappings and perturbation overlap. To overcome the above limitations, we propose the Unified Target-Aware Prior Knowledge (UTPK) framework that generates high-quality target-specific prior knowledge by leveraging target class feature representations instead of class labels to realize more affluent condition mapping. Specifically, we design a saliency-driven target instance refinement module and a semantic property alignment module to effectively extract target-aware prior knowledge, which is then integrated into the generator via a semantic fusion module to enhance its ability to control decision boundaries. To optimize adversarial distribution alignment, the Divergence-aware Classification Loss is proposed to minimize the feature space divergence between adversarial examples and their similar target classes by incorporating non-target class k-nearest neighbors. Sufficient experimental results verify that the proposed UTPK achieves superior transferability compared with existing multi-target generative adversarial attack approaches. As a concrete case, our method raises the attack success rate from ResNet-152 to Inception-v3 by 16.65%. The code of UTPK is available at: https://github.com/NA-13340/UTPK.

title: Invariant Interest Learning for Sequential Recommendation with Conditional Distribution Bottleneck
affiliations: South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN and South China University of Technology

detail.title: Invariant Interest Learning for Sequential Recommendation with Conditional Distribution Bottleneck
detail.abstract: Sequential recommendation (SR) aims to predict users' future interests from historical interactions. However, evolving recommendation environments often induce distribution shifts, causing SR models to capture spurious environment-specific patterns rather than stable user interests, thereby degrading their generalization ability. In this paper, we propose CDIB, an invariant interest learning method with Conditional DIstribution Bottleneck. The key idea is to learn predictive interest patterns that remain invariant across diverse distributions. Specifically, CDIB consists of: 1) a context-aware subsequence identifier that adaptively disentangles intrinsic interests from environment-specific interactions, extracting stable behavioral patterns across varying environments; 2) a generative distribution constructor that explicitly simulates distribution shifts during training based on the inferred environment-specific interactions, synthesizing diverse sequences to broaden the training distribution; and 3) a conditional distribution bottleneck regularization that constrains generated distributions to preserve critical user interests, enabling the model to learn robust representations for adaptation to heterogeneous environments.Theoretically, we show that the proposed method suppresses variant information and retains invariant predictive signals, thereby facilitating invariant interest learning. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of CDIB over state-of-the-art methods.The code is available at https://github.com/KNwbq/CDIB.

title: Anytime-Valid Tests of Factor Alphas
affiliations: Hong Kong Chu Hai College

detail.title: Anytime-Valid Tests of Factor Alphas
detail.abstract: Standard tests of cross-sectional predictors—p-value corrections, Bayesian posterior odds—assume a fixed sample size. Factor research is sequential: a predictor is discovered, new data are added, and what gets tested next depends on what has been seen. Under such optional stopping and continuation, no classical procedure retains the error rates its users assume. I construct an anytime-valid test of H₀: α_F = 0 in two steps. Factor returns are first projected on benchmark loadings estimated from past data alone, without an intercept, so the residual series has mean equal to the intercept and contains no look-ahead. A hypothetical investor then places bounded, predictable bets on those residuals; her wealth is an e-process, a nonnegative martingale under the null, and the test rejects when it exceeds 1/α. Ville's inequality keeps the error probability below α at every stopping time. The construction is closed-form and runs on any long–short return series. We apply it to the 212 publicly available predictors, conditioning on the Fama–French five factors over 1963/07–2023/12. Of the 212, 76 reject at the 1/α = 20 threshold. The median post-publication growth rate of the 212 predictors falls to 22% of its pre-publication level. Out of sample, e-value screening selects fewer factors than |t| > 2 or |t| > 3, and its e-BH variant earns the largest point estimate of FF5 alpha (5.0%/yr).

title: Prediction of transient heat exchange performance of energy pile groups using a physics-constrained DeepONet
affiliations: Shenzhen University, Shenzhen University, Shenzhen University and Shenzhen University

detail.title: Prediction of transient heat exchange performance of energy pile groups using a physics-constrained DeepONet
detail.abstract: Predicting the transient heat exchange performance of energy pile groups becomes particularly challenging when thermal interference among piles, groundwater seepage, and intermittent operation act simultaneously. Numerical simulations are computationally expensive, whereas data-driven models mainly focused on the quasi-steady-state response of an isolated pile. This study developed an integrated framework of an analytical model and a physics-constrained deep operator network for transient thermal performance of energy pile groups under groundwater seepage and intermittent operation. The model for pile groups was based on the moving finite cylindrical source theory, thermal resistance model, and spatiotemporal superposition principles. After validated with numerical and experimental results, the analytical model was used to generate 15,000 cases for energy pile groups during a summer season, including nine physical parameters, operation strategies, time, and corresponding heat exchange data. Three machine learning models were proposed to predict the time-dependent heat exchange performance of pile groups. The physics-constrained deep operator network showed superior performance in both validation set and test set, because of embedded physics constraints. Illustrative cases further demonstrated that the proposed model can reproduce the transient thermal performance of individual piles and pile groups over a 90-day period within 1 second. SHAP analysis identified the relative importance of ten input features, and the initial ground temperature and operation strategy were the most important for thermal performance of energy pile groups. The proposed framework provides a physically credible and computationally efficient surrogate model for parametric screening and preliminary optimization of energy pile groups.

title: Budget-constrained multi-objective optimization of a lean-burn hydrogen Miller engine via intelligent infill strategies
affiliations: Tongji University, Tongji University, Tongji University and Tongji University

detail.title: Budget-constrained multi-objective optimization of a lean-burn hydrogen Miller engine via intelligent infill strategies
detail.abstract: In surrogate-assisted engine calibration the computational cost is dominated by high-fidelity sampling, so how a limited sample budget is distributed over the decision space sets the upper bound of optimization quality. In lean-burn hydrogen internal combustion engines (ICEs) the learning difficulty of the power, economy and emission response surfaces is strongly non-uniform, and non-uniform in different places for each objective: thermal NOx emissions change by orders of magnitude as the excess air ratio λ crosses approximately 2.0, whereas the difficult regions of the power and economy surfaces, which vary smoothly with λ, cannot be located in advance from combustion physics, yet the prevailing one-shot uniform sampling is agnostic to this difficulty distribution. An adaptive infill sampling method is therefore proposed for the multi-objective optimization of a 350 kW six-cylinder direct-injection Miller cycle hydrogen ICE at 1500 r/min, with Miller degree, intake manifold absolute pressure, hydrogen injection timing and λ as decision variables. Starting from a continuous Latin hypercube seed, samples are added batch by batch according to the spatial distribution of three-objective cross-validation errors, and sampling stops on whichever of accuracy convergence and a batch cap occurs first. A budget-matched comparison, in which the adaptive scheme and a uniform baseline share one seed, expand in synchronized batches and are scored on a sealed hold-out set, is followed by non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) optimization and GT-Power closed-loop validation. Seed-stage errors cluster in λ-dominated bands with a concentration ratio of 1.75, and the difficulty peaks of the three objectives are separated along λ, so that the aggregated field is bimodal. The adaptive scheme places nearly 60% of its infill samples in the steep-gradient band λ = 1.5–2.5 — the band carrying the power and economy difficulty lobe, into which maximin spreading of the targeted candidates further concentrates them — and saves 25–33% of the samples needed for equal surrogate accuracy. At the same 240-sample budget its mean relative NOx error in the critical region is 9.97% against 12.06% for the baseline, with no accuracy loss elsewhere, and its Pareto-front hypervolume averages 0.968 against 0.931. In closed-loop validation its compromise solution stays within 2.8% for all three objectives, whereas the baseline overestimates the indicated mean effective pressure (IMEP) of its own compromise by 11.8%, and the two recommended Miller degrees differ by 24.2 °CA. Sample distribution therefore governs not only accuracy metrics but the engineering calibration conclusion itself.

title: Patch Transition Modeling for Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection
affiliations: City University of Hong Kong, City University of Hong Kong, Southern University of Science and Technology, Shandong University, Southern University of Science and Technology, Lingnan University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Patch Transition Modeling for Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection
detail.abstract: Multivariate time-series anomaly detection is a critical task in real-world monitoring systems, where multiple correlated variables continuously reflect the operating status of complex systems. Existing deep learning methods have achieved promising results by modeling normal patterns in multivariate time series. However, many methods focus primarily on whether the current window or patch can be reconstructed or predicted correctly, while explicitly modeling state transitions between adjacent patches remains limited. In this paper, we propose Patch Transition Modeling for Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection (PTM). The method first divides each input window into non-overlapping patches along the temporal dimension and learns patch-level latent representations. Patch-level transition modeling is then introduced to capture normal state evolution between adjacent patches, and a cross-view prediction mechanism is further designed to enhance representation-level consistency across neighboring patches. Together, these transition-aware components enable the model to detect anomalies from abnormal evolution patterns rather than relying solely on reconstruction errors. In addition, we propose a calibrated multi-score fusion strategy to integrate reconstruction, transition, and cross-view prediction scores. By normalizing heterogeneous scores with running statistics estimated from normal training samples, the strategy reduces scale imbalance among different score sources and produces more robust anomaly scores. Extensive experiments on five benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves strong and competitive performance against representative baselines under threshold-independent evaluation metrics. Ablation studies, score component analysis, calibration analysis, patch size sensitivity analysis, and supplementary point-adjusted F1 results further verify the effectiveness and robustness of patch-level transition modeling and calibrated multi-score fusion.

title: Neural-Network Policy Approximation for Finite-Horizon Models with EGM-Style Targets

detail.title: Neural-Network Policy Approximation for Finite-Horizon Models with EGM-Style Targets
detail.abstract: This paper introduces DeepEGM, a deep learning solver for finite-horizon consumption-savings models. Instead of minimizing first-order-condition residuals, it uses analytically inverted Euler-equation targets as supervised regression labels. The proposed method trains one compact feedforward neural network per time period through backward induction. Each period's network is initialized from its neighbor's trained weights, so the optimizer learns only the marginal policy change from one period to the next. A forward-simulation pass between backward sweeps concentrates training data on the on-policy state distribution, focusing network capacity on states that agents actually visit. I benchmark DeepEGM against classical EGM on a five-dimensional buffer-stock model with three continuous heterogeneity dimensions. The leading deeplearning solver for this class of models reports a mean log 10 Euler equation error of -3.4 after one hour of training on a GPU. DeepEGM surpasses this accuracy in a fraction of the training time, reaching -3.5 in roughly 223 seconds on a CPU. A hardware-invariant floating-point operation count shows that DeepEGM requires roughly 29,300× fewer training FLOPs than the current state-of-the-art. Classical EGM remains more precise in five dimensions but requires dense grids that scale exponentially with the state space. When the model is extended to six dimensions with agent-specific discount factors, grid coarsening degrades EGM accuracy below that of DeepEGM, which maintains its performance.

title: IQs of the 5,570 Greatest Geniuses in History

detail.title: IQs of the 5,570 Greatest Geniuses in History
detail.abstract: We present a historiometric method by means of which it is possible to make objective estimates of cognitive levels, on a standardised IQ scale, for 5,570 intellectuals who lived from 2700 BC onwards. Most of the data used come from Charles Murray’s book “Human Accomplishment” [1], which covers the period from 800 BC to AD 1950 and includes 4,596 subjects. We expanded Murray’s list with standardised encyclopaedic data, filtered out duplicates and errors, arriving at 5,570 subjects. To estimate the IQs, a new method for norming psychometric tests was used, which produces scores on a ratio scale – “Norming of IQ Tests on a Ratio Scale” [2] – along with the meaning of “intelligence” discussed in the article “The Correct Meaning of Intelligence” [3], with an effective range 3 to 3.5 times broader than the spectrum covered by traditional tests. This detail is indispensable for producing accurate assessments at the highest levels, avoiding manifestly untenable figures such as IQ=123 for Feynman, IQ=105 for Copernicus or IQ=160 for Einstein, etc. To link and calibrate the scale, IQ estimates for 302 intellectuals were used, of whom 262 had their IQs correlated with 26 quantitative indices based on these individuals’ intellectual output (26 explanatory variables X1, X2 ..., Xn), such as numbers of publications, awards, citations, etc. The 26 variables were then scaled to [0,1] and weighted so as to produce scores XiWi, whose sum yields the composite score Z=∑_(i=1)^n▒〖X_i W_i 〗. The weights are optimised by means of SLSQP (SQP+BFGS) so as to maximise the correlation between Z and IQ. The model was applied to the 5,570 subjects, generating preliminary IQ estimates. In a second stage, 208 explanatory variables (including the initial 26) were used for fine-tuning. Not all 208 variables were used in the first stage in order to avoid overfitting. In both stages, outliers were removed up to a limit of 7% by means of an adaptive elliptical filter using Mahalanobis distances, calibrated by χ_p^2 with α dependent on N. The result for pIQ × Z26 was r=0.9059 and for pIQ × Z208 was r=0.9781, standing out in two important respects: (1) the correlation obtained between Z and IQ is higher than the correlation between pairs of psychometric instruments compared with one another (~0.6); (2) the metric of the HM26 and HM208 models is based on variables recognised as more relevant to intellectual assessment at the highest levels, whereas the construct validity of traditional tests (WAIS, SB, CCFIT, etc.), which assess speed in solving elementary questions, is compromised when assessing IQs above 130 [2] [3].

title: Relational Fields and Criticality Preparation: A Conditional Model of Generative Escape

detail.title: Relational Fields and Criticality Preparation: A Conditional Model of Generative Escape
detail.abstract: A perturbation can disappear quickly in one dynamical regime and cross a transition boundary in another. This paper studies the gradual transformation that changes that response. It proposes criticality preparation as a typed, route-specific comparison in which a persistent intervention changes local recovery, threshold geometry, potential barrier, finite-time gain, stochastic escape, or viable receiving access over a declared horizon. The concept is developed independently from its oceanographic inspiration. A dimensionless fold model yields exact expressions for the stable branch, unstable threshold, recovery rate, threshold margin, and potential barrier. A negative kick of fixed magnitude h crosses the frozen threshold exactly when a < h 2 /4. Along a linear slow path, this condition gives a closed-form preparation time. A small-noise escape expression states a separate stochastic route with explicit asymptotic conditions. A triangular two-state extension then preserves both stable eigenvalues while cross-channel transient gain changes with relational coupling. Reproducible simulations verify the deterministic threshold within the toy system. With fixed noise and horizon, the estimated escape frequency rises from zero observed events among 10,000 paths at the two deepest parameter settings to 0.9732 at the shallowest setting. Step-size and noise checks preserve the qualitative parameter ordering. These results establish conditional model consequences and a computational benchmark.

title: One Rate, Uneven Transmission: Monetary Policy after Oil Supply Shocks in the Euro Area

detail.title: One Rate, Uneven Transmission: Monetary Policy after Oil Supply Shocks in the Euro Area
detail.abstract: How should the ECB respond to an adverse oil supply shock when a single monetary policy stance is transmitted unevenly across member economies? We answer this question for the EA12 by combining Bayesian Panel Local Projections with empirical counterfactuals. First, we estimate how an adverse oil supply shock propagates across member economies under the historical monetary policy response. Separately, we estimate how identified monetary policy shocks change the expected near-term monetary policy stance and macroeconomic outcomes. We then combine these responses to construct alternative common monetary policy responses while preserving country-specific transmission. This allows us to ask whether the ECB can bring headline inflation closer to its no-shock path over the medium term without raising aggregate real economic costs above those associated with its historical response. Our preferred counterfactual rule calls for a moderate front-loading of the expected near-term monetary policy stance, followed by a gradual withdrawal of the additional restraint. It improves medium-term inflation stabilization without exceeding historical aggregate real costs. These aggregate gains do not imply uniform national outcomes: countries more exposed to the initial oil shock are not necessarily those bearing greater real economic costs from the monetary policy response. Moreover, oil supply news and geopolitical oil supply shocks differ during particular phases of their propagation, yet favor similar monetary policy responses. The results show that the timing of a common monetary policy response can improve aggregate stabilization even when its transmission within the monetary union is uneven.

title: Self-Reproducing Generative Power: Dependency, Counter-Power, and Closure

detail.title: Self-Reproducing Generative Power: Dependency, Counter-Power, and Closure
detail.abstract: Power can persist through law, habit, coordination, external scarcity, or organizational inertia. A narrower mechanism appears when present exercise changes a condition of future power and that change returns as greater later power. This paper proposes the term selfreproducing generative power for that mediated return. The proposal is actor-, target-, domain-, action-, comparison-, and horizon-specific. Three candidate paths receive separate treatment. A material path runs through practical exit and dependence. A counter-power path runs through contraction of viable contestation. An institutional-legitimation path runs through justificatory assertion, audience uptake, institutional conversion, and later power. Under a local differentiable model, each path contributes a chain-rule product to the one-step power multiplier. The direct persistence term remains algebraically separate. The result measures local mediated return; multidimensional stability depends on the full Jacobian and nonlinear regime. A set-valued construction defines counter-power through efficacious actions that preserve a declared viability condition. A finite-trace countermodel then establishes that an observed trajectory of power and dependence underdetermines an endogenous return loop across unrestricted model classes. The paper therefore requires edge-specific causal evidence, plausible rivals, longitudinal-confounding analysis, and strategic-response analysis. Self-reproduction, restricted closure, domination, injustice, generativity exploitation, responsibility, and legal wrong remain separate registers. The current contribution is a revisable mechanism grammar, a conditional local derivation, an identification warning, and a comparative research programme. Empirical prevalence, historical application, normative evaluation, and legal classification remain open.

title: Generative Upwelling and Relational Transport: Formal Scope and Analogy Limits

detail.title: Generative Upwelling and Relational Transport: Formal Scope and Analogy Limits
detail.abstract: Oceanic upwelling offers a compelling image for a relational process in which changes to surrounding channels and receiving conditions make movement possible for a constrained state. Its scientific use across domains requires a stricter architecture than resemblance alone. This paper reconstructs a minimal physical source model and proposes an analogy-transfer certificate for ocean-inspired relational research. In the source domain, mass continuity under the Boussinesq approximation yields an integrated relation between vertical velocity, an upper boundary value, and horizontal divergence through the water column. A local divergence sign determines a vertical derivative; boundary data and vertical integration determine the resulting velocity. A slab Ekman relation adds wind stress and rotation, while modern coastal-upwelling research adds geostrophic transport, stratification, coastal geometry, mixing, and source-water properties. The proposed certificate records purpose, source and target models, state map, preserved relations, declared disanalogies, open correspondences, observables, comparison models, and failure conditions. Exact commutation carries source trajectories into target trajectories on a declared domain. A vocabulary map alone leaves target dynamics underdetermined. The target construction therefore defines relational upwelling independently through changes in viable receiving paths and finite-horizon access to a declared open region. Six failed mappings separate incompressibility from social conservation, depth from moral rank, buoyancy frequency from generic stability, sea surface from a critical manifold, turbulence from proximity to a tipping point, and vertical compensation from emancipation. The present result is a verified source-domain reconstruction, a heuristic analogy, and a proposed target model. Structural and empirical status remain conditional on mapping, measurement, comparison, and defeat tests.

title: Difference-Verified Bilateral Interaction and Edge Restoration for Building Change Detection in Remote Sensing Images
affiliations: Southwest Petroleum University, Baidu Zhitu Technology Co., Ltd, University of Liverpool, Southwest Petroleum University and Southwest Petroleum University

detail.title: Difference-Verified Bilateral Interaction and Edge Restoration for Building Change Detection in Remote Sensing Images
detail.abstract: Building change detection (BCD) from bi-temporal high-resolution imagery is conventionally formulated as a similarity-matching problem: bi-temporal features are aligned through attention weights derived from feature correlation, and boundaries are sharpened using generic edge priors. Both conventions are misaligned with the task. Correlation-driven attention allocates most of its mass to temporally consistent background rather than to the regions that actually differ, and edge priors extracted from single-temporal texture enhance every contour irrespective of whether it belongs to a changed object. We therefore reformulate BCD as a discrepancy-verification problem and propose BIE-EdgeNet. A temporal bilateral information exchange (TemporalBIE) module verifies discrepancies before aggregating them: an inverse-cosine-similarity difference prior converts temporal inconsistency into an explicit response map, a batch-adaptive gate attenuates weak responses arising from illumination change, sensor noise and registration error, and the screened evidence modulates bilateral cross-attention, so that interaction follows difference significance rather than similarity. A difference-guided edge fusion enhancement module (DEFEM) then recasts boundary refinement as conditioned edge restoration, in which the verified discrepancy representation determines which contours are restored into the semantic features. We further release Chengdu Change Detection (CDCD), a 2,558-pair benchmark of irregular, fragmented and pseudo-change-rich urban-renewal scenes. Against 15 representative methods under an identical protocol, BIE-EdgeNet attains the highest IoU and F1 on LEVIR-CD (84.34/91.51), WHU-CD (85.44/92.15) and CDCD (62.83/77.17); the margin is negligible on LEVIR-CD and widens with scene complexity to 1.57 IoU points on CDCD.

title: Global Material Use Targets Between Environmental Limits, Decent Living for All and Political Feasibility
affiliations: CSIRO Environment, Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK), Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation, Yale University, Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation, Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation, Government of the Commonwealth of Australia - CSIRO Health & Biosecurity,  SYSTEMIQ,  SYSTEMIQ, United Nations - Environment Programme (UNEP), Hot or Cool Institute and United Nations - Environment Programme (UNEP)

detail.title: Global Material Use Targets Between Environmental Limits, Decent Living for All and Political Feasibility
detail.abstract: Material extraction underpins economic development and human well-being but is also a major driver of greenhouse gas emissions, biodiversity loss, pollution, and resource depletion. Yet no globally agreed target for material use reconciles environmental limits with the resource requirements for decent living standards. We integrate macroeconomic, land-use, stock-flow, and multiregional input-output modelling to compare a baseline with four global transition scenarios to 2060. Despite different policy mixes, the scenarios converge on a sustainable range of approximately 107–123 billion tonnes of annual material extraction, equivalent to 9–13 tonnes per person, while substantially reducing environmental impacts. Comparing material footprints with material stocks reveals persistent trade-offs between environmental ambition and equitable development, leaving only limited scope to expand essential infrastructure in low-income countries. These findings provide a scientifically grounded reference range for global material use and support differentiated national pathways that combine environmental ambition with fairness and political feasibility.

detail.abstract: This paper uses Taylor expansions to derive innovative log-linearized versions of first-order conditions that address household behavior about indebtedness and default within a general equilibrium framework. This novel micro-founded tool is designed to monitor the evolution of a broad range of credit types in countries facing worrying scenarios. In practical terms, these revised Euler equations help restrict the admissible region of household optimal decisions based on plausible sets of preferences and credit market parameters. For example, I perform an empirical exercise comparing theoretical upper bounds with actual values for mortgage, credit card, and auto loans in the U.S. from 2001:1 to 2026:1. Americans hold nearly one-third of global household debt despite comprising just 4% of the world’s population. The recent and recurring concern of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York is consistent with the main findings reported here.

title: Recognition Networks and Value Accessibility: Detection, Constitution, and Future Opportunity

detail.title: Recognition Networks and Value Accessibility: Detection, Constitution, and Future Opportunity
detail.abstract: A contribution can remain difficult to evaluate, difficult to translate, or unable to reach the institutions that allocate future opportunities. These conditions are often compressed into the statement that value lacks recognition. This paper proposes a typed account of recognition accessibility. It separates standard-relative qualification, favorable evaluation, constituted standing, attribution, transmissible evidence, and opportunity-gate access. Recognition can detect a qualification specified under a declared standard, constitute a social or institutional status, or link both layers in a hybrid mechanism. A route decomposition distinguishes exposure, translation, judgment, and attributable transmission. Under conditionally independent evaluators, exact formulas give network sensitivity, false-positive access, and the marginal effect of another evaluator. A shared route barrier creates a strict accessibility ceiling, which separates nominal evaluator count from effective evaluator diversity. A discrete-time hazard identity represents first recognition over a finite horizon. A directed opportunity graph then defines reachable gates and a recognition cut number. Portable evidence weakly enlarges reachability and improves cut robustness only when it bypasses prior bottlenecks. Finally, a two-model construction shows that a finite recognition trace can have the same distribution under a detection model with an unobserved qualification and a constitution model without that variable. Recognition observations therefore require an explicit value ontology and discriminating evidence. Studies of academic judgment, delayed citation, novelty, and interdisciplinary funding motivate the problem while remaining tied to their own indicators and institutions. The resulting framework is a revisable conceptual model. Empirical use requires calibrated standards, dependence analysis, longitudinal network evidence, rival-mechanism tests, and separate evaluation of accuracy, distribution, participation, contestability, privacy, and institutional dependency.

title: Assessing and Redesigning an Urban Air-Quality Monitoring Network: Population-Weighted PM10 Exposure, Socioeconomic Inequality, and Monitoring Gaps in Istanbul
affiliations: , Istanbul University - Cerrahpasa, Istanbul University - Cerrahpasa and Istanbul Rumeli University

detail.title: Assessing and Redesigning an Urban Air-Quality Monitoring Network: Population-Weighted PM10 Exposure, Socioeconomic Inequality, and Monitoring Gaps in Istanbul

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Air-quality monitoring networks are routinely evaluated by where their stations stand, and rarely by whom those stations allow the network to represent. We ask who Istanbul's municipal network misses, and at what social cost. We combine 1.37 million hourly PM10 observations from 26 stations (2021-2026) with covariate-assisted regression and residual inverse-distance interpolation, dasymetrically recalibrated gridded population surfaces, and official socioeconomic registers to estimate population-weighted exposure for all 39 districts over fifteen periods, with uncertainty quantified by a 2,000-replicate station bootstrap. Twenty districts housing 48.2% of the population contain no station, and monitor access is itself socially patterned: 40% of the lowest socioeconomic quintile lives more than 5 km from any monitor, against 15% of the highest. Measured exposure is socially graded - the concentration index is negative in all fifteen periods (2024: -0.053, 95% interval -0.097 to -0.021), with the poorest quintile breathing 1.36 times the PM10 of the richest - and the gap widens in summer, consistent with quarry-dominated sources, while no gradient exists for traffic-related NO2. An equity-weighted expansion design returns 53% of the unobserved population to view with eight stations, at a cost of only 0.3 percentage points of conventional variance reduction. Monitoring networks should be assessed by the populations they represent, not by station geometry alone.

title: Three Foresight Models for Policymaking in Dynamic Economic Systems From Fixed-Path Backcasting to a Dynamic Architecture of the Future
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Three Foresight Models for Policymaking in Dynamic Economic Systems From Fixed-Path Backcasting to a Dynamic Architecture of the Future
detail.abstract: Backcasting is an established foresight method that begins with a desired future and works backward to identify the conditions and steps required to reach it. Its application to economic and other human systems, however, raises a fundamental problem: the system does not remain unchanged while a strategy is being implemented. Each intervention may alter actors' behavior, expectations, interests, power relations, coalitions, market structures, and even the mechanisms through which policy effects are transmitted. Consequently, the second stage of a strategy may be implemented in a system materially different from the one on which the original design was based. This conceptual article develops three related models to address that problem. The first, REM1, reformulates backcasting as a scenario-based, dynamic process that converts a desired future into stage objectives and requires a renewed diagnosis of reality and redesign of the next stage after every intervention. The second, REM2, shifts attention from policy instruments alone to the actors, institutions, rules, and structures capable of endogenously generating and reproducing movement toward the desired future. The third, DREM, integrates the first two models within a single architecture. The article argues that strategy in human systems must contain not only a pathway toward a desired future, but also mechanisms for causal scenario analysis, stage-gate assessment, reality reassessment, path correction, interest alignment, safeguards against rent-producing power, and the creation of endogenous engines of change. Foresight thereby becomes the architecture of a learning and self-correcting process for navigating uncertain futures, rather than the design of a fixed route.

title: Assessment of the Innovation Potential of the Republic of Bashkortostan

detail.abstract: The article assesses the innovative potential of Bashkortostan and the effectiveness of its application in the republic. The analysis is based on the statistical data of such indicators as the share of innovative products, fulfilled work and provided services in the total volume of products manufactured in the republic; the share of organisations engaged in the technological innovations; the current expenditures on research and development; the number of scientific and technical personnel in the republic year after year. It presents a description of innovative initiatives, projects and activities carried out in Bashkortostan as part of the national projects «Science and Universities», «New Health Preservation Technologies», «Infrastructure for Life», «New Materials and Chemistry», «Means of Production and Automation». The role of innovative potential in the steady development of the republic and increasing the country’s technological sovereignty has been justified.

title: The Impact of Trade Policy Uncertainty on Foreign Direct Investment Flows: Evidence from U.S.-China Relations (2016-2024)

detail.title: The Impact of Trade Policy Uncertainty on Foreign Direct Investment Flows: Evidence from U.S.-China Relations (2016-2024)
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether trade policy uncertainty (TPU), particularly changes in its volatility, is associated with bilateral foreign direct investment (FDI) between the United States and China from 2016 to 2024. Using the Baker-Bloom-Davis Trade Policy Uncertainty index and annual bilateral FDI data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis, I estimated a time-series regression. I also used annual event-study-equivalent comparisons around major trade policy shocks. A three-year rolling measure of TPU volatility is negatively and significantly associated with total bilateral FDI (coefficient =-20.05, p = .039, N = 8, 2017-2024). The coefficient remains negative when a two-year volatility window is used and when U.S.-to-China and Chinato-U.S. FDI are estimated separately. However, the small annual sample limits the precision of these estimates and the robustness tests that can be performed. Overall, the results suggest that greater volatility in trade policy uncertainty is associated with lower bilateral investment between the United States and China.

title: The Threshold That Binds First: Value Added Tax Registration Sequencing for Owner-Managed Companies in Bulgaria, 2026

detail.title: The Threshold That Binds First: Value Added Tax Registration Sequencing for Owner-Managed Companies in Bulgaria, 2026

declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. The study involves no human participants, patients, or personal data; it is a documentary analysis of published legislation and institutional guidance. No ethics approval or consent was required.

detail.abstract: Two companion papers examined what an owner-managed Bulgarian company costs to run and what can cause the arrangement to be disregarded altogether. Both were concerned with direct taxation. This paper turns to value added tax, and argues that the registration threshold on which the entire public discussion rests-€51,130 from 1 January 2026, now measured on a calendar-year basis-is, for the population that actually incorporates in Bulgaria, the last threshold to bind and frequently the only one that never binds at all. Bulgarian law contains at least four independent grounds of registration. Three of them carry figures below the headline threshold or no figure whatsoever. The ground that binds first, Article 97a, has no threshold: it is triggered by the receipt of a single service from a supplier not established in Bulgaria, is due no later than seven days before the tax becomes chargeable, and confers no right to deduct the tax the registrant is then obliged to self-assess. A company with no turnover whatsoever is registrable on the day it buys its first cloud subscription. The paper derives a closed-form condition under which voluntary full registration dominates that default: registration is the cheaper regime whenever the ratio of taxed inputs to turnover exceeds five-sixths of the share of turnover supplied to domestic final consumers. For a company selling only to business customers abroad the condition is satisfied at any positive level of input cost, which is to say always. The paper then shows that the special scheme for small enterprises introduced on 1 January 2026 under Directive (EU) 2020/285, with its €100,000 Union threshold and its EX identifier, cannot relieve this constraint, because the exemption it confers operates on supplies made while the binding obligation arises on supplies received. The reforms of 2026 are output-side reforms addressed to an input-side problem.

detail.abstract: The Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act lifts a foreign state's immunity when its act abroad causes "a direct effect in the United States." Congress never defined that phrase, and the Supreme Court has construed it only once, holding in 1992 that an effect is direct if it follows as an immediate consequence of the sovereign's act. In the vacuum, ten of the twelve courts of appeals have divided. Six require a plaintiff to identify a contractual place of performance in the United States, or a legally significant act here, before the causal question is reached. Four apply ordinary causation principles and reject any such prerequisite. The Supreme Court denied certiorari on the question in 2025, leaving the division entrenched. This Article argues that neither camp is faithful to the governing standard: the bright-line circuits add requirements the Court expressly refused to read into the text, and the causation circuits leave immediacy undisciplined. It proposes a unified three-step framework. A court identifies the sovereign's act and the obligation it breached, asks whether the American effect followed without an intervening actor or choice, and treats place of performance and legally significant acts as evidence of immediacy rather than as jurisdictional gates. Tested against decided cases, the framework preserves the results both camps reach in the canonical disputes while supplying a single question for the marginal ones. No circuit must overrule its own precedent to adopt it.

title: When the Benchmark is Already Efficient: Sheltering Without an Atom under Value-at-Risk Verification

detail.title: When the Benchmark is Already Efficient: Sheltering Without an Atom under Value-at-Risk Verification
detail.abstract: A sender is read by two audiences: an agent who responds to a posterior mean and a verifier who responds to a quantile of the same posterior. When the verifier's read is convex in the sender's beliefs it cannot be gamed, and an optimal disclosure is a single accept/reject partition-at every prior and every level of stakes. Value-at-Risk is not belief-convex, and the known failure of the guarantee is conditional: at a prior with an atom on the worst type a three-posterior disclosure beats every binary one, but only when the deterrence stake is large enough. This paper asks where the condition comes from and answers with one quantity: the liability inefficiency of the binary benchmark, the gap between the least expected read a binary disclosure can reach and the least any disclosure can reach while deterring maximally. A stake condition is unavoidable wherever that gap is nonpositive-at the atomic prior a binary disclosure already attains the global floor, so sheltering can sell nothing but deterrence, and no disclosure with any number of posteriors escapes the condition. Where the gap is positive the condition can vanish, and in the leading case it does: at a uniform prior with a median read and a compliance target below a threshold this paper computes in closed form, an explicit six-posterior disclosure attains the same deterrence as the best binary one and strictly lower liability, so it dominates every binary disclosure at every stake and every degree of leakage short of a perfect seal. This closes, in the affirmative and without an atom, a question left open in the companion paper. The mechanism is not topological: a complying pool that is an interval cannot separate its mean from its quantile, and a two-band pool can, so what a diffuse prior supplies is not disconnection but slack. Read the quantile level as a standard of proof, and the same inequality is the verifier's only guarantee: under a strict enough standard, or a demanding enough compliance target, some stakes condition is unavoidable and the verifier is safe at low stakes.

title: The Possible Use of Herbs and Spices in the Food Processing and Food Safety
affiliations: Kulumsa agricultural Research center, Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural research, Ethiopia.

detail.title: The Possible Use of Herbs and Spices in the Food Processing and Food Safety
detail.abstract: Spices and herbs are utilised in many different cuisines and food items, but they are consumed in small amounts, making them a special market within the food industry. These plants are rich sources of valuable bioactive components that are utilised for a range of functions, such as flavouring, colouring, medicinal, and preservation. The food industry recognises the potential of plant extracts, and not just because of their nutritional benefits. Antimicrobials and antioxidants, such as various essential oils with antibacterial qualities, are mostly found in plants. Herbs and spices including rosemary, sage, basil, oregano, thyme, cardamom, and clove contain a variety of essential oils. To increase product value and shelf life, plant essential oils are also included as additives to edible or biodegradable films and coatings for active food packaging. However, it is important to consider and thoroughly research any potential harmful consequences of specific phyto-compounds. However, this chapter's findings are more comprehensive, represent significant and timely advances towards potential applications in food sector as well as the food safety aspects of commodities containing spices and herbs by effectively protecting consumers from potential risks resulting from unintentional or intentional contamination of spices and herbs.

title: Quantum Field Theory and VIX Dynamics: Implications for Establishing a VIX Microstructure Systemic Risk Management System

detail.title: Quantum Field Theory and VIX Dynamics: Implications for Establishing a VIX Microstructure Systemic Risk Management System
detail.abstract: This paper is the third in a series applying physics-inspired formalisms to VIX microstructure for systemic-risk analysis. Paper I described the microstructure's instantaneous state — entropy, enthalpy, effective temperature, and Gibbs free energy computed from a single snapshot of the term-structure curve. Paper II described how a single such state evolves, modeling the curve as a normalized ”financial wave function” advancing under a Schrödinger-type equation. Both share a structural limitation of single-particle quantum mechanics: a fixed set of contracts, a conserved ”particle number.” This paper instead recasts the microstructure as a field φ(T,t) with a variable number of degrees of freedom — contracts are created and destroyed at listing and expiry — governed by a Euclidean action with curvature, mass, and quartic self-interaction terms. This paper completes a three-paper arc—from equilibrium thermodynamics (Paper I) to wave mechanics (Paper II)—by recasting the VIX Microstructure as a quantum field. We define the deviation field φ(T,t)=lnF(T,t)-lnF0(T,t) over the maturity continuum, decompose it via the Karhunen–Loève expansion—which we prove is mathematically identical to the mode decomposition of a Gaussian free field—and construct a Fock space of occupation numbers nk(t)=qk2/λk for each excitation mode. Roll events and shock repricings are interpreted as creation–annihilation events. We estimate the propagator (mode lifetimes, cross-maturity information cone with finite propagation speed), the renormalization group flow under Wilsonian coarse-graining (showing higher-order modes—curvature and beyond—are irrelevant operators, providing the first field-theoretic explanation for why three-factor term-structure models suffice), and an Onsager–Machlup effective potential whose double-well structure (contango/backwardation attractors separated by a barrier) allows a Kramers tunneling rate that quantifies—rather than merely illustrates—the ”financial quantum tunneling” identified qualitatively in Paper II. All layers integrate into a five-layer systemic-risk confirmation framework.
