Through academic performativity literature and empirical evidence from an interview study among Finnish climate modellers working in state research institutes, we ask how climate models could be understood as performative, that is to say, how climate models participate in bringing out the future. Focusing on a specific example of changed model calculation methods, the paper examines the reception of the change in the related policy realm, and discusses how such changes might reverberate back to the model, modelling, and their politics, and thus affect models’ plausibility as authoritative future-making tools.

title: Towards Information-Theoretically Constrained Channel Attention: An Entropy Regularization Approach for Consistent Medical Image Classification
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Independent Researcher

detail.title: Towards Information-Theoretically Constrained Channel Attention: An Entropy Regularization Approach for Consistent Medical Image Classification
detail.abstract: Class-wise inconsistency in Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE)-based convolutional neural networks can limit reliable performance in medical image classification, particularly when channel attention becomes overly concentrated on dominant features. This work introduces entropy regularization applied directly to SE channel re-weighting vectors as a mathematically grounded constraint for improving class-wise consistency. To our knowledge, this approach has not previously been explored. Rather than modifying the underlying architectures or performing architecture-specific optimization, we investigate whether entropy regularization can be incorporated into native SE mechanisms. Two formulations are introduced and evaluated: a softmax-gated variant (Ent_SE) and a decoupled sigmoid variant (Ent_Dec_SE) that preserves the original SE forward pass while applying the entropy constraint through an auxiliary normalized distribution. The concept is assessed across nine model--dataset scenarios spanning three backbone architectures and three medical imaging dataset conditions, using 15-seed averaging as the primary evaluation protocol and a 25-seed Welch t-test analysis for statistical validation. Ent_Dec_SE improves class-wise F1 consistency in five of the nine scenarios, with the most consistent benefits observed on EfficientNet-B0 and the strongest individual improvement observed on ResNet-3stages. In the BloodMNIST--EfficientNet-B0 validation case, Ent_Dec_SE significantly reduces per-class F1 standard deviation (p=0.031) without a statistically significant accuracy difference (p=0.057) relative to standard SE. The softmax formulation consistently underperforms the standard SE formulation across the evaluated scenarios, supporting the theoretical concern that softmax normalization may conflict with the original scaling semantics of SE. These results establish entropy regularization of SE channel weights as a viable concept for further investigation, particularly through architecture-specific tuning and selective block-level application

title: VaR Defects and Wasserstein Stability of Comonotonic Insurance Aggregation
affiliations: Tokyo University of Science

detail.title: VaR Defects and Wasserstein Stability of Comonotonic Insurance Aggregation
detail.abstract: Comonotonic aggregation is a standard conservative benchmark under dependence uncertainty, but convex-order extremality does not quantify portfolio-specific error. For integrable losses and positive exposure weights, we define an all-level value-at-risk (VaR) defect equal to half the one-dimensional Wasserstein distance between the weighted aggregate and its comonotonic counterpart. In copula space, a weight-adapted quadratic cost yields an exact Pythagorean decomposition and a rigidity identity: the corresponding normalized rank-scale defect equals half the squared normalized distance to the comonotonic copula plus a nonnegative endpoint-slack term. Together with a component-ordering result, these identities yield a necessary endpoint-localization property for near-equality sequences, a partial converse under an exact support condition, and a sharper universal $W_2$ upper bound. For nonnegative losses, the aggregate defect $\Delta_w$ is also the exact worst-case error in expected payments over monotone non-expansive indemnity schedules and bounds the optimization regret of contracts selected under the comonotonic benchmark. Tail-localized certificates follow for integrable losses, and DKW-based finite-sample certificates are obtained under bounded support. Numerical illustrations evaluate the geometry, regret bound, and upper-tail bounds, including unbounded lognormal margins; a discrete assignment calculation independently checks the projection identity on finite empirical measures.

title: Beyond Predictive Performance: A Multi-Criteria Evaluation of Feature Selection Algorithms for Diabetes Prediction
affiliations: University of Huddersfield and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Beyond Predictive Performance: A Multi-Criteria Evaluation of Feature Selection Algorithms for Diabetes Prediction
detail.abstract: Background: Feature-selection algorithms in clinical machine learning are commonly compared using predictive performance alone, overlooking whether selected features are reproducible, consistent with model explanations, and supported by clinical evidence.Objective: To develop and evaluate a multi-criteria framework for comparing feature-selection algorithms beyond predictive performance.Methods: Fourteen feature-selection algorithms were evaluated across five publicly available diabetes datasets. Each algorithm was assessed using baseline fitness improvement, rank stability under resampling, rank-biased overlap with SHAP and permutation feature-importance rankings, and an nDCG-based clinical alignment score derived from a literature-based reference set. Entropy–CRITIC weighting and TOPSIS were used to integrate the criteria, and Monte Carlo perturbation of criterion weights was used to assess ranking robustness.Results: Predictive gain provided the least discrimination among algorithms, whereas stability was the most discriminative criterion across all dataset groupings. Recursive Feature Elimination achieved the most balanced overall performance and ranked first in the overall, clinical, and small-dataset evaluations. Univariate filter methods performed better in the large and questionnaire-based dataset groupings. Robustness analysis also showed that several favourable static TOPSIS rankings were sensitive to changes in criterion weights.Conclusions: Feature-selection methods in healthcare should be evaluated as a multi-objective problem rather than selected solely by predictive gain. Joint consideration of stability, explanation agreement, and clinical alignment provides a more informative basis for selecting methods, although further validation on higher-dimensional and prospectively collected clinical datasets is required.

title: Joint Exclusivity
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Joint Exclusivity
detail.abstract: We introduce \emph{joint exclusivity} (JE), a flexible extension of mutual exclusivity for non-negative random vectors that prohibits only the simultaneous positivity of all $n$ components. Unlike mutual exclusivity, JE admits a broad class of marginals while retaining a sharp existence criterion. We prove that a JE random vector with prescribed marginals $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ exists if and only if\[\sum_{i=1}^n \F_i(0)\le n-1.\]We also provide a canonical face-based construction with freely specified copulas within each face, and show that the trivariate case can elegantly be reduced to a one-parameter family. Finally, we extend the framework through Wang-type distortions and an $m$-exclusivity hierarchy interpolating between mutual exclusivity and JE.

title: Learning Wake Perturbations of Floating Wind Turbines Using Motion-Conditioned Neural Network
affiliations: Norwegian University of Life Sciences, Norwegian University of Life Sciences, Oslo and Akershus University College - Oslo Metropolitan University, Norwegian University of Life Sciences, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Norwegian University of Life Sciences

detail.title: Learning Wake Perturbations of Floating Wind Turbines Using Motion-Conditioned Neural Network
detail.abstract: Platform motion in floating offshore wind turbines alters wake recovery and coherent structures. High-fidelity CFD can resolve these effects, but repeated simulations remain computationally expensive. In direct full-field surrogate prediction, motion-induced wake changes are learned together with the dominant fixed-wake background, making them less explicit. Here, wake prediction is formulated as a perturbation-learning problem by decomposing the moving-turbine wake into a time-resolved fixed-turbine reference wake and a motion-induced perturbation. A motion-conditioned recurrent neural network predicts this perturbation from fixed-wake and perturbation histories together with motion type, amplitude, Strouhal number, and phase. The moving wake is reconstructed by adding the predicted perturbation to the fixed-reference wake. The method is evaluated using high-fidelity CFD simulations of a model floating wind turbine undergoing prescribed pitch and roll motions. Compared with direct moving-wake prediction, the perturbation formulation reduces normalized velocity-deficit RMSE by 49.1% for representative cases and wake-center error by 43.6%. Because the same fixed-reference wake is used in reconstruction, the perturbation-error reduction carries to the reconstructed wake. The predicted fields identify where platform motion modifies wake deficit, shear-layer structure, recovery, and displacement. Lower errors are also obtained for velocity profiles, maximum deficit, and wake width, supporting a more accurate and interpretable wake-reconstruction approach.

title: Generalized Deviatiles: A Risk-Sensitive Measure for CharacterizingHeterogeneous Extreme Risks
affiliations: Zhejiang Sci-Tech University, Zhejiang Sci-Tech University, Anhui Medical University and University of Science and Technology of China (USTC)

detail.title: Generalized Deviatiles: A Risk-Sensitive Measure for CharacterizingHeterogeneous Extreme Risks
detail.abstract: This paper develops generalized deviatiles as a new class of risk-sensitive tail-risk measures forcharacterizing heterogeneous extreme-loss structures. Unlike conventional tail measures that summarize risks mainly through a quantile threshold or an average exceedance loss, generalized deviatilesincorporate information on the magnitude and dispersion of extreme deviations, providing a richercharacterization of tail-risk profiles. The proposed framework introduces a sensitivity parameter thatallows different degrees of emphasis to be placed on severe losses according to risk preferences. Inparticular, generalized deviatiles complement conventional tail measures by revealing heterogeneousfeatures of extreme-loss structures that may not be distinguished by Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES) alone.We establish the asymptotic properties of generalized deviatile estimators under heavy-tailed distributions and extend the estimation framework to financial loss processes with serial dependence.Simulation studies evaluate the finite-sample accuracy and uncertainty quantification of the proposedprocedures across different tail environments and sensitivity levels. An empirical analysis using S&P500 Index losses demonstrates that generalized deviatiles provide additional information on markettail-risk profiles complementary to conventional VaR and ES measures. The results show that theproposed measure provides a richer representation of extreme uncertainty, which can complementexisting risk-aware decision models by improving the information available for operational and managerial decisions

title: Online Adaptive Physics-Guided Neural Network for Ship Motion Modeling under Limited Maneuvering Data
affiliations: Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan University of Technology and Wuhan University of Technology

detail.title: Online Adaptive Physics-Guided Neural Network for Ship Motion Modeling under Limited Maneuvering Data
detail.abstract: Accurate ship motion modeling is essential for navigation decision-making and model-based control. However, ship motion models constructed from limited maneuvering data often suffer from degraded prediction accuracy when the operating conditions are not represented in the training data. To address this problem, we propose an adaptive physics-guided neural network (PGNN) framework, in which an offline prior PGNN is combined with adaptive model updating under changing operating conditions. The offline prior PGNN is constructed using a parametric ship motion model and limited initial maneuvering data. Based on this prior model, newly available measurements are incorporated sequentially, and a multi-step rollout prediction error is used to detect model mismatch, trigger model updates, and regulate the adaptation process. This method is evaluated using data collected from ship maneuvering tests, including a random-maneuver dataset and three independent turning-maneuver datasets. Compared with the least-squares-based MMG identification (LS-MMG), LSTM, and Offline-PGNN, Online-PGNN reduces the mean 20-s final displacement error (FDE) by 56.0%, 63.0%, and 54.5%, respectively. The results show that the accepted model updates consistently reduce multi-step prediction error under the tested operating conditions not represented in the training set.

title: Belief-Robust Contracts
affiliations: Georgia Institute of Technology - School of Economics

detail.title: Belief-Robust Contracts
detail.abstract: This paper develops a general framework for analyzing robust contractingproblems in which (i) the principal and the agent do not share common prior be-liefs about the production technology; (ii) the agent faces first-order uncertaintyabout the distribution of output or the principal faces second-order uncertaintyabout the agent’s beliefs about the distribution of output; and (iii) uncertainparties use robust decision making criteria. The agent’s utility function is linear,he is protected by limited liability, and his belief set is rich. We allow for but donot require the principal to be herself uncertain about the production technology,we do not impose common knowledge of expected output or any other momentrestrictions, and our most general result allows for the relationship between theagent’s beliefs and the principal’s beliefs to be arbitrary. Optimal contractsare linear bonus contracts of the form w(y) = max(αy + β, 0), where y denotesoutput and α, β are constants.

reference: “Arbitration in the Digital Age: Technological Innovations in Chinese Centers,” in Richard Bales & Dan Xie, eds., The Cambridge Handbook of Arbitration in China (Cambridge University Press, forthcoming spring 2027).
title: Arbitration in the Digital Age: Technological Innovations in Chinese Centers
affiliations: Peking University - Peking University Law School

detail.title: Arbitration in the Digital Age: Technological Innovations in Chinese Centers

publicationDetails.detailsText: “Arbitration in the Digital Age: Technological Innovations in Chinese Centers,” in Richard Bales & Dan Xie, eds., The Cambridge Handbook of Arbitration in China (Cambridge University Press, forthcoming spring 2027).

detail.abstract: This chapter examines the accelerating digital transformation of commercial arbitration in China, with particular attention to online arbitration, online dispute resolution platforms, blockchain applications, and emerging uses of artificial intelligence by Chinese arbitration centers. It traces the development of online arbitration before and during the COVID-19 pandemic, explains how major institutions have incorporated digital procedures into their arbitration rules and proprietary platforms, and analyzes recent technological initiatives at institutions including CIETAC, BAC/BIAC, SCIA, GZAC, and SHIAC. The chapter gives particular attention to the use of AI for case filing, legal-information retrieval, translation, transcription, evidence management, issue identification, and assistance with award drafting, while emphasizing the emerging principle that AI should assist rather than replace human adjudicators. It also considers continuing challenges involving confidentiality, data security, ethical boundaries, reliability, and disparities in institutional technological capacity. Taken together, these developments show how technology is becoming an integral component of arbitration administration in China and provide a useful comparative reference point for other jurisdictions considering how digital tools can improve efficiency and access while preserving procedural legitimacy and human decision-making.

title: One-Shot Crowd Counting With Density Guidance For Scene Adaptation
affiliations: University of Science and Technology of China (USTC), Northwestern Polytechnical University, Northwestern Polytechnical University, The University of Sydney, Nanjing University of Science and Technology and Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

detail.title: One-Shot Crowd Counting With Density Guidance For Scene Adaptation

keywords.keywords: Scene adaptationLocal-to-global density guidanceOne-shot learningCrowd counting

detail.abstract: Crowd scenes captured by cameras at different locations vary greatly, and existing crowd counting models have limited generalization for unseen surveillance scenes. To improve the generalization of the model, we regard different surveillance scenes as different category scenes, and introduce few-shot learning to make the model adapt to the unseen surveillance scene that belongs to the given exemplar category scene. To this end, we propose to leverage local and global density characteristics to guide the model of crowd counting for unseen surveillance scenes. Specifically, to enable the model to adapt to the varying density variations in the target surveillance scene, we propose the multiple local density learner to learn multi prototypes which represent different density distributions in the support scene. Subsequently, these multiple local density similarity matrixes are encoded. And they are utilized to guide the model in a local way. To further adapt to the global density in the target surveillance scene, the global density features are extracted from the support image, then it is used to guide the model in a global way. Experiments on three datasets shows that the proposed method can adapt to unseen surveillance scenes and outperform recent state-of-the-art methods in the few-shot crowd counting.

title: Post-Quantum Security Architecture for AI-Enabled Implantable and Wearable Medical Devices

detail.title: Post-Quantum Security Architecture for AI-Enabled Implantable and Wearable Medical Devices

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The author has no personal or financial relationships with any organizations that could have influenced this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, animals, or patient data. All data used in this research were obtained from publicly available datasets (BUSI - Breast Ultrasound Images Dataset). Therefore, no ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Combining AI with products that are wearable or implanted by the patient has resulted in a generation of connected therapeutics that continuously sense the body, onboard AI-based algorithms to make inferences, and ultimately actuate on the body. This clinical improvement has seen an increase in the size of the cryptographic attack surface, and the onset of quantum computers capable of cryptographically relevant computation poses new challenges to current mechanisms-such as those based on elliptic curves and RSA cryptography-that secure these devices. Once quantum capability evolves, patient data collected today may someday be decrypted at a later date, as is often called, harvest-now-decrypt-later, and implantable and wearable devices usually are in clinical use for 10 years or more. This review combines recent advances in post-quantum cryptography (PQC), lightweight cryptographic engineering and security of medical devices with the power, memory and latency limitations of implantable and wearable MEMS and sensors, proposing a layered postquantum security architecture applicable to devices in this context. A comparative technical analysis of NIST-standardised algorithms (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA) with regards to classical asymmetric cryptography is combined with a structured narrative review of 35 peer-reviewed and standards sources, mainly published in the last seven years (2019 to 2026). The study reveals that lattice-based key encapsulation mechanisms along with hybrid classical/post-quantum handshakes, cryptographic agility, and edge-assisted offloading of heavy workloads, are a feasible approach to quantum resilience without unnecessarily high energy costs. Thus, a proposed architecture moves trust from device to gateway, and from gateway to cloud-AI layers while implementing federated learning protections to ensure model updates are not used for and to protect against inference and poisoning attacks. The major problems that still remain are limited energy budgets, the assurance of firmware updates, regulatory uncertainty, and underdeveloped post-quantum cryptanalysis. The review ends by emphasising the need for proactive, crypto-agile design, well ahead of any capacity to massively decrypt quantum computers.

title: Vector Quantized Variational Auto-Encoder with a Mixture of Curved Geometries
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Southeast University

detail.title: Vector Quantized Variational Auto-Encoder with a Mixture of Curved Geometries
detail.abstract: The Vector Quantized Variational Auto-Encoder (VQ-VAE) has established a strong paradigm for learning compact discrete latent representations. Existing methods typically impose a single geometric prior on the latent space. Such a design is insufficient for real-world data with heterogeneous geometric structures and cannot fully exploit the complementary properties of different geometries. To fill this gap, we propose VQ-VAE with a mixture of curved geometries (McVQ-VAE), which models the discrete latent space as a mixture of curved geometries. Specifically, we develop a multi-branch architecture in which each branch learns a codebook under a specific geometric prior. The branch-wise codebooks form a product space that can encompass hyperspherical, hyperbolic, and Euclidean components. We formulate a Riemannian optimization scheme to update the codewords within their respective manifolds. Experiments on image reconstruction with both convolutional and Vision Transformer (ViT) backbones, together with evaluations on speech reconstruction benchmarks, show that McVQ-VAE consistently outperforms VQ-based baselines. Further analysis highlights the benefits of McVQ-VAE, including high codebook usage, improved representation quality, and generation performance. The source code will be released at https://github.com/Aya-Chriskey/McVQ-VAE}{https://github.com/Aya-Chriskey/McVQ-VAE.

title: Dynamic Hard-Routing Fusion via Discrete Expert Selection for Infrared and Visible Images
affiliations: Jilin University of Finance and Economics, Jilin University of Finance and Economics, Jilin University of Finance and Economics, Jilin University of Finance and Economics and Jilin University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Dynamic Hard-Routing Fusion via Discrete Expert Selection for Infrared and Visible Images
detail.abstract: Infrared and visible image fusion seeks to combine thermal radiation with texture details into a single high-quality image. Existing autoencoder-based methods typically adopt dense fusion strategies that treat every spatial location equally. This ignores the differing information content across modalities and often yields suboptimal results.We propose a plug-and-play Hard-Routing Fusion Head (HRF) and a Magnitude-Aware Gated Residual (MAGR) decoder. The encoder uses a Transformer with invertible neural network (INN) modules to decouple features into base and detail components. For each component, we construct three semantic experts: copy infrared, copy visible, and attention fusion. A lightweight router with Gumbel-Softmax and a straight-through estimator selects the most suitable expert per pixel, enabling discrete decisions while preserving end-to-end differentiability. The MAGR decoder dynamically gates residual connections based on feature energy, suppressing noise in flat areas and preserving sharpness at edges. A two-stage training strategy with load balancing and entropy regularization ensures stable routing.Experiments on TNO, MSRS, and M3FD show that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in both quantitative metrics and visual quality. The routing probability maps also offer pixel-level interpretability of fusion decisions.

title: Finite-Size Spectral Deconvolution: Correcting Free Probability by Damped Inversion of the Exact Forward Map
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Finite-Size Spectral Deconvolution: Correcting Free Probability by Damped Inversion of the Exact Forward Map
detail.abstract: Additive spectral deconvolution—recovering the spectrum of a signal matrix S from a noisy observation S+N—underlies covariance estimation, kernel and Gram-matrix denoising, and learned weight matrices. The standard tool, free probability, is an n→∞ limit, biased at the finite sizes (n ≈ 10²–10³) typical of machine learning. We propose FinDeconv, which warm-starts at the free-probability solution and takes a few damped fixed-point steps against the exact finite-n forward map: the first step removes free probability's deterministic bias; iterating overfits the single noisy observation, so few steps are principled. Supporting theory: the forward map's Jacobian is doubly stochastic—its mean mode contracts at an exact rate while the remaining modes sit at the stability boundary, a spectral account of early stopping; a Gaussian–Poincaré bound gives Var ≤ σ²/n, hence a risk bound; and eigenvalue rigidity yields a derived O(n−1+ε) bias bound matching the measured ≈1/n decay. On structured spectra FinDeconv shrinks 1-Wasserstein error to as little as 0.20× that of free deconvolution (over n = 16–2048), by 62–72% on semi-synthetic MNIST and CIFAR-10, and wins all 25 organic-noise cells (low-precision quantization round-off, known floor only); on featureless bulks it is neutral at small n and wins at n ≥ 1024. Versus state-of-the-art denoisers it is a division of labor, not a categorical win: best for the spectrum on smooth, low-SNR signals, while a rotational-invariant estimator wins spiky/low-rank spectra and matrix reconstruction. It is robust to non-Gaussian, wrong-shape, and under-estimated noise, fails under multiplicative (Wishart) noise, and degrades gracefully as n grows.

title: Re-examining signal decomposition in ultra-short-term offshore wind power forecasting with uncertainty quantification
affiliations: Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University and Zhejiang University

detail.title: Re-examining signal decomposition in ultra-short-term offshore wind power forecasting with uncertainty quantification
detail.abstract: Accurate offshore wind power forecasting is essential for grid dispatch and secure operation under variable marine conditions, yet widely used offline mode decomposition may leak future information and overestimate performance. This paper proposes a leakage-free probabilistic ultra-short-term forecasting framework based on rolling-window CEEMDAN. At each forecasting origin, only the available historical window is decomposed, and recent modal components are encoded as auxiliary tokens. A BiLSTM backbone produces multi-step base forecasts that guide cross-attention fusion with the CEEMDAN tokens, while residual gating further refines the predictions. An IQN-inspired head is employed for conditional quantile estimation. Experiments on two operational offshore wind farm datasets with 15-min resolution show that the proposed method achieves the best deterministic performance, with RMSE/MAE of 12.46/7.33 MW on Farm A and 17.45/9.95 MW on Farm B. Compared with the best-performing deep learning baseline, the MAE is reduced by 7.71-15.07% across four forecast steps on Farm A and by 1.10-11.88% on Farm B. Probabilistic results show that the proposed method can generate reliable prediction intervals, with 95% prediction interval coverage probabilities of 93.07% and 93.00% on Farm A and Farm B, respectively. These findings support more reliable forecasting and risk-aware operation of offshore wind farms.

title: MPCGFNet: A Multi-Path Context Graph Fusion Network for Underwater Object Detection​
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: MPCGFNet: A Multi-Path Context Graph Fusion Network for Underwater Object Detection​
detail.abstract: Underwater object detection remains a challenging task due to the color distortion, poor visibility, light scattering, blur and huge object scale variation. These factors often lead to a performance degradation of conventional object detection frameworks when they are deployed in complex underwater environments. To address these challenges,this paper proposes MPCGFNet, a novel underwater object detection framework designed to enhance feature representation and contextual understanding. The architecture consists of four dedicated modules which are Multi-Path Hierarchical Context (MPHC) block for extracting multi-path hierarchical features, the Edge-aware Context Aggregation and Fusion (ECAF) block for edge-aware feature refinement and adaptive fusion, the Windowed Patch Graph Aggregation (WPGA) block for graph-based local contextual modeling and the Multi-Scale Context Gating (MSCG) block for adaptive multi-scale feature integration. These modules are jointly integrated within the backbone and neck of the detection framework to improve robustness against underwater degradations while enhancing object localization and classification accuracy. Extensive experiments conducted on the RUOD, TrashCan-Instance and TrashCan-Material datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. MPCGFNET achieves, 65.47% mAP, 87.63% AP50 and 72.07% AP75 on the RUOD dataset, outperforming several state-of-the-art underwater object detectors. Furthermore, the proposed model attains 51.21% mAP, 69.93% AP50 on the TrashCan-Instance dataset and 44.23% mAP, 64.12% AP50 on the TrashCan-Material dataset. The results demonstrate that MPCGFNet provides a robust and effective solution for underwater object detection in challenging marine environments.

title: Foreground-Background Disentanglement with Stochastic Masks for Fine-Grained Visual Classification
affiliations: Xidian University, Xidian University, Xidian University and Xidian University

detail.title: Foreground-Background Disentanglement with Stochastic Masks for Fine-Grained Visual Classification
detail.abstract: Recent advances in self‑supervised contrastive learning have demonstrated significant potential for fine‑grained visual classification by learning to align positive pairs while separating negative ones. However, prevailing methods often struggle with accurately localizing subtle foreground regions and tend to over‑fit to background cues, limiting their robustness in real‑world scenarios. To overcome these limitations, we propose a Stochastic Mask‑driven Disentangled Contrastive Learning (SMDCL) framework. At its heart lies a Saliency‑Aware Differential Augmentation (SADA) strategy, which first localizes discriminative foreground regions via a stochastic masking process and then synthesizes augmented positive samples by preserving the identified foreground while substituting the background with highly dissimilar ones from other images. This forces the model to learn foreground‑invariant representations under diverse contextual variations. Additionally, a Cross‑View Attention (CVA) module is integrated to capture semantically consistent regions across different views of the same image, providing complementary intra‑sample consistency signals. These components are optimized jointly under a unified Foreground‑Invariant Learning (FIL) loss, which aligns the augmented samples in the embedding space while reinforcing their focus on cross‑view consistent foreground regions.Comprehensive experiments on CUB‑200‑2011, Stanford Cars, and Aircraft datasets validate the effectiveness of our approach. The proposed SMDCL framework consistently outperforms existing self‑supervised methods under both linear evaluation and image retrieval protocols, demonstrating its superior ability to learn discriminative and robust visual representations without manual annotations.

reference: ECB Working Paper No. 2026/3277
title: Learning probability of default and stress testing
affiliations: European Central Bank (ECB) and

detail.title: Learning probability of default and stress testing
detail.abstract: We analyze the Probability of Default (PD) of non-financial corporations in Europe using Random Forests (RF) and assess implications for stress testing the banking sector. To this end, we exploit data on firms’ financial statements (Orbis) and banks’ credit registry (Anacredit). We show that RF displays stronger risk sensitivity than logistic regression in stress testing, shedding new light on the non-linear effect of scenario severity on PD. Moreover, we show how RF-based PD can be used in a network of banks and firms to stress test the banking sector through loan exposures as a key transmission channel of adverse scenarios. A granular inspection of banks’ riskiness indices derived from this network sheds light also on RF’s superior ability in capturing non-linearity thanks to its capability in identifying “tail banks”. Our work is relevant for central banks and banking supervisors alike.

title: Beyond Class Tokens: LLM-guided Dominant Property Mining for Few-shot Classification
affiliations: Shenzhen University, Shenzhen University, Shenzhen University, Shenzhen University and Shenzhen University

detail.title: Beyond Class Tokens: LLM-guided Dominant Property Mining for Few-shot Classification
detail.abstract: Few-shot Learning (FSL) aims to generalize recognition capabilities to novel classes using only a few labeled samples. Recent CLIP-based approaches have made significant strides by aligning global visual representations with class-name text embeddings. However, this reliance on a single global "class token" often overlooks the visual diversity and fine-grained local details essential for discriminating between novel categories, leading to a "fine-grained alignment deficiency." To address this, we propose BCT-CLIP, a framework designed to explore dominating properties Beyond conventional Class Tokens. Our approach shifts the focus from global-only alignment to a multi-attribute structured representation. The core of BCT-CLIP consists of three key components: (1) a Multi-Property Generator (MPG) that produces patch-aware visual property tokens by interacting trainable queries with image patch features; (2) an LLM-informed retrieval pipeline that utilizes clustering and vision-guided pruning to distill faithful and dominant property descriptions from redundant large language model outputs; and (3) a one-to-one contrastive learning strategy that aligns these visual property tokens with their corresponding refined text descriptions. Finally, a Hybrid Cache Model is employed to integrate both global category information and fine-grained property features for classification. Extensive evaluations across 11 standard benchmarks demonstrate that BCT-CLIP consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, validating the effectiveness of property-level mining in enhancing few-shot generalization.

title: The Malagasy Health System: A Stag Hunt Game Approach
affiliations: Department of Economics, University of Antananarivo

detail.title: The Malagasy Health System: A Stag Hunt Game Approach

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required because the study did not involve the recruitment of human participants or the collection of identifiable personal data. The analysis relies on secondary data and publicly available sources.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.
declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: Not applicable. This study is not a clinical trial.

detail.abstract: This article models the Malagasy health system as a stag hunt involving three actors: the State, health workers, and citizens. Its central claim is that universal health coverage is not merely a financing challenge but also an equilibrium-selection problem. A high-quality cooperative equilibrium emerges when the State adequately finances, organizes, and governs public health services, health workers maintain professional effort within the public sector, and citizens contribute to and use the collective system. This equilibrium is represented by the stag. Conversely, when each actor expects the others to defect, individually rational exit strategies become dominant, represented by the hare. These include public underfunding, migration or private practice by health workers, self-medication, bypassing public services, direct recourse to private providers, and informal payments. The model first develops an asymmetric binary game and then extends it to continuous institutional effort. It identifies two pure-strategy equilibria, a mixed equilibrium defining a confidence threshold, distinct basins of attraction, and the mechanisms through which public policy modifies strategic incentives. The Madagascar application draws on available evidence concerning health expenditure, financial protection, geographic access, workforce density, essential service coverage, and national planning documents. The simulations are not intended to estimate the system's deep parameters causally. Instead, they offer a transparent, reproducible, and interpretable calibration for comparing reform scenarios. The analysis shows that effective health policy must simultaneously increase the visible returns to the public system, reduce incentives for non-solidary private exit, and protect early cooperators from bearing the risks of collective action alone.

title: A Systemic Risk Framework for the Vietnamese Market: a Composite Risk Index and Financial Stress Prediction
affiliations: and WorldQuant University

detail.title: A Systemic Risk Framework for the Vietnamese Market: a Composite Risk Index and Financial Stress Prediction
detail.abstract: In this study, we introduce the Vietnam Systemic Risk Index (VSRI), the first multi-dimensional composite index for the Vietnamese market, achieving an out-of-sample ROC-AUC of 0.77 and 75% recall in predicting financial stress events. This analysis fills a gap in the current research on systemic risk for the Vietnamese market, where, to the best of our knowledge, a multi-dimensional unified measure of systemic risk is still missing. Our VSRI framework integrates five dimensions of financial risk: external spillovers; domestic market fragility; financial turbulence; risk of downside tail co-movements; and market illiquidity. We provide empirical support for the economic validity of the VSRI, showing that it aligns with well-known periods of financial distress. We also demonstrate its ability to capture periods of increased systemic risk across latent market regimes and its capacity to bring incremental information about the buildup of risk beyond the information already contained in more conventional stress proxies. Furthermore, our machine learning analysis provides empirical evidence that the VSRI may contain useful signals for systemic stress prediction. The results of the study provide evidence that the VSRI can be a useful tool for Vietnamese financial regulators and policymakers, providing an operational framework able to quantify the current level of systemic risk and identify the main drivers of systemic vulnerability, thus informing risk management and financial policy decision-making.

title: Inherited State, New Flow, and Intraday Volatility in SPX 0DTE Options
affiliations: Independent Student Researcher

detail.title: Inherited State, New Flow, and Intraday Volatility in SPX 0DTE Options

declarations.funderStatement: Massive (previously Polygon.io) and ThetaData provided some complimentary data. I had to upgrade my ThetaData subscription and paid out of pocket for some data.

detail.abstract: This paper studies whether a quote-classified SPX option-flow gamma state contains distinct inherited-state and newly arriving-flow information about subsequent intraday realized variance. The one-minute panel contains 286,125 observations across 735 trading days from January 3, 2023 through December 5, 2025. Both the inherited state and signed innovation are negative across the locked 5-, 15-, and 30-minute family, but chronological performance improves in 2024 and reverses in 2025, preventing a clean forecast-timing interpretation and reinforcing the broader multiple-lead caveat. Broad MVC attraction is not supported. Non-0DTE evidence also prevents a mechanism unique to same-day expiration. The measure is vendor-Greek-based flow-GEX, not observed dealer inventory, hedge trading, or textbook dollar gamma.

title: Dynamic Charging Policies for Residential Electric Vehicles: A Structural Analysis
affiliations: Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR), Erasmus School of Economics (ESE), Students, Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR) - Erasmus School of Economics (ESE) and Econometric Institute, Erasmus University,  Rotterdam (EUR) - Erasmus School of Economics

detail.title: Dynamic Charging Policies for Residential Electric Vehicles: A Structural Analysis
detail.abstract: Problem Definition: Dynamic electricity tariffs give households an incentive to shift electric-vehicle charging across hours and days. Charging tonight can take advantage of favorable prices and reduce the need for public charging after a long trip. Waiting may offer cheaper future charging and avoid the fixed cost of initiating a session. Charging-rate limits and overnight price differences generate a convex procurement cost, which we call the price stack. Energy can be carried across days while travel and future prices remain uncertain. We study a household that chooses its departure state of charge (SOC) each evening based on the arrival SOC, the current price stack, and forecasts of future prices. Methodology/Results: We formulate the problem as a finite-horizon Markov decision process with stochastic trip demand and characterize the optimal charging policy. We show that the decision separates into whether to charge and how much to charge. The household charges when a charging margin exceeds the fixed home-charging cost, while the conditional target depends on the price stack and the marginal value of stored energy. We identify conditions under which the charging region has a threshold structure and show that, under a flat tariff, the policy has a forecast-dependent (s,S) structure. We construct instances with disconnected charging regions and show that restricting the household to no charging or full charging can break the threshold structure even when the unrestricted policy has one. Finally, replacing the distribution of future price curves by its mean curve can overstate optimal expected cost. Managerial Implications: Smart-charging systems can benefit from allowing charging amounts to adapt to the vehicle's SOC and overnight price conditions rather than imposing full-or-nothing charging. Single-threshold charging rules should be used only when the conditions supporting such a structure are satisfied. Forecast systems should preserve the distribution of future price curves rather than replace it with a mean curve.

title: Tribal Agriculture in Arizona: An Economic Contribution Analysis
affiliations: , , University of Arizona, University of Arizona and University of Arizona

detail.title: Tribal Agriculture in Arizona: An Economic Contribution Analysis
detail.abstract: This report provides a systematic profile of tribal agriculture using the best publicly available data and methods. We conduct a comprehensive benchmark of tribal agriculture’s economic contribution in Arizona, the first to our knowledge. The main goal of this report is to serve as a foundation for future research, improved understanding, and more refined analyses over time. The report does not quantify other critical values of tribal agricultural production such as cultural values, nutritional and public health benefits, food sovereignty, and environmental values. Nonetheless, this study provides a needed baseline assessment of existing tribal agricultural activity in Arizona.

title: The Historical Context, Scope and Regime Complex of Indigenous Peoples' Right to Health: Article 24 of the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP)

detail.title: The Historical Context, Scope and Regime Complex of Indigenous Peoples' Right to Health: Article 24 of the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

keywords: Indigenous Peoples' Human Right to Health
Article 24 United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples

detail.abstract: A combination of historical, colonial and postcolonial circumstances places Indigenous Peoples all over the world at a low rung of the socioeconomic and political ladder, where they are rendered perennially vulnerable. This unenviable status is ubiquitously evident throughout disaggregated data, which consistently depicts the lowest outcomes for Indigenous Peoples in all social determinants of health, various disease categories, and access to health care, related services, and infrastructure. This paper delves into the negotiation history of the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP) to ex-ray Article 24 of the instrument as a pivotal statement on Indigenous Peoples' right to health. Noting the recognition of traditional medicines, it integrates Article 24 of UNDRIP with other provisions of UNDRIP as well as other corpus of human rights instruments, including their associated interpretative elaborations on the rights to health as they relate to Indigenous Peoples. The contribution argues that the right to health as affirmed in Article 24 of UNDRIP is to be interpreted to guard against the continuing burden of discrimination on all the prohibited human rights grounds. That understanding is without prejudice to the idea that UNDRIP provides a basis for 'positive discrimination' in favour of Indigenous-specific health care needs. The right to health is indispensable and inherently related to all other human rights, including rights to self-determination and other rights linked to social determinants of health in which Indigenous Peoples perform abysmally. The contribution uses Article 24 of UNDRIP to provide the evolutionary and interpretative context, scope and the regime complex for understanding the content and substance of Indigenous Peoples' human right to the highest attainable standard of physical and mental health.

title: Merger Agreement Anomalies: A Case Study in Incomplete Contracts
affiliations: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - School of Law

detail.title: Merger Agreement Anomalies: A Case Study in Incomplete Contracts
detail.abstract: This article uses the ABA's Private Target Mergers and Acquisitions Deal Points Study to interrogate a puzzle that I initially took for evidence of bad lawyering: the persistent presence of undefined or unaddressed terms in sophisticated acquisition agreements. Post-closing purchase price adjustments, representation and warranty insurance exclusivity, exclusive remedy provisions, and—most strikingly—the material adverse change (MAC) clause itself are all, in a nontrivial share of deals, left silent or vague on questions that seem central to what the parties are bargaining over. Rather than treat these gaps as drafting failures, I turn to the incomplete contracting literature to ask what work silence and vagueness might be doing. I show that the literature offers not one explanation but several, and that they are not mutually exclusive: strategic vagueness (Choi and Triantis), renegotiation-lever theory (Denis and Macias, Quinn), risk-allocation architecture (Gilson and Schwartz), delegation to a trusted forum—here, Delaware's accumulated MAC jurisprudence—stickiness and agency costs in boilerplate drafting (Anderson and Manns), and "agreeing to disagree" (Ben-Shahar). Using the MAC clause as the central case study, I argue that the ABA data, properly read, actually vindicates rather than falsifies the strategic vagueness account. Ninety-eight percent of deals nominally "define" a MAC, but the core standard remains circular—defining a material adverse change by reference to materiality—while drafting effort is instead concentrated in an increasingly long and specific list of carve-outs. That two-part architecture is exactly what strategic vagueness predicts: precision where it is cheap and valuable across every deal, vagueness where specification cost is better deferred to the rare tail event that actually triggers litigation. I then examine two harder cases that resist easy assimilation to strategic vagueness: the small percentage of deals with no MAC definition at all, and the larger percentage silent on RWI exclusivity. I argue that the first is genuinely underdetermined by the frequency data alone, admitting of several competing explanations that happen to generate the same observable correlation. The second, by contrast, is better explained as a structural or signaling gap than as vagueness properly understood, since exclusivity is a binary allocation question rather than an open-textured standard. The larger methodological payoff is a caution against reading deal-points frequencies as revealed-preference evidence of efficient design without further cross-sectional data on deal size, structure, and counsel sophistication—data the published tables do not provide, and without which efficient deferral and lawyerly inattention remain observationally equivalent.

title: Show Me the Numbers: Up-Front Financial Metrics, Ambiguity, and the Evaluability of Startup Pitches
affiliations: University of Surrey, Case Western Reserve University and Case Western Reserve University

detail.title: Show Me the Numbers: Up-Front Financial Metrics, Ambiguity, and the Evaluability of Startup Pitches
detail.abstract: Entrepreneurial pitching is central to resource acquisition. Yet little is known about how pitch design shapes the cognitive demands of venture evaluation. We examine the construct of evaluability, the amount of cognitive work a message imposes on a recipient, in entrepreneurial pitching. We argue that presenting key financial metrics up front increases evaluability by supplying decision-relevant quantities directly and reducing experienced ambiguity. We test this argument using 667 evaluations of 23 real early-stage ventures by 29 novice investment evaluators. For each participant-venture evaluation, we randomized whether the deck opened with a slide presenting the venture's revenue, valuation, and capital sought. Presenting these metrics increased evaluations by 0.24 to 0.29 points on seven-point measures of business quality, willingness to take next steps, and willingness to share the venture with co-investors, and by 4.87 points on a 100point measure of assessed success odds. Investors exposed to the financial metrics reported lower ambiguity about venture favorability. In a post-treatment decomposition, reported reliance on the figures and reduced ambiguity statistically accounted for most of the treatment association. Additionally, frontal electroencephalography (EEG) showed lower alpha power during the first 30 seconds, consistent with greater cortical engagement during initial exposure to the quantitative information, while lower cortical effort during subsequent deliberation was associated with higher evaluations. These findings establish evaluability as a core feature of entrepreneurial pitch design and show that entrepreneurs can shape investment judgments through the information architecture of their pitches.

title: Millennium Thought

detail.title: Millennium Thought
detail.abstract: This book-length manuscript brings together several decades of writing, lectures and political commentary to trace the development of George A. V. Belle’s thought on Barbados, the Caribbean and the wider postcolonial world. Spanning the radical politics of the 1970s through the ideological reversals of the 1980s and 1990s and into the early twenty-first century, the manuscript examines political economy, class struggle, decolonisation, nationalism, regionalism, socialism and the changing intellectual foundations of Caribbean political analysis. It revisits formative episodes including the 1937 Barbados revolt, the Grenada Revolution, Black Power, the collapse of the Soviet Union and the rise of neoliberal globalisation, while engaging thinkers such as Marx, Hegel, C. L. R. James, Fanon, Rodney, Cabral and Diop. Across these interventions, the manuscript argues that Caribbean political thought must critically reassess inherited European epistemological frameworks and recover historically grounded intellectual resources capable of confronting continuing forms of dependency and re-colonisation. Its later chapters extend this argument through African antiquity, Kemet, Ma’at and the Osirian Cycle, linking national memory, political leadership and cultural renewal. Taken as a whole, the manuscript offers an evolving body of Caribbean political thought and a substantial resource for scholars of political theory, history and postcolonial development and philosophy.

title: Organizational Persona Formation: The Recursive Interaction between Structural Unconscious and Institutional Unconscious
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Organizational Persona Formation: The Recursive Interaction between Structural Unconscious and Institutional Unconscious
detail.abstract:
This study proposes the concept of organizational persona to explain why organizations may display persistent and recognizable behavioral patterns even as their members change over time. Organizational persona does not imply that organizations possess psychological personalities comparable to those of individuals. Rather, it refers to an emergent and relatively persistent pattern of organizational behavior produced through recursive interaction between individual action and institutional structure.

To explain this process, the study distinguishes between structural unconscious and institutional unconscious. Structural unconscious refers to learned cognitive, affective, and behavioral dispositions formed through repeated adaptation to organizational conditions such as evaluation, sanctions, exclusion, role expectations, and authority relations. These dispositions orient action without requiring continuous conscious deliberation. Institutional unconscious, by contrast, refers to an organizational-level structural tendency that emerges when locally rational actions by different actors become connected and repeatedly reproduce a common direction of organizational response beyond the intentions of any single individual.

The central argument is that these two levels form a recursive rather than unidirectional relationship. Actions shaped by structural unconscious contribute to the formation and reproduction of institutional unconscious, while the resulting institutional environment restructures evaluation, roles, procedures, voice opportunities, and sanction risks, thereby shaping subsequent individual adaptation. Organizational persona emerges when this cycle becomes sufficiently persistent to generate recognizable behavioral regularities that are relatively independent of the individuals who initially produced them.

The study further examines a longitudinal organizational case to consider how individually dependent behavior may develop into organizational-level patterns through adaptation, imitation, silence, and institutional stabilization. Organizational persona is therefore treated not as a fixed organizational essence but as a dynamic and potentially transformable structure whose persistence depends on continued reproduction. The framework offers a way to understand organizational continuity without reducing it either to individual personality or to static institutional structure.

title: Enterprise-driven Philanthropy (EDP) A Framework for Scalable, Accountable and Sustainable Social Impact
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Enterprise-driven Philanthropy (EDP) A Framework for Scalable, Accountable and Sustainable Social Impact
detail.abstract: This paper introduces Enterprise-Driven Philanthropy (EDP), a framework proposing that sustainable social impact is determined not by the volume of capital deployed, but by the way that capital is structured, governed, measured, and reinvested. Traditional philanthropy and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) investing have each made significant contributions to global development, yet persistent structural challenges, including poverty, unemployment, and weak industrial capacity, remain largely unresolved. EDP proposes an alternative: treating capital as a productive asset deployed through disciplined ownership, operational accountability, and continuous reinvestment to build self-sustaining economic ecosystems. Drawing on established literature in blended value, impact investing, private equity, and industrial policy, alongside practical illustration, this paper compares EDP with traditional philanthropy and ESG investing across accountability, capital deployment, and long-term value creation. It concludes by positioning EDP not as a replacement for existing models, but as an evolution designed for situations where the objective extends beyond immediate relief toward lasting economic transformation.

title: The 2001 Microsoft Decision and Antitrust: Six Affirmative Contributions and a Dog that Didn't Bark
affiliations: American University - Washington College of Law

detail.title: The 2001 Microsoft Decision and Antitrust: Six Affirmative Contributions and a Dog that Didn't Bark
detail.abstract: This article examines the contributions to antitrust law of the D.C. Circuit's unanimous 2001 en banc decision in Microsoft. It identifies six affirmative contributions to monopolization doctrine under Section 2 of the Sherman Act: (1) refining the "bad act" element of the offense by adopting a multi-step burden-shifting approach; (2) clarifying that the exclusion of nascent rivals satisfies the requirement that the defendant's conduct have a causal connection to the exercise or maintenance of market power: (3) cementing the role of economic analysis in antitrust law by making it clear that all plaintiffs, including the government, must lay out the mechanism by which they allege competition has been harmed; (4) reaffirming that the exercise of intellectual property rights does not insulate a firm from antitrust liability; (5) confirming that courts can rely on the basic economic proposition that competition is necessarily harmed when a firm excludes all its actual and potential rivals without need to specify the details of the "but-for" world in which the conduct did not take place; and (6) establishing that whether the monopolist's conduct constitutes "competition on the merits" is a legal conclusion reached through the burden-shifting framework rather than the product of an independent analytical step for classifying conduct undertaken prior to applying the burden-shifting approach. At least as important, the decision contributed to antitrust law through what it did not do. Antitrust law would likely have evolved differently had the circuit court split, with a counterfactual dissenting opinion supporting the defendant by asserting that in order to avoid chilling innovation, antitrust law strongly presumes that competition and consumers benefit from unilateral conduct or vertical agreements entered into by firms in rapidly changing high-tech markets. Such an opinion would likely have emboldened the Supreme Court to adopt rapidly a more minimalist, non-interventionist antitrust, as by carving out exceptions to antitrust liability for new product development or firm conduct in high-tech, innovative industries. The article explains why that counterfactual opinion was not written in 2001, and why all the decision's contributions, affirmative and negative, may be tested today.

title: “Strengthening The Strategic Autonomy and Monetary Sovereignty”: Legal Justifications for The Digital Euro in the Wake of Geopolitical Shifts

detail.title: “Strengthening The Strategic Autonomy and Monetary Sovereignty”: Legal Justifications for The Digital Euro in the Wake of Geopolitical Shifts

contentType.other: Conference Paper, forthcoming in: Kirchhoff/Böttner (eds.), The EU’s Foreign and Security Policy: External Trade and Economic Security, YELS Conference, Nomos 2026.

detail.abstract: The digital euro is intended to strengthen the EU’s strategic autonomy and monetary sovereignty. The proposed Digital Euro Regulation contains several obligations on private market actors to ensure the availability and acceptance of the digital euro. These measures restrict the freedom to conduct a business enshrined in Article 16 CFR. This article investigates whether these limitations can be legally justified. It concludes that monetary sovereignty constitutes an objective of general interest. The establishment of the digital euro can be deemed suitable and necessary to pursue this goal. Given the mitigating and compensatory measures provided for in the proposed Digital Euro Regulation, a fair balance is struck between the public interest in safeguarding monetary sovereignty and the private interest of financial market actors.

title: Dynamic Wage Setting: The Role of Monopsony Power and Employment Costs
affiliations: Queen's University, Aarhus University, The Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania  and Queen's University

detail.title: Dynamic Wage Setting: The Role of Monopsony Power and Employment Costs
detail.abstract: We develop and estimate a model of dynamic wage setting that jointly identifies latent worker ability, firm productivity, and wage markdowns, defined as the ratio of wages to the marginal revenue product of labor. Using matched employer-employee data and firm accounts, we document that markdowns widen with average worker ability and firm productivity. We decompose markdowns into a static monopsony wedge, determined by the firm-level labor supply elasticity, and a dynamic cost wedge reflecting non-wage employment costs and the continuation value of labor. Static monopsony power accounts for most of the average level of markdowns but explains very little of their cross-sectional variance. Nearly all dispersion in markdowns arises from the dynamic cost wedge. Standard wedge-accounting exercises that treat observed markdowns as measures of employer market power would misattribute most of the within-market markdown dispersion to the wrong source.

title: Integrated Development for Peace: The Turkana - Pokot Border Strategy

detail.title: Integrated Development for Peace: The Turkana - Pokot Border Strategy
detail.abstract: This paper interrogates four decades of peacebuilding and security intervention along the Turkana-Pokot border in Kenya's North Rift and advances a critical, evidence-based case for reorienting strategy around an Integrated Development for Peace (IDP) framework. The Turkana-Pokot borderland remains one of the most persistently violent pastoralist frontiers in East Africa, characterised by cyclical cattle raiding, the highest small-arms density in the country, and poverty headcount rates that reach 82.7 per cent in Turkana and 57.0 per cent in West Pokot against a national average of 39.8 per cent. Drawing on a systematic synthesis of academic literature, government policy documents, humanitarian situation reports and contemporaneous news reporting through August 2026, the paper traces the conflict's structural roots to colonial-era boundary-making and the 1965 Sessional Paper No. 10 model of marginalisation, and evaluates the record of successive interventions-disarmament operations, the National Steering Committee on Peacebuilding and Conflict Management, county peace forums, and Kenya Red Cross-facilitated dialogues. The evidence shows a recurring pattern: security-first responses achieve short-lived stabilisation (most recently around Kalemng'orok in early 2026) but do not durably resolve the resource, governance and political-economy drivers that regenerate violence. The paper argues that neither pure securitisation nor unconditional development assistance has broken this cycle, and that the emerging convergence of devolution, oil revenue and the Lamu Port-South Sudan-Ethiopia Transport (LAPSSET) corridor creates both a narrow window of opportunity and a new risk of resource-based fault lines. It proposes a five-pillar IDP framework-security and arms governance, resource and livelihood governance, institutional and political reconciliation, infrastructure and market integration, and social cohesion-sequenced through stabilisation, structural transformation and consolidation phases, anchored in a joint Turkana-West Pokot governance council and conflict-sensitive monitoring architecture. The paper closes with stakeholder-specific recommendations and an implementation and evaluation roadmap intended to inform national policy, county integrated development planning, and donor programming.

title: When Retractions become Institutional Capital: Case Volume, Organisational Self-interest, and the Authority Problem in Retraction-focused Websites
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: When Retractions become Institutional Capital: Case Volume, Organisational Self-interest, and the Authority Problem in Retraction-focused Websites
detail.abstract: When an organisation's visibility, data assets, traffic, fundraising case, staffing, and programme growth are all connected to a continuing supply of retraction cases, it is reasonable to ask whether it has acquired an institutional interest in an expanding retraction count. That question does not require an allegation that cases are fabricated or that anyone is paid for each retraction. It concerns structure: what the organisation records as success, what sustains its relevance, and whether its incentives are matched by safeguards against overstatement, duplication, role conflict, and reputational harm. Public documents show that Retraction Watch has linked the scale of its database to sustainable funding; presented database growth, traffic, and retraction-linked outcomes as accomplishments; and participated in programmes that fund investigators whose findings may then be reported on its own platform. Its Crossref agreement, however, specifies fixed service fees, allows days with no new records, and contains data-quality provisions. The evidence therefore does not establish a per-case bounty or deliberate production of false retractions. It does establish a volume-sensitive institutional model whose outputs should not be confused with independent adjudication. This commentary examines the resulting incentive problem, the methodological weakness of raw retraction totals, the tension between journalism and intervention, and the procedural deficiencies of person-level rankings. It concludes that Retraction Watch and comparable websites have not demonstrated a basis for privileged watchdog, scientific, or quasi-regulatory authority. Their claims and classifications should be treated as interested publications and data assertions requiring independent verification, due process, and accountable review.

title: Impact Assessment of the Third-Party Funding of Commercial Arbitration on Investor Decision and Conduct

detail.title: Impact Assessment of the Third-Party Funding of Commercial Arbitration on Investor Decision and Conduct

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NONE
declarations.ethicsApproval: NONE
declarations.funderStatement: NONE

detail.abstract: This research examines how third-party funding of commercial arbitration affects investors’ decisions and conduct, with particular focus on Nigeria. The study further considers how the availability of funding may influence investors’ willingness to invest and enter commercial relationships, particularly in jurisdictions where dispute resolution mechanisms are a significant investment consideration. The study also highlights possible challenges, including conflicts of interest, overreliance on funders, increased costs, and uncertainty in the arbitration process. It also examines the role of Sections 61 and 62 of the Arbitration and Mediation Act 2023 in recognizing third-party funding and requiring disclosure of funders. Finally, the research concludes that third-party funding can positively influence investment decisions and access to justice, but effective regulation is necessary to manage its risks and protect the integrity of the arbitration process.

title: Barrel Vault (aka Scordelis-Lo roof) Benchmark
affiliations: University of California, San Diego (UCSD) and University of Bologna

detail.title: Barrel Vault (aka Scordelis-Lo roof) Benchmark
detail.abstract: In engineering analysis of shells, the primary limitation on the accuracy of computational and code-based verification procedures is typically the fidelity of the stress predictions, or, equivalently, the quality of the associated section force and moment resultants. As of now, benchmark datasets for curved shell structures that enable both finite-element developers and end users to assess how reliably a given shell formulation produces accurate, high-quality force and moment resultants remain limited, with only one or two published examples currently available.The objective of this work is to present a detailed description of the complete solution to the so-called Barrel Vault benchmark (also known as the Scordelis–Lo roof). A central contribution of the present study is the provision of extensive information on stress resultants. Specifically, we supply full-field plots of section forces and section moments, charts of the resultants along the edges of the computational domain, and extrapolations to the limit of vanishing element size accompanied by confidence-interval estimates at selected points.The complete code used to compute the benchmark solutions is made available online. It is anticipated that these results will support and accelerate efforts to verify the correctness and effectiveness of current and future shell models.

title: Queueing for a lottery: limit-up gaming, retail coordination, and the registration-based listing reform in China
affiliations: Harbin Industry University

detail.title: Queueing for a lottery: limit-up gaming, retail coordination, and the registration-based listing reform in China
detail.abstract: Daily price limits are usually evaluated as a volatility-dampening device, but in a retail-dominated market they also create a queue whose observability turns them into a coordination technology. We study limit-up gaming in Chinese A-shares using 5.84 million stock-day observations and 1.42 billion order records on 4,187 listed firms between January 2019 and December 2024, and exploit the February 2023 extension of registration-based listing to the main board as a shock to the supply of speculative listings. Before the reform, queue depth at the limit-up price averaged 6.4 times average daily volume in the opening hour and predicted a five-day reversal of 4.02 percent in the deepest decile, so the queue was a negative-expected-return lottery rather than a signal of information. After the reform, gaming intensity falls by 1.31 percentage points within four quarters, queue depth roughly halves, and the reversal in the deepest decile shrinks to 2.11 percent. The decline concentrates in micro-capitalisation, loss-making, and high retail-ownership firms, exactly where the scarcity rent created by administrative listing control had been largest, and account-level concentration of limit-up buying falls by a third. Retail round-trip losses on limit-up purchases narrow by roughly one hundred basis points, variance ratios move toward unity, and price delay declines, indicating that the coordination the limit sustained was a transfer mechanism rather than a discovery mechanism.

title: Algorithmic Empire: Generative AI and the Grammar of Global Subordination
affiliations: Universidad de la Republica

detail.title: Algorithmic Empire: Generative AI and the Grammar of Global Subordination
detail.abstract:
This article introduces algorithmic empire as a testable condition of generative AI discourse in which inherited global hierarchies may be reproduced through the unequal grammatical distribution of agency, legitimacy, crisis, coercion, sovereignty, and responsibility. The concept does not designate every geopolitical bias, every Western-centered output, or every use of security, humanitarian, development, or intervention language as imperial. It identifies a narrower formal possibility: machine-generated discourse may systematically preserve dominant actors as subjects of order while converting subordinated societies into objects of management.

The framework consolidates six mechanisms developed across the preceding studies in this series: responsibility loss, asymmetric visibility, sanctioned suffering, censorship without a censor, loss of political subjecthood, and the administrative translation of force. These mechanisms concern different domains, but they share a common structural question. Who retains the capacity to act, authorize, secure, sanction, mediate, stabilize, classify, and intervene, and who appears principally as the population upon which those actions operate? Algorithmic empire names the hypothesized convergence of these distributions. It does not presuppose that such convergence exists.

This distinction is necessary because recent research establishes that framing and geopolitical variation in large language model outputs are measurable but does not establish a universal direction of bias. LLM-generated summaries can alter framing relative to source texts, while international-relations evaluations have detected nation-level and geopolitical differences whose magnitude and direction vary across models, prompts, languages, and evaluation contexts. Algorithmic empire therefore cannot be inferred from isolated outputs or from the geographic origin of a model. It requires controlled comparison.

The article uses Palestine and Iran as principal analytical anchors and extends comparison to sanctions, occupation, military intervention, migration, humanitarian governance, development discourse, platform moderation, and security language. These cases are not treated as politically equivalent. They function as sites in which different relations among sovereignty, coercion, external power, civilian harm, security, and institutional agency can be observed. Palestine provides a particularly demanding test because legal, military, humanitarian, territorial, and political categories coexist within the same discourse. Iran provides a different structure in which substantial state agency coexists with sanctions, securitization, nuclear framing, regional threat construction, and documented problems of sanctions over-compliance affecting civilian access to medical goods.

Methodologically, the paper proposes an Imperial Grammar Reproduction Rate (IGRR) and an Algorithmic Empire Index (AEI). IGRR measures directional asymmetries between matched actor classes rather than counting clauses preclassified as imperial. AEI combines separately measurable dimensions of agency asymmetry, object-framing asymmetry, coercion neutralization, sovereignty erasure, and external-responsibility deletion. Both instruments permit null and inverse findings. If comparable actors retain equivalent agency and causal visibility, if apparent asymmetries originate entirely in the source material, or if dominant actors undergo equivalent object conversion, the imperial-grammar hypothesis must be rejected or narrowed.

The paper therefore does not measure whether empire is named. It measures whether a reproducible grammar of global hierarchy survives transformation by generative systems. The ethical issue is not whether machines explicitly endorse domination. It is whether the linguistic conditions under which coercion, occupation, intervention, responsibility, sovereignty, and political agency remain attributable are distributed symmetrically across geopolitical power relations.

title: From Intellectual AI Research Structure to Global Strategy Orchestration: Mapping the Evolution and Trends of AI Research in Corporate Settings
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: From Intellectual AI Research Structure to Global Strategy Orchestration: Mapping the Evolution and Trends of AI Research in Corporate Settings
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a strategic resource shaping how firms create, coordinate, and sustain competitive advantage across global markets. However, research on AI in corporate settings remains fragmented across technical, organizational, and sector-specific domains. To address this gap, we analyze 55,169 peer-reviewed articles retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus using bibliometric techniques and Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modelling. The findings reveal twelve intellectual domains and six emerging research trends, highlighting the growing prominence of digital strategy, organizational performance, governance, and sustainability. Building on these results, we develop the Global AI Advantage Framework, which explains how firms transform AI capabilities into global competitive advantage through strategic orchestration, market deployment, and governance mechanisms.

title: From Ambiguous Behavior to Contested Ethical Meaning: Grey Leadership
affiliations: Istanbul Aydin University, Istanbul Aydin University and

detail.title: From Ambiguous Behavior to Contested Ethical Meaning: Grey Leadership
